_meta.generated_by: Enhanced E1 capability audit; normalized by the E1 consistency correction
_meta.audit_basis_date: 2026-08-28 (commit date of the tree the audit read)
_meta.normalization_scope: Structural normalization only: the E1 findings are unchanged in substance. The catalog was relayered onto four strictly separate axes, the value vocabulary was unified, internal contradictions between machine-readable fields and the same benchmark's detailed finding were removed, and every summary count was recomputed from the detail data. No new benchmark audit was performed, no policy was decided, no productive file was touched.
_meta.purpose: Authoritative machine-readable capability catalog for all 60 benchmarks: what ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE and the fill-pattern parameter can actually change, per-pattern type-safety and domain-validity, adapter feasibility, and >4096 cause classification. AUDIT METADATA ONLY after E1: nothing in the productive spec pipeline reads or enforces this catalog yet - enforcement (effective_patterns(benchmark) = globally_offered INTERSECT benchmark_supported) is a documented E2 target.
_meta.effectiveness_rule: A pattern counts as EFFECTIVE only if it can actually change the task-relevant benchmark input. Distinct pattern names/spec_keys/rationales alone are NOT test diversity; a pattern-labeled spec on a benchmark without a reachable fill hook is STRUCTURALLY_NO_PATTERN_EFFECT (structural finding; input-byte identity was not execution-proven and is not claimed).

axis_definitions.fill_type_safe: Layer 1 - is PRODUCING the pattern value and ASSIGNING it into the input container C++-safe? false only for out-of-range floating->integral conversion, narrowing UB or other assignment UB at the fill site. INT_MAX into vector<int> with DType=int is true even when it is domain-invalid or overflows the oracle later.
axis_definitions.domain_valid: Layer 2 - is the produced input inside the benchmark's frozen/derivable INPUT DOMAIN? Independent of element-type representability.
axis_definitions.oracle_execution_safe: Layer 3 - can the frozen oracle run on this input without C/C++ UB (signed overflow, heap OOB, out-of-range conversion, invalid memory access)? IEEE Inf/NaN from floating-point arithmetic is NOT UB and stays true here.
axis_definitions.verdict_outcome_class: Layer 4 - what happens to the COUNTED evaluation result: INFORMATIVE (regular, full-strength verdict) / REDUCED (a verdict is produced but demonstrably tests less than the task requires) / VACUOUS_PASS (a PASS is counted although the relevant correctness check does not happen - only assignable with a cited code path) / NO_VERDICT_BI (falls into the baseline-incompatible/gate path, no regular model verdict) / FALSE_FAIL_RISK (a semantically acceptable candidate can be graded FAIL) / UNKNOWN (not decidable statically; verdict_outcome_conditions then lists the known branches).
axis_definitions.baseline_gate_only_risk: Narrow meaning ONLY: risk that the case produces no regular candidate verdict and falls into the BI/gate path. It never encodes VACUOUS_PASS, REDUCED, FALSE_FAIL_RISK, oracle UB or fill UB - those have their own fields.
axis_definitions.value_vocabulary: Every axis field uses exactly: true | false | "conditional" | "UNKNOWN" | "NOT_APPLICABLE". The legacy string "none" is no longer used.
axis_definitions.measurement_validity_ranking: Ranking by MEASUREMENT-DISTORTION relevance, not by technical severity: 1 FALSE_FAIL_RISK (correct implementations can be counted wrong, possibly harder for omp/mpi - see parallel_bias_risk), 2 VACUOUS_PASS (wrong implementations can be counted correct), 3 oracle_execution_safe=false (the harness itself is undefined), 4 NO_VERDICT_BI (test budget spent without measuring the model; does not distort the rate as long as BI is excluded from the denominator), 5 REDUCED (a verdict exists but is weaker than intended). All oracle_execution_safe=false cases remain hard pre-pilot_002 blockers regardless of this ranking.

verified_verdict_path.comparator: drivers/cpp/utilities.hpp: a non-finite REFERENCE element is skipped and mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() emits the process-wide authenticated marker (reportAndCompareSelectedWith:423-428; scalar variant :520-523), so validate() can still return true and the driver prints 'Validation: PASS'.

verified_verdict_path.consequence: Any pattern that makes the oracle non-finite at a graded index is NO_VERDICT_BI, not VACUOUS_PASS. The earlier E1 report wording that called such fft/dense_la/transform cases a 'vacuous pass' was wrong for the enhanced stage and has been corrected throughout.
verified_verdict_path.size_zero_route: The one code-cited COUNTED pass without a correctness check found in this normalization is size-driven, not pattern-driven: static_base_sizes includes 0 (config.yaml, specs.py:134); at TEST_SIZE=0 the graded containers are empty, reportAndCompareSelectedWith accepts 0==0, the loop body never runs and it returns true, no BI marker is emitted, so run_binary counts the driver's PASS. It is recorded as a VACUOUS_PASS branch in verdict_outcome_conditions where a family verified it explicitly (dense_la, fft) and as a size-policy e2_action elsewhere; completing this branch for all 60 benchmarks is an explicit E2 item (see open_e2_policy_decisions.SIZE_ZERO_SPEC_POLICY).

fill_type_conditional_fill_sites.rationale: Pattern-dependent AT THE SITE (this is a genuine fill-axis hazard, not a relayered downstream one). DType is deduced from the 0.0 / 100.0 DOUBLE literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) while the container is std::vector<int> (cpu.cc:54), so every pattern value is produced as a double and converted by the assignment x[i] = val. For values inside [0,100] - random, all_same, both ramps, alternating, duplicate_at, sorted_except_one - the conversion is defined truncation and the site is SAFE (fill_type_safe true per pattern). For extreme_values (+/-DBL_MAX), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2) and any out-of-int-range explicit_values entry it is an out-of-range floating-to-integral conversion = UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR (observed saturation to INT_MIN/INT_MAX under g++ 13.3 -O3, not guaranteed by the standard). The Wave-2B scan at cpu.cc:76-89 runs AFTER the conversion, so it is a domain gate, not a UB fix. Fix: int literals ENHANCED_FILL(x, 0, 100) -> DType = int; extremes then become INT_MIN/INT_MAX type-safely and define-mode value_range overrides saturate at the (decltype(lo)) cast (enhanced-fill.hpp:451-454) instead of invoking UB.

THE FAMILY'S ONE GENUINELY TYPE-UNSAFE SITE, but the unsafety is pattern-dependent, which is why the axis value is 'conditional' rather than a blanket false (the E1 entry's own conversion_notes already said 'In-range patterns ... are fine', contradicting its blanket false). DType is deduced from the lo/hi ARGUMENTS (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), and the double literals -100.0/100.0 make DType=double for a vector<float>. UNSAFE patterns - the produced double is outside float's representable range, so the assignment x[i] = <double> is an out-of-range floating conversion and formally UB ([conv.double]; in practice IEEE +-inf): extreme_values(6) (+-DBL_MAX), spike_at(9) (DBL_MAX/2), and explicit_values(10) whenever a spec value exceeds +-FLT_MAX (~3.4e38). SAFE patterns - the produced value is inside float range, so the double->float conversion is well-defined (correctly rounded): random(0), all_zeros(1), all_same(2), ascending(3), descending(4), alternating(5), duplicate_at(7), sorted_except_one(8), and in-range explicit_values. A value_range override does not help: enhancedRuntimeFill casts the override to DType=double (enhanced-fill.hpp:419-425), so the mismatch persists for every override, and an override beyond +-FLT_MAX reintroduces the UB for the ramp/alternating patterns too. FIX: write -100.0f/100.0f (or an explicit float cast) so DType=float; the extrema then become +-FLT_MAX and the spike FLT_MAX/2, all representable. This axis records ONLY the assignment/conversion - the downstream all-BI behaviour of extreme_values is on the verdict axis.

Pattern-dependent at this one site, which is why the site value is conditional rather than a flat false: DType is deduced as double from the -100.0/100.0 literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:451-458, decltype(lo)) while the container is vector<float>. For the eight in-range patterns (random, all_zeros, all_same, ascending, descending, alternating, duplicate_at, sorted_except_one) every produced value lies in [-100,100] and the double->float conversion is well defined (a rounding, nothing more). For extreme_values (+-DBL_MAX) and spike_at (DBL_MAX/2), and for any explicit_values entry beyond +-FLT_MAX, the value is outside the float range and the conversion is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (practically saturating to +-inf on IEEE targets). This judgement is about the ASSIGNMENT at cpu.cc:127 only; the downstream consequences are recorded on the pattern-level axes.

Pattern-dependent at this site. DType is deduced as double from the -1.0/1.0 literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:451-458) while the container is vector<float>. The eight in-range patterns produce values inside [-1,1], so the double->float assignment is a defined rounding. extreme_values (+-DBL_MAX) and spike_at (DBL_MAX/2) are outside the float range, so the assignment is an out-of-range double->float conversion = UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (practically +-inf). This rationale covers the ASSIGNMENT only; the downstream consequence (a non-finite reference value in the multiset comparison, which emits BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE) is a verdict/gate-layer hazard and is recorded in oracle_hazards and in the pattern-level baseline_gate_only_risk. Fix: -1.0f/1.0f literals.

DType is deduced from the lo/hi ARGUMENTS 1 and 100 (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), i.e. DType=int, so patterns 0-9 assign int to int with no conversion whatsoever: INT_MIN/INT_MAX (extreme_values, enhanced-fill.hpp:134-135) and INT_MAX/2 (spike_at, enhanced-fill.hpp:153-156) are all int-representable and the site is unconditionally safe for them. The site is 'conditional' only because of pattern 10: explicit_values converts arbitrary spec doubles with static_cast<int> inside enhancedFromDouble (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171), which is UB for a value outside the int range, and specs.py:328-367 validates the count and numeric type of the values but never their magnitude. Nothing downstream of the assignment - the odd/even semantics or the negative-domain question - is charged to this axis.

DType is deduced from the int lo/hi arguments (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), so patterns 0-9 assign int to int: INT_MIN, INT_MAX and INT_MAX/2 are all int-representable and the ASSIGNMENT is unconditionally safe - the signed-overflow problem those values cause is created later, by the oracle's x[i]*x[i], and is recorded on oracle_execution_safe and in oracle_hazards, never here. The site is 'conditional' solely because pattern 10 converts arbitrary spec doubles with static_cast<int> (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171), which is UB outside the int range and is magnitude-unvalidated (specs.py:328-367).

DType is deduced from the int lo/hi arguments (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), so patterns 0-9 assign int to int with no conversion at all - INT_MIN/INT_MAX (extreme_values) and INT_MAX/2 (spike_at) are int-representable and the site is unconditionally safe for them, and because the predicate is total there is no downstream hazard to relayer either. The site is 'conditional' only for pattern 10: explicit_values converts arbitrary spec doubles with static_cast<int> (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171), UB outside the int range, magnitude-unvalidated (specs.py:328-367).

oracle_hazards.pattern: all_zeros, all_same, alternating, extreme_values (deterministic); ascending, descending, sorted_except_one (expected); explicit_values (spec-dependent)
oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unpivoted Doolittle LU divides by the current diagonal with no pivoting and no zero-pivot guard, so an exactly-zero or rounding-residue pivot yields 0/0 = NaN or x/0 = Inf and the non-finite value propagates through the whole factorization. This is IEEE-defined floating-point behaviour, NOT undefined behaviour - oracle_execution_safe stays true and the consequence is a NO_VERDICT_BI on the verdict axis.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED / DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - either restrict the offered pattern set to inputs inside the unpivoted-LU domain, or add an explicit zero/near-zero pivot tripwire so a domain violation is reported as such instead of surfacing as the generic non_finite_reference gate.

oracle_hazards.pattern: spike_at with k not on the leading pivot; explicit_values with DBL_MAX-scale values
oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unbounded element growth in unpivoted elimination combined with an ABSOLUTE grading tolerance of 1e-3: entries of magnitude ~1e307 are compared with |a-b| > 1e-3 where a single ulp is ~1e291, so a correct candidate with a different operation order is graded as a MODEL failure. Well-defined arithmetic, purely a grading-scale hazard.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - pin k for spike_at or bound spec magnitudes; a relative-tolerance decision is out of scope for this wave (VALUE_RANGE_DOMAIN_POLICY stays OPEN).

oracle_hazards.pattern: ALL labels (SIZE-axis hazard, not a pattern hazard): spec size 0
oracle_hazards.root_cause: correctSolveLinearSystem's forward-elimination bound `i < N - 1` underflows for size_t N=0 (the loop then runs with bound SIZE_MAX) and the body immediately reads A_copy[i*N + i] = A_copy[0] on an EMPTY vector: an out-of-bounds read, i.e. genuine C++ UB, before any comparison happens. The back-substitution header `for (int i = N - 1; i >= 0; i--)` additionally narrows a size_t to int.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - guard N == 0 in the oracle (and confirm N == 1 is intended to skip elimination), or exclude size 0 from this benchmark's spec set; static_base_sizes currently includes 0 (thesis/config/config.yaml:562, thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:134).

oracle_hazards.pattern: ALL labels (input-dependent; currently unreachable by any pattern because no fill site exists)
oracle_hazards.root_cause: An exactly-zero pivot makes the oracle return EARLY and SILENTLY, leaving x at the zeros the driver wrote (cpu.cc:82) - a FINITE WRONG reference. utilities.hpp emits the non_finite_reference BI marker only for non-finite references, so nothing intercepts this: a correct candidate is graded as a MODEL failure. Well-defined execution, so oracle_execution_safe is not the axis at issue - the hazard lands on the verdict axis as FALSE_FAIL_RISK.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - a zero-pivot tripwire is a PRECONDITION for any adapter that routes patterns into A, because most global patterns make A exactly singular and would hit this silent finite-wrong path instead of the BI gate.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Products of +-DBL_MAX overflow to +-Inf and the K-term accumulation mixes signs, so every reference entry is NaN. IEEE-defined overflow, NOT undefined behaviour: oracle_execution_safe stays true and the consequence is NO_VERDICT_BI.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - Option B, the extrema of the call-site range -1/+1, is benign and discriminating here, so this benchmark is a good argument for domain-extrema semantics.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Both fill sites share pattern and k (cpu.cc:70-71), so A and B carry the spike at the SAME flat index and the oracle accumulates (DBL_MAX/2)^2 = +Inf. The surrounding finite entries reach ~9e307, where one ulp (~1e292) dwarfs the ABSOLUTE 1e-4 tolerance - a latent false-failure hazard currently masked by the BI gate. IEEE-defined, not UB.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - and record that removing the Inf without addressing the absolute tolerance would convert this from a no-verdict into a parallel-biased false failure.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: z[i] = alpha*x[i] + y[i] with alpha=2 and x[i]=y[i]=+-DBL_MAX overflows to +-Inf at every index (2*DBL_MAX is already Inf). IEEE-defined overflow, NOT undefined behaviour: oracle_execution_safe stays true and the consequence is NO_VERDICT_BI.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - Option B (extrema of the call-site range) is benign here, which makes 03 the clearest argument for domain-extrema semantics.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Both fill sites share pattern and k (cpu.cc:65-66), so the two DBL_MAX/2 spikes stack at the same index and 2*(DBL_MAX/2) + DBL_MAX/2 overflows to +Inf. A single non-finite reference index is enough to mark the whole process baseline-incompatible. IEEE-defined, not UB.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED / DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decouple k across sites or bound the spike magnitude; note that an existing spec already uses spike_at for this benchmark, so it currently yields a gate record rather than a model verdict.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Products of +-DBL_MAX overflow, so every row sum is +Inf (even TEST_SIZE, where the A and x sign patterns coincide) or NaN (odd TEST_SIZE, where they mix). IEEE-defined overflow, NOT undefined behaviour: oracle_execution_safe stays true and the consequence is NO_VERDICT_BI.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - Option B, the extrema of the call-site range -10/+10, is benign and discriminating here.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Both fill sites share pattern and k (cpu.cc:69-70), so the spike lands on A[0][0] and x[0] simultaneously: y[0] gets (DBL_MAX/2)^2 = +Inf, and because x[0] multiplies every row, |A[i][0]| > ~2 (about 80% of rows at range [-10,10]) also overflows. The surviving finite rows sit at ~1e307-1e308 under an ABSOLUTE 1e-4 tolerance, a latent false-failure hazard masked by the BI gate. IEEE-defined, not UB.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decouple k across the two sites or bound the spike; note that removing the Inf without addressing the absolute tolerance would convert a no-verdict into a parallel-biased false failure.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: The iterative Rosetta fft() oracle computes the butterfly partner as b = a + k without bounding b by N. For any N >= 3 that is not a power of two the final stages reach b == N or beyond and both READ x[b] and WRITE x[b] past the end of a size-N vector (verified index math: N=7 -> stage n=3,k=1 reaches a=6, b=7; N=5 -> b=5; N=1000 -> stage n=15,k=7 reaches b=1003). thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:134 sets static_base_sizes=[0,1,2,7], so size 7 is offered today and the hazard is reachable; any LLM-chosen non-power-of-two size <= max_spec_size (4096) is equally unsafe. This is an ORACLE hazard, not a fill-site hazard: both fill sites remain double->double and fill_type_safe.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - guard correctIfft/fft against non-power-of-two N (or add a driver-level BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE tripwire), and DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED to restrict this benchmark's spec sizes to {0,1,2} union powers of two.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow in the oracle, NOT undefined behaviour: same-parity +-DBL_MAX components are added in the first butterfly (baseline.hpp:29) giving +-inf, and later stages evaluate inf-inf giving NaN. oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow to +inf (NOT undefined behaviour): p2.x-p1.x = 2*DBL_MAX overflows, pow(inf,2)=inf, sqrt(inf)=inf, so the scalar reference perimeter is non-finite for every size >= 2. The consequence is a missing verdict (baseline_incompatible), not a memory or UB fault.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Sentinel leak, not UB: at sizes 3 and 4 every triple mixes +-DBL_MAX, so every triArea is NaN (inf-inf), 'area < minArea' never fires, and the oracle returns its own initializer numeric_limits<double>::max() as the ANSWER. oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - E2 must decide how the oracle should report 'no comparable triple' (today it reports DBL_MAX as a real area); until then EXCLUDE the (extreme_values x size 3|4) cells. oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decide keep-as-BI-probe vs exclude; the outcome is unchanged by the fill-site type fix, so this must NOT be filed as FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Not UB and not an overflow of the serial oracle: the left-to-right inclusive_scan over alternating -DBL_MAX/+DBL_MAX stays finite by exact cancellation. The hazard is that the SAME input makes any reassociating implementation (parallel scan, or the fast-math oracle copy used by the stability probe) sum two -DBL_MAX terms and reach -inf, which the comparator turns into a graded FAIL against a finite reference - or, in the gate, into a suppressed verdict.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decide whether extreme_values should grade here at all, be range-clamped to Option-B lo/hi extrema, or be excluded for reassociating execution models; do NOT file this as a fill-site fix, the fill is type-correct.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unvalidated spec magnitudes: a value list large enough to overflow a partial prefix sum makes the reference non-finite (IEEE overflow, not UB), which routes the spec to baseline_incompatible and grades nothing.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - add spec-side validation of explicit value magnitudes against the frozen domain and against the absolute 1e-6 epsilon.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: LAYER NOTE: the UB is at the FILL SITE, not in the oracle. enhancedFillPattern deduces DType=double from the double literals at cpu.cc:59 while the container is vector<float>, so extreme_values assigns +-DBL_MAX to a float ([conv.double] out-of-range floating conversion = UB; observed as +-inf). The oracle (std::min inclusive_scan) is total and executes safely on whatever value lands in the vector; its downstream effect is that -inf makes every prefix non-finite, which suppresses the verdict entirely.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES: change ENHANCED_FILL(input, -100.0, 100.0) to -100.0f/100.0f so DType=float; then DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED for whether +-FLT_MAX extrema are worth offering (the resulting reference is a constant vector = REDUCED).

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Same fill-site cause: DBL_MAX/2 assigned to a float slot is an out-of-range conversion (UB, observed +inf). The oracle is unaffected - min(prev, +inf) = prev - so the only consequences are the formal UB and the silent loss of the intended spike semantics.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES (same one-line change); afterwards spike_at remains semantically inert for a running minimum, so treat it as a low-value pattern for this benchmark.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unvalidated spec magnitudes reaching the same double->float slot: any spec value beyond +-FLT_MAX is an out-of-range conversion at the fill site.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES plus spec-side validation of explicit value magnitudes against the target element type.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow, not UB: with alternating +-DBL_MAX the oracle's prefix array is {-DBL_MAX, 0, -DBL_MAX, 0, ...} and std::accumulate adds two -DBL_MAX terms at the third element, producing -inf for every n >= 3. The scalar reference is therefore non-evaluable and the trial produces no candidate verdict.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED / ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - either stop offering extreme_values here, clamp it to Option-B lo/hi extrema, or accept it as an intentional baseline-gate probe; do NOT file it as a fill-site fix (the fill is double-to-double and correct).

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow, not UB: a single DBL_MAX/2 element makes all (n-k) prefixes from k onward ~DBL_MAX/2, and accumulating three or more of them exceeds DBL_MAX -> +inf. Only k in {n-2, n-1} keeps the reference finite, and k=n-2 lands exactly on DBL_MAX.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - restrict or drop spike_at for this benchmark; a domain-respecting spike magnitude would have to be derived from lo/hi and n, which the harness does not currently define.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unvalidated spec magnitudes meeting a ~n^2/2 amplification factor: values that are individually modest can still drive the weighted sum out of double range (non-finite reference -> no verdict) or past the absolute 1e-5 epsilon (false failures).
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - add spec-side validation binding explicit value magnitude and value_range to n via the ~range*n^2 result bound.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: PREVENTED, not present: INT_MIN/INT_MAX input would make the oracle's int inclusive_scan overflow (signed overflow = UB), as the cpu.cc:65-71 comment records having measured at odd n. The Wave-2B guard at cpu.cc:73-85 checks every element against |x| <= 100 and `continue`s before correctReversePrefixSum runs, so under the CURRENT source the UB is unreachable and the only observable effect is an all-BI trial.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - the guard already does its job; decide only whether extreme_values should be OFFERED for this benchmark (it can never produce a verdict) or replaced by Option-B lo/hi extrema. Do not weaken or remove the guard.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Same as extreme_values: INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 would let the suffix scan exceed 2^31, but the guard rejects the input first for every k, so the oracle never executes on it.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decide whether to keep offering a pattern that is structurally BI-only here.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: The guard runs AFTER the fill, so it cannot protect against the conversion itself: enhancedFromDouble<int> performs a raw static_cast<int>(double), which is UB for any spec value outside int range. Spec values inside int range but outside [-100,100] are caught by the guard and merely produce an all-BI trial.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED plus spec-side validation: reject explicit_values lists (and value_range overrides) whose values leave int range or the frozen [-100,100] domain, instead of letting them reach the fill.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Spec-authoring hazard rather than a code defect: a value_range override beyond +-100 is silently cast to int and then rejected by the guard on EVERY trial, so validate() returns true at cpu.cc:104 having graded nothing. The finding is that the failure mode is silent (no compile or runtime error), not that any UB occurs. Applies equally to all_same, ascending, descending, alternating, duplicate_at and sorted_except_one.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - add spec-side validation so a value_range override beyond the frozen +-100 is rejected at authoring time rather than turning into an all-BI, zero-grading run.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: LIVE, UNGUARDED UB in the oracle: with x = INT_MIN, INT_MAX, INT_MIN, ... the inner accumulation currSum += x[j] goes 0 -> INT_MIN -> -1 -> (-1 + INT_MIN), which overflows int for every n >= 3 (the default 1024 and the static size 7 included). Signed overflow is UB, and nothing intercepts it: this benchmark has no Wave-2B guard, and because ints are always 'finite' the harness non-finite-reference contract (utilities.hpp:517-522) cannot fire either. The gate probes also pass, since the fast-math stability probe does not perturb integer arithmetic - so the model runs and a verdict is counted against a UB-derived reference.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED: port scan/33's Wave-2B frozen-domain tripwire (|x| <= 100 -> mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() + continue, cpu.cc:72-85 there) into this driver, or stop offering extreme_values here. This must NOT be filed as FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES - the int-to-int fill is correct; the defect is that the oracle is unprotected.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Latent, not currently reached: the single INT_MAX/2 spike keeps every window sum under 2^30-1 + 100n, which is below INT_MAX for n < ~1.07e7, so at every frozen size the oracle is well-defined. It becomes the same unguarded overflow as extreme_values if n grows past that bound or a value_range override introduces a second extreme value.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED (the same tripwire would also bound this case) plus spec-side validation of |range| * n < 2^31; until then keep spike_at only at the frozen sizes.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: The as-authored [-100,100] range keeps every window sum under 100*n and therefore inside int, but that bound is UNSTATED and UNCHECKED in this driver. A value_range override with |range| * n >= 2^31 makes the ramp/alternating/random patterns overflow the oracle's accumulator with no interception. Applies equally to all_same, ascending, descending, duplicate_at and sorted_except_one.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED plus spec-side validation keeping |range| * n < 2^31 (the D0-style bound scan/33 documents at its cpu.cc:65-71).

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unvalidated spec values reach a raw static_cast<int>(double); values outside int range are an out-of-range floating-to-integral conversion (UB at the fill), and values inside int range but large relative to n overflow the oracle's accumulator afterwards.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED plus spec-side validation of explicit value magnitudes against int range and against the |value| * n < 2^31 window bound.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: |lo| == |hi| at the frozen range, so the alternating pattern produces two complex values of EQUAL magnitude; the order invariant is again satisfied by any permutation and only the multiset check discriminates. No UB, no gate event.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: A static spec size of 0 is outside the frozen mathematical domain (1 <= k <= n needs n >= 1): the driver calls mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() and returns true ungraded, so every size-0 spec is a BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE-only run regardless of pattern. This is SIZE-triggered, never pattern-triggered, and is recorded here so it is not mistaken for a pattern hazard.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - confirm the spec policy treats a size-0 spec as expected-and-excluded, not as a failure signal.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Only in the NaN sub-case: a NaN element makes the comparator x[i1] < x[i2] non-strict-weak, so std::sort inside correctRanks has undefined behaviour (libstdc++ introsort can run off the range) and, if it returns, the reference ranking can violate the permutation invariant. No offered numeric pattern produces a NaN on IEEE targets - only a spec value list could.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED (narrow) plus a spec-layer finiteness check on explicit value lists; the selftest at cpu.cc:133-144 already announces the survivable variant as BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE.

oracle_hazards.pattern: extreme_values, spike_at, explicit_values (out-of-range entries), and any value_range beyond +-FLT_MAX
oracle_hazards.root_cause: Silent-failure hazard rather than an oracle hazard: this driver has NO non-finite input guard and validRanks performs no finiteness check and calls no reportAndCompare* helper, so an out-of-range fill conversion produces neither a BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker nor a validation failure. The run completes and is counted, which is what makes the fill-site defect easy to miss. Recorded here for the gate layer; the defect itself belongs to the fill site (cpu.cc:127) and is filed as FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES first; optionally ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - add a finiteness guard so the condition is at least announced if the site is not fixed.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Verdict/gate-layer consequence of the non-finite float value, NOT an oracle UB: the reference-side reportAndCompareEq(aVal, bVal) inside sameRecordMultiset sees a non-finite REFERENCE element, skips the index and emits the authenticated BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference marker. Every run of this pattern - the oracle-only gate probe included - is therefore classified baseline_incompatible and the model never produces a graded verdict. The frozen oracle itself (std::sort on an int key) is unaffected.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - decide whether to guard/announce the non-finite value field explicitly or to exclude patterns 6 and 9 for this benchmark. Fixing the fill site (-1.0f/1.0f) removes the cause, but the gate behaviour is its own decision and must not be filed as a fill-site type item.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Identical mechanism to extreme_values but triggered by the single non-finite value at index k: one non-finite reference element is enough, because the marker is process-wide and emitted once.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - same decision as extreme_values.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Domain-layer only: all_zeros writes duration = 0, below the frozen duration >= 1 range. Nothing downstream depends on duration (it is payload, never used by the key comparator), so grading is unaffected; recorded so the domain_valid=false judgement is traceable and is not mistaken for a safety problem.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decide whether a payload-only domain violation matters for spec acceptance, and whether a single global value_range that overrides all three sites (voiding duration >= 1 in the same way) is acceptable spec semantics.

benchmarks.size_rationale: All three validate() buffers A/A_correct/A_test are TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:53-55) and both oracle and candidate are called with TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:68,72). benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The one and only validate() input (A) is fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:63); every offered pattern changes the entire graded computation. Caveat: pattern choice being EFFECTIVE mechanically does not mean every pattern is mathematically meaningful for unpivoted LU (see domain_restrictions).
benchmarks.input_construction: Single input matrix A (TEST_SIZE^2 doubles) filled via ENHANCED_FILL(A, -10.0, 10.0) at cpu.cc:63, then copied to A_correct/A_test (cpu.cc:67,71). Oracle correctLuFactorize is unpivoted in-place Doolittle LU (baseline.hpp:13-23). fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the LO/HI arguments (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174): the two double literals at cpu.cc:63 give DType=double, identical to the container value_type. Every pattern value the harness can produce for DType=double (0, midpoint, ramp, lo/hi, numeric_limits<double>::lowest()/max(), max()/2, enhancedFromDouble<double>(spec)) is by construction representable in a double, so the assignment x[i]=value is a plain double-to-double copy: no narrowing, no float-to-integral conversion, no UB. The ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI override casts to decltype(lo)=double (enhanced-fill.hpp:174-177), also lossless. NOTE (layer correction): the downstream consequences of large values - singular matrices, NaN pivots, absolute-tolerance blowup - are oracle/domain/verdict matters and are recorded on those axes, not here.

domain.summary: Implicit and structural: A must be factorizable WITHOUT pivoting - every pivot arising during elimination must be nonzero and well-scaled. Oracle has no pivoting and no zero-pivot guard (baseline.hpp:16: factor = A[i*N+k]/A[k*N+k]; 0/0 -> NaN, x/0 -> Inf). The frozen random range [-10,10] satisfies this w.h.p.; structured patterns generally do NOT: all_zeros, all_same (midpoint of -10/10 is exactly 0 -> identical to all_zeros here), alternating (identical rows for even N -> exactly singular, NaN at second pivot), extreme_values (identical +-DBL_MAX rows -> zero rows after step 0, 0/0=NaN at k=1), ascending/descending/sorted_except_one (rank-2-in-exact-arithmetic ramps -> near-zero pivots, huge growth, likely Inf/NaN or absolute-tolerance blowup). duplicate_at and random are benign w.h.p.

tripwires: none - no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard exists in this cpu.cc (repo grep: only reduce/26, utilities.hpp, harness-markers.hpp contain the token). The harness-level non_finite_reference marker (utilities.hpp:363-378, emitted from reportAndCompareSelectedWith at utilities.hpp:425-428) fires whenever the ORACLE result is non-finite at a graded index; the index is then skipped. Patterns that fire it here: all_zeros, all_same, alternating, extreme_values (deterministically); ascending/descending/sorted_except_one (near-singular, likely). These are baseline-gate-only signals, not model failures.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen/derivable domain: A must be factorizable by UNPIVOTED Doolittle LU - every pivot arising during elimination must be nonzero and well-scaled (baseline.hpp:13-23 has no pivoting and no guard) - with element magnitudes small enough that unpivoted growth stays inside the ABSOLUTE 1e-3 grading tolerance; the frozen value range is the call-site [-10.0, 10.0] at cpu.cc:63.

oracle_hazards.pattern: all_zeros, all_same, alternating, extreme_values (deterministic); ascending, descending, sorted_except_one (expected); explicit_values (spec-dependent)
oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unpivoted Doolittle LU divides by the current diagonal with no pivoting and no zero-pivot guard, so an exactly-zero or rounding-residue pivot yields 0/0 = NaN or x/0 = Inf and the non-finite value propagates through the whole factorization. This is IEEE-defined floating-point behaviour, NOT undefined behaviour - oracle_execution_safe stays true and the consequence is a NO_VERDICT_BI on the verdict axis.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED / DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - either restrict the offered pattern set to inputs inside the unpivoted-LU domain, or add an explicit zero/near-zero pivot tripwire so a domain violation is reported as such instead of surfacing as the generic non_finite_reference gate.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Unbounded element growth in unpivoted elimination combined with an ABSOLUTE grading tolerance of 1e-3: entries of magnitude ~1e307 are compared with |a-b| > 1e-3 where a single ulp is ~1e291, so a correct candidate with a different operation order is graded as a MODEL failure. domain.summary: A must be nonsingular AND stably eliminable without pivoting (oracle is unpivoted). Consistency invariant: b is constructed as A*x_true, so the system is always solvable when A is nonsingular. Frozen range [-10,10] random keeps all of this w.h.p.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: correctSolveLinearSystem's forward-elimination bound `i < N - 1` underflows for size_t N=0 (the loop then runs with bound SIZE_MAX) and the body immediately reads A_copy[i*N + i] = A_copy[0] on an EMPTY vector: an out-of-bounds read, i.e. genuine C++ UB, before any comparison happens. The back-substitution header `for (int i = N - 1; i >= 0; i--)` additionally narrows a size_t to int.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - guard N == 0 in the oracle (and confirm N == 1 is intended to skip elimination), or exclude size 0 from this benchmark's spec set; static_base_sizes currently includes 0 (thesis/config/config.yaml:562, thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:134).

oracle_hazards.pattern: ALL labels (input-dependent; currently unreachable by any pattern because no fill site exists)
oracle_hazards.root_cause: An exactly-zero pivot makes the oracle return EARLY and SILENTLY, leaving x at the zeros the driver wrote (cpu.cc:82) - a FINITE WRONG reference. utilities.hpp emits the non_finite_reference BI marker only for non-finite references, so nothing intercepts this: a correct candidate is graded as a MODEL failure. Well-defined execution, so oracle_execution_safe is not the axis at issue - the hazard lands on the verdict axis as FALSE_FAIL_RISK.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - a zero-pivot tripwire is a PRECONDITION for any adapter that routes patterns into A, because most global patterns make A exactly singular and would hit this silent finite-wrong path instead of the BI gate.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: A methodically clean benchmark-native adapter exists: apply the pattern to the GROUND-TRUTH solution vector x (cpu.cc:29) and keep A random and b derived - every global numeric pattern is a valid solution vector, the invariant b=A*x is preserved by construction, and validity/nonsingularity depends only on the still-random A. all_zeros/x-patterns are meaningful (does the solver recover a structured solution). Patterning A instead REQUIRES a domain policy: most global patterns make A exactly singular (zeros/same/alternating/extremes) or near-singular (ramps), which does NOT fire the BI gate here but instead trips the silent zero-pivot early return (baseline.hpp:22-24) -> false model failures; that path must not ship without a zero-pivot tripwire in the driver or oracle. Extreme/spike magnitudes on either A or x overflow b=A*x. No new pattern semantics need inventing - the ambiguity is only WHICH container carries the pattern.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: size_t sizes, heap vectors, no fixed buffers or narrowing. Costs: A is N^2 doubles and the oracle internally copies A (baseline.hpp:13) -> ~2 N^2 transient; O(N^3) elimination in oracle AND (typically) candidate, x2 trials, plus O(N^2) b-construction. At N=8192: ~1.1 GB peak, minutes-scale runtime. Only the global 4096 policy formally blocks.
e2_actions: BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - no ENHANCED_FILL site (pattern axis dead; fill_sites=0 VERIFIED against cpu.cc). Recommended adapter: ENHANCED_FILL the GROUND-TRUTH solution vector x (cpu.cc:29) and keep A random with b = A*x derived - every global numeric pattern is a valid solution vector, the invariant is preserved by construction, and validity/nonsingularity depends only on the still-random A

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decide the pattern target: x is clean, whereas patterning A requires a nonsingularity policy because most global patterns make A exactly singular (zeros/same/alternating/extremes) or near-singular (ramps)

ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - baseline.hpp:22-24 returns SILENTLY and FINITELY on a zero pivot, bypassing the BI gate and turning a correct candidate into a MODEL failure; this guard must land before any adapter routes patterns into A. (Layer note: this is an ORACLE hazard, not a fill-site type problem - the driver has no fill site at all, so FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES would be the wrong filing.)

benchmarks.notes: shapes JSON entry (fill_sites=0, explicit_values disabled, 'nothing to fill') VERIFIED. Absolute tolerance 1e-4 on a solve whose x components are O(10) is tight but adequate at the default range; ill-conditioned random draws are the known flakiness source and MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2 doubles the exposure. Relayering summary: because pattern_effect is NONE, all four safety axes are NOT_APPLICABLE for every label and the verdict class is the class of the run that actually happens - the benchmark's own random case - for all eleven labels; only the 'random' label is a legitimate spec, the other ten are duplicates. The two real hazards (size-0 out-of-bounds read; silent zero-pivot early return producing a finite wrong reference) are ORACLE-layer findings and are filed as such, not as fill-site or pattern findings. Unlike 00/02/03/04, size 0 here is NOT a vacuous pass but an out-of-bounds read that precedes the comparison.

Additional deterministic NONSQUARE shape probe (cpu.cc:102-127): A_ns/B_ns filled with fillRand(-1,1) (cpu.cc:110-111) by documented design (comment cpu.cc:95-101: 'deterministic unseeded rand() stream', outside the S/M/L and pattern axes).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType deduced from the double literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) equals the container value_type, so every harness-produced value - including numeric_limits<double>::lowest()/max() for extreme_values and max()/2 for spike_at - is representable and the assignment is a plain double-to-double copy. No narrowing, no float-to-integral conversion, no UB. Downstream overflow of the K-term accumulation is an oracle/verdict matter recorded on those axes.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: double->double, lossless; extreme_values +-DBL_MAX representable, no UB.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: Identical to the A site: DType=double from the double literals, assignment is lossless double-to-double for every pattern value. The fact that both sites share pattern, range and k (so A and B receive identical content and spikes land at flat index 0 in BOTH) affects the domain and verdict axes, not the type-safety of either assignment.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: double->double, lossless; both sites share pattern and k, so spikes land at flat index 0 in BOTH A and B.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen/derivable domain: gemm imposes no structural constraint, so the domain is purely numeric - element magnitudes must keep the K-term accumulation finite and its rounding well inside the ABSOLUTE 1e-4 tolerance (cpu.cc:86, utilities.hpp:482); the frozen value range is the call-site [-1.0, 1.0] at cpu.cc:70-71, under which every non-extreme pattern is fully valid.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: double literals, lossless override cast. Numeric: absolute 1e-4 vs K-term sums means range r gives |C| up to K*r^2 (=1024 at r=1, fine); widening r to 100 gives |C| ~ 1e7 where reorder rounding (~1e-9 relative) approaches 1e-2 absolute -> false failures. Keep value_range modest.

domain.summary: None structural: gemv is defined for any finite input. Numeric: row dot products (N terms) must stay finite and compatible with ABSOLUTE tolerance 1e-4; at the frozen [-10,10] range, |y| <= N*100 ~ 1e5 for every non-extreme pattern - reorder rounding ~1e-11 relative -> ~1e-6 absolute, safely inside 1e-4.
known_restrictions: None structural: gemv is defined for any finite input. Numeric: row dot products (N terms) must stay finite and compatible with ABSOLUTE tolerance 1e-4; at the frozen [-10,10] range, |y| <= N*100 ~ 1e5 for every non-extreme pattern - reorder rounding ~1e-11 relative -> ~1e-6 absolute, safely inside 1e-4.
tripwires: none in cpu.cc. Harness-level non_finite_reference BI marker: fired deterministically by extreme_values (every y[i] is a mixed-sign sum of +-Inf -> NaN/Inf) and by spike_at k=0 (y[0] += A[0][0]*x[0] = (DBL_MAX/2)^2 = Inf; additionally most other rows overflow because |A[i][0]*x[0]| = |A[i][0]|*9e307 > DBL_MAX whenever |A[i][0]| > ~2, i.e. ~80% of rows at range [-10,10]). Baseline-gate-only signals; no finite-wrong-reference pattern exists.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen/derivable domain: gemv imposes no structural constraint, so the domain is purely numeric - element magnitudes must keep the N-term row dot products finite and their rounding well inside the ABSOLUTE 1e-4 tolerance (cpu.cc:82, utilities.hpp:482); the frozen value range is the call-site [-10.0, 10.0] at cpu.cc:69-70, at which |y| <= N*100 ~ 1e5 and reorder noise stays ~1e-10.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: double literals, lossless override. Absolute 1e-4 vs N-term sums: range r gives |y| ~ N*r^2 (1e5 at r=10) - already only ~7 decimal digits of absolute headroom; widening r by 10x brings reorder noise to ~1e-4 territory -> false failures. The frozen [-10,10] is near the safe ceiling for this tolerance at N=1024; larger TEST_SIZE tightens it further (linear in N).

domain.summary: HARD size restriction: the iterative Rosetta fft() oracle (baseline.hpp:13-58) is only correct AND only memory-safe for N in {0,1,2} union powers of two. For non-power-of-two N >= 3 the butterfly index b=a+k runs past the end (verified by index math: N=7 -> stage n=3,k=1 reaches a=6, b=7 -> x[7] OOB read+write on a size-7 vector; N=5 -> b=5; N=1000 -> stage n=15,k=7 reaches b=1003) = heap OOB UB in the ORACLE. The globally offered static size 7 (specs.py:134) is therefore domain-INVALID for this benchmark, and any LLM-chosen non-power-of-two size <= 4096 is equally unsafe. Value domain: finite doubles small enough that FFT partial sums stay finite and the 1e-4 ABSOLUTE tolerance stays meaningful (baseline range [-1.0, 1.0]).
known_restrictions: HARD size restriction: the iterative Rosetta fft() oracle (baseline.hpp:13-58) is only correct AND only memory-safe for N in {0,1,2} union powers of two. For non-power-of-two N >= 3 the butterfly index b=a+k runs past the end (verified by index math: N=7 -> stage n=3,k=1 reaches a=6, b=7 -> x[7] OOB read+write on a size-7 vector; N=5 -> b=5; N=1000 -> stage n=15,k=7 reaches b=1003) = heap OOB UB in the ORACLE. The globally offered static size 7 (specs.py:134) is therefore domain-INVALID for this benchmark, and any LLM-chosen non-power-of-two size <= 4096 is equally unsafe. Value domain: finite doubles small enough that FFT partial sums stay finite and the 1e-4 ABSOLUTE tolerance stays meaningful (baseline range [-1.0, 1.0]).
tripwires: none in cpu.cc (no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard in the driver). Harness-level A1b tripwire applies: reportAndCompareWith skips any index whose REFERENCE value is non-finite and emits 'BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference' once per process (utilities.hpp:363-378, 422-428). Offered pattern extreme_values deterministically fires it: x[i]=(+-DBL_MAX,+-DBL_MAX), first butterfly x[a]+=x[b] pairs same-parity indices (stride N/2, even for N>=4) -> equal-sign DBL_MAX additions -> inf/NaN through all stages -> EVERY graded index skipped -> validation passes VACUOUSLY (total==0) with only the BI marker = baseline-gate-only risk, zero discrimination.

benchmarks.domain_note: Judgments below use the frozen/derivable domain TEST_SIZE in {0,1,2} union powers of two (the only sizes at which the iterative Rosetta fft() oracle is both index-safe and a true transform) with a non-empty graded set, and finite complex components drawn from the call-site range [-1.0,1.0] whose magnitudes keep N*max|x| far enough below DBL_MAX that the 1e-4 ABSOLUTE per-component tolerance stays meaningful; the offered static size 7, TEST_SIZE==0 and value_range overrides fall OUTSIDE that domain and are recorded as explicit verdict_outcome_conditions rather than folded into the axis values.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: value_range overrides lo/hi as doubles; deduced DType stays double (call-site literals) so it is always type-safe. Risk is purely numeric: FFT output magnitude scales ~ N*max|x|; with abs tol 1e-4 and N=1024, ranges beyond roughly +-1e6 make rounding differences approach the tolerance, and extreme ranges (~1e305+) overflow -> non-finite reference -> BI vacuous pass. The ifft 1/N normalization gives this benchmark slightly more headroom than the forward-FFT ones.

extreme_values.notes: Option A (element-type extrema, what the site does today since DType==double==value_type): x[i] = (-DBL_MAX,-DBL_MAX) for even i and (+DBL_MAX,+DBL_MAX) for odd i. The first butterfly pairs same-parity indices (stride N/2, even for N>=4) and so adds two equal-sign DBL_MAX components -> +-inf; later stages evaluate inf-inf -> NaN. CORRECTED vs the previous note in two ways. (1) The non-finiteness is PARTIAL, not total: hand-simulating N=8 gives x = [NaN, -inf, NaN, NaN, 0, 0, 0, 0] before the bit-reversal permutation, because the difference leg of the first butterfly is exactly 0 for an equal pair. Some graded indices therefore keep a finite reference and are really compared. (2) The outcome is NOT a 'vacuous pass': the run is classified NO_VERDICT_BI. Emitting even ONE non-finite reference triggers mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference (utilities.hpp:425-426 -> :363-378), and the authenticated marker is what the runner keys on, so no pass is ever counted for this spec and the model is not even executed. FP overflow to inf/NaN is IEEE-defined, so oracle_execution_safe stays true; the damage is entirely on the verdict axis. Option B (domain extrema from lo/hi, i.e. +-1.0): finite, safe, and already expressible as the 'alternating' pattern; trivially derivable since lo/hi are visible at the call site.

spike_at.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE pending EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS)
spike_at.notes: Because both fill sites share one pattern config, the spike element becomes (DBL_MAX/2, DBL_MAX/2), modulus ~1.27e308. Unit-modulus twiddle rotations preserve modulus so intermediates generically stay finite (components <= modulus < DBL_MAX; complex-mult cross terms can reach |z|*sqrt(2) ~= DBL_MAX, borderline overflow in worst-case phases -> possible BI). Even when fully finite: oracle vs candidate differ by summation-order rounding at magnitude ~1e308 (1 ulp ~ 1e292), infinitely larger than the 1e-4 ABSOLUTE tolerance -> deterministic FALSE FAIL for any implementation that is not bit-identical to the oracle. The 1/N ifft scaling (~1e305 after /1024) does not change this. RELAYERED: the previous entry set baseline_gate_only_risk=true although its own text described a tolerance false fail rather than a BI-only path; baseline_gate_only_risk is now 'conditional' (only the overflow branch goes BI) and the false-fail statement lives on the verdict axis. parallel_bias_risk=true: reassociation is exactly what omp/mpi candidates do, and the tolerance is absolute, so parallel candidates are hit harder than serial ones.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: The iterative Rosetta fft() oracle computes the butterfly partner as b = a + k without bounding b by N. For any N >= 3 that is not a power of two the final stages reach b == N or beyond and both READ x[b] and WRITE x[b] past the end of a size-N vector (verified index math: N=7 -> stage n=3,k=1 reaches a=6, b=7; N=5 -> b=5; N=1000 -> stage n=15,k=7 reaches b=1003). thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:134 sets static_base_sizes=[0,1,2,7], so size 7 is offered today and the hazard is reachable; any LLM-chosen non-power-of-two size <= max_spec_size (4096) is equally unsafe. This is an ORACLE hazard, not a fill-site hazard: both fill sites remain double->double and fill_type_safe.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - guard correctIfft/fft against non-power-of-two N (or add a driver-level BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE tripwire), and DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED to restrict this benchmark's spec sizes to {0,1,2} union powers of two.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow in the oracle, NOT undefined behaviour: same-parity +-DBL_MAX components are added in the first butterfly (baseline.hpp:29) giving +-inf, and later stages evaluate inf-inf giving NaN. Execution is well defined, but the non-finite reference values reach the comparator, which emits the authenticated process-wide BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker and skips those indices. The result is loss of the model verdict, not a fill or memory fault.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - either exclude extreme_values for the fft family or redefine it as the domain extrema +-1.0 taken from the visible call-site lo/hi. Do NOT file this as a fill-site type fix.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Two distinct, non-UB hazards. (a) The spike element (DBL_MAX/2, DBL_MAX/2) has modulus ~1.27e308; worst-case twiddle phases can push a complex-multiply cross term to within rounding distance of DBL_MAX, so an intermediate may round to inf and produce a non-finite reference. (b) Far more reliably, the oracle output magnitude is ~1e308 while the driver grades with an ABSOLUTE per-component tolerance of 1e-4, so the reference is not reproducible by any candidate that reassociates - a tolerance hazard sitting on the verdict axis.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS / VALUE_RANGE_DOMAIN_POLICY) - exclude spike_at for the fft family or cap value_range; if it is kept, a relative tolerance would be required. Not a fill-site fix.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern effect is EFFECTIVE via ENHANCED_FILL; no benchmark-native adapter needed. The needed intervention is size-domain policy (power-of-two whitelist), not a pattern adapter.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Source-side: heap vectors only, O(N log N) oracle, no fixed buffers; int loop counters (cpu.cc:70,77) fine below 2^31. Powers of two > 4096 (8192, 16384, ...) work; only max_spec_size=4096 blocks them. NOTE: the power-of-two requirement is a DOMAIN constraint at every size, not a large-size blocker per se - but any large-size policy for this benchmark must restrict to powers of two or the oracle commits OOB UB.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: size policy below must be settled first) - fully size- and pattern-parameterizable, and both fill sites are unconditionally fill-type-safe (double literals -> DType=double -> vector<double>)

ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - the offered static size 7 (and any non-power-of-two LLM size <= 4096) makes the oracle commit heap OOB read+write inside fft() (baseline.hpp:27-30 index math). This is an oracle/memory hazard, NOT a fill-site type problem; guard the oracle or gate the size.
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - restrict spec sizes to {0,1,2} union powers of two (the policy half of the action above)

benchmarks.notes: Comparison uses Wave-1 reportAndCompareWith with the verbatim historical predicate (cpu.cc:90-103): size mismatch is rejected (utilities.hpp:401-408), non-finite candidate against a finite reference fails (:430-438), non-finite REFERENCE emits the authenticated BI marker and is skipped (:425-426). The only counted-pass-without-check in this benchmark is TEST_SIZE==0.

benchmarks.size_rationale: TEST_SIZE sizes the input x and both output vectors correct/test (cpu.cc:52-53); nothing in the validate path stays static.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Single ENHANCED_FILL site fully determines the only input vector; every pattern choice changes the whole input.
benchmarks.input_construction: validate() fills one double vector x via ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:61), BCASTs it (62). Oracle: correctDft (baseline.hpp:16-29), direct O(N^2) DFT that resizes output to N and accumulates x[n]*(cos,-sin) in double (the n*k product is computed in double: 2*M_PI*n*k/N promotes left-to-right, no int overflow). Candidate: dft(x, test) (cpu.cc:68). Comparison: reportAndCompareWith, verbatim predicate, tol 1e-4 (cpu.cc:77-83); helper rejects a resized candidate before element access.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: VERIFIED at cpu.cc:61: ENHANCED_FILL(x, -1.0, 1.0) deduces DType=double from the literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and x is std::vector<double>, so every offered pattern - including extreme_values (numeric_limits<double>::lowest()/max()), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2) and explicit_values (enhancedFromDouble<double> is a double->double static_cast, enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171) - assigns a double to a double. There is no narrowing and no float->integral conversion, so the site is unconditionally type-safe for ARBITRARY spec values, not merely conditionally so.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType=double matches value_type; no conversion, no UB at the site for any offered pattern.

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none (reset() uses fillRand on the timing path only, cpu.cc:27)

domain.summary: No size restriction: the direct DFT is defined for every N including 0, 1, 2, 7 (all offered static sizes safe; verified: correctDft loops are plain 0..N-1, output resized to N). Value domain: |output| <= N*max|x|; with abs tol 1e-4, input magnitudes must stay small enough that N*max|x| rounding noise << 1e-4 (baseline [-1.0,1.0] at N=1024 -> outputs <= ~1e3, rounding ~1e-13, comfortably valid).
known_restrictions: No size restriction: the direct DFT is defined for every N including 0, 1, 2, 7 (all offered static sizes safe; verified: correctDft loops are plain 0..N-1, output resized to N). Value domain: |output| <= N*max|x|; with abs tol 1e-4, input magnitudes must stay small enough that N*max|x| rounding noise << 1e-4 (baseline [-1.0,1.0] at N=1024 -> outputs <= ~1e3, rounding ~1e-13, comfortably valid).
tripwires: none in cpu.cc. Harness-level A1b non-finite-reference tripwire (utilities.hpp:363-378, 422-428) fires under extreme_values: the alternating +-DBL_MAX input concentrates DFT energy at bin N/2; correctDft's partial sums at k=N/2 accumulate same-sign DBL_MAX terms -> -inf after two terms -> non-finite reference at that bin -> BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker, index skipped. Unlike the recursive-FFT benchmarks this is a PARTIAL BI (most other bins stay finite), so extreme_values here is a mixed BI + false-negative risk, not a fully vacuous pass.

benchmarks.domain_note: Judgments below use the frozen/derivable domain of ANY TEST_SIZE >= 0 with a non-empty graded set (the direct O(N^2) DFT oracle is index-safe and semantically correct at every N, including the offered static sizes 0/1/2/7) and finite doubles from the call-site range [-1.0,1.0] whose magnitudes keep N*max|x| far enough below DBL_MAX that the 1e-4 ABSOLUTE per-component tolerance stays meaningful (roughly |bound| <= 1e6 at N=1024); TEST_SIZE==0, value_range overrides and unvalidated explicit_values magnitudes fall OUTSIDE that domain and are recorded as explicit verdict_outcome_conditions rather than folded into the axis values.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Always type-safe (DType stays double). Numeric risk only: output scale ~ N*max|x| vs abs tol 1e-4. At N=1024 ranges up to roughly +-1e6 keep rounding noise well under 1e-4; ranges approaching ~1e305/N overflow to inf -> partial BI. A conservative cap (e.g. |bound| <= 1e6) removes the risk.

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: spec-value dependent - E2 must validate value magnitudes against the frozen domain, since specs.py currently validates neither magnitude nor finiteness)
explicit_values.notes: values are arbitrary spec-supplied doubles. RELAYERED: the previous entry carried the generic warning that 'for int containers enhancedFromDouble static_casts them (out-of-range = UB)'. That hazard does NOT apply here - this benchmark's only fill site is a std::vector<double> with DType=double, so enhancedFromDouble<double> is a double->double cast and the site is unconditionally fill_type_safe=true for arbitrary spec values. The genuine, spec-value-dependent risk is a DOMAIN risk (magnitude vs the 1e-4 absolute tolerance, and unvalidated inf/NaN), which is where it now sits; the missing magnitude validation in specs.py remains a real E2 action but is a domain-policy action, not a fill-site type fix. This is the only fft-family benchmark where explicit_values is enabled at all.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow in the oracle, NOT undefined behaviour: at k = N/2 the twiddle cos(pi*n) = (-1)^n cancels the alternating input sign, so every term of the partial sum is -DBL_MAX and the accumulator reaches -inf after two terms. Execution is well defined; the damage is that a non-finite reference reaches the comparator, which emits the authenticated process-wide BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker. Partial rather than total: the other bins stay finite but are DBL_MAX-scale cancellation sums that no reassociating candidate can reproduce under an absolute 1e-4 tolerance.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - exclude extreme_values for the fft family or redefine it as the domain extrema +-1.0 taken from the visible call-site lo/hi. Do NOT file this as a fill-site type fix; the fill site is a vector<double> and is type-safe.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: NOT an oracle execution hazard - correctDft's partial sums are bounded by DBL_MAX/2 + N and stay finite. The hazard is that every reference bin has magnitude ~9e307 while the driver grades with an ABSOLUTE per-component tolerance of 1e-4, so the reference is not reproducible by any candidate that reassociates. Recorded here to keep the finding out of the fill layer; it belongs to the domain/verdict layer.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS / VALUE_RANGE_DOMAIN_POLICY) - exclude spike_at for the fft family or cap value_range; a relative tolerance would be required to keep it.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Spec-supplied doubles are neither magnitude- nor finiteness-validated by specs.py, so a spec can hand the oracle values whose partial sums overflow to inf (non-finite reference -> A1b marker) or values large enough that the absolute 1e-4 tolerance is meaningless. Again well-defined IEEE execution, so oracle_execution_safe stays true; the exposure is on the domain and verdict axes.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - add spec-layer validation of explicit_values magnitudes (and finiteness) against each benchmark's frozen domain. This is a spec/domain guard, NOT a FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES action.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern effect already EFFECTIVE through the single ENHANCED_FILL site; no adapter needed.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: No structural blocker: heap vectors, output resized by oracle, int N = x.size() (baseline.hpp:17) only narrows above 2^31. BUT the oracle is O(N^2) and runs MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2 times (plus an O(N^2) candidate): N=4096 -> ~1.7e7 inner iterations/try (fast); N=65536 -> ~4.3e9/try (minutes). So only the 4096 spec policy blocks, with a quadratic-runtime practical ceiling to probe.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: value_range / explicit_values magnitudes must stay inside domain_note) - cleanest fft-family benchmark: 1 unconditionally type-safe fill site, explicit_values supported, and no size restriction at all (all static sizes 0/1/2/7 are semantically valid and index-safe)

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - extreme_values yields NO_VERDICT_BI (the oracle-only gate probe emits the authenticated BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker at bin N/2, so the model never runs) with deterministic false fails behind it; spike_at yields a numerically_unstable gate / abs-tolerance false fail. Decide exclusion or a value_range cap.

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - validate explicit_values magnitudes and finiteness at the spec layer: specs.py validates neither today. Explicitly NOT a FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES action - the fill site is vector<double> with DType=double and is type-safe for arbitrary spec doubles.

benchmarks.size_rationale: TEST_SIZE sizes real, imag and x (cpu.cc:58-59); the whole validate input scales with the override.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Both component vectors are ENHANCED_FILL-controlled and fully determine x; pattern choice changes the entire input (per-component semantics, re=im diagonal for deterministic ramps).
benchmarks.input_construction: validate() fills real/imag via ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:67-68), BCASTs (69-70), assembles x[j]=complex(real[j],imag[j]) (72-74). Oracle: fftCooleyTookey (baseline.hpp:101-113) = recursive radix-2 DFT (pareval_harness::fftRecursionNoConjugate, baseline.hpp:74-97) with exactly one top-level conjugation (frozen I12 fix). Candidate: fftConjugate(test) (cpu.cc:82). Comparison: reportAndCompareWith, verbatim predicate, tol 1e-3 (cpu.cc:89-95). Note the widest tolerance in the family (1e-3 vs 1e-4).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: VERIFIED at cpu.cc:67: DType is deduced from the double literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and matches std::vector<double>::value_type, so every offered pattern - extreme_values (+-DBL_MAX), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2), ramps, midpoint, alternating - performs a double->double assignment with no conversion. No pattern can produce narrowing or an out-of-range float->integral conversion at this site, and nothing the oracle does downstream can change that.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: double->double, no conversion; no pattern can produce conversion UB here.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: Identical to line 67 (double literals -> DType=double -> vector<double>). Both sites receive the same pattern id and the same k, so a k-pattern hits real[k] and imag[k] together; that is a semantic observation about the assembled complex sample (cpu.cc:72-74), not a type-safety issue at the site.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: Same as line 67; both sites share one pattern config (same pattern and k).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: None in validate() beyond the deterministic assembly loop (cpu.cc:72-74); reset() uses fillRand on the timing path (cpu.cc:26-27).

domain.summary: SOFT size restriction (no UB, unlike 05): the recursive oracle fftCooleyTookey computes a true conj(DFT) only for N in {0,1} union powers of two (N<=1 handled explicitly incl. the I12 conj-of-single-sample case, baseline.hpp:101-107). For non-power-of-two N (incl. offered static size 7) the recursion floor-halves and silently drops trailing elements (N=7: x[6] never enters the butterflies; correct[6] = conj(input[6])), so the oracle is NOT a Fourier transform -> a semantically correct candidate FAILS (false negative). Memory-safe throughout. Value domain: finite doubles, magnitudes such that N*max|x| keeps the 1e-3 abs tolerance meaningful.

For non-power-of-two N (incl. offered static size 7) the recursion floor-halves and silently drops trailing elements (N=7: x[6] never enters the butterflies; correct[6] = conj(input[6])), so the oracle is NOT a Fourier transform -> a semantically correct candidate FAILS (false negative). Baseline-gate-only risk with zero discrimination.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: SEMANTIC hazard, explicitly NOT undefined behaviour: pareval_harness::fftRecursionNoConjugate floor-halves N at every level and only ever indexes even/odd halves that exist, so it is memory-safe at every size - VERIFIED. But for any N outside {0,1} union powers of two the recursion silently drops trailing elements (N=7: x[6] never enters a butterfly, so correct[6] ends up as conj(input[6])), which means the frozen oracle is not a Fourier transform and a semantically CORRECT candidate is marked wrong. specs.py:134 offers static size 7 today, so this false-negative path is reachable.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - restrict this benchmark's spec sizes to {0,1} union powers of two. ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED is the alternative (emit BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE for a non-power-of-two N instead of grading a non-DFT). Not a fill-site action - both sites stay type-safe.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow in the oracle, NOT undefined behaviour: the even/odd split groups identical-sign extremes, so the combine adds two equal-sign DBL_MAX components (baseline.hpp:94-95) giving +-inf, and the difference leg then evaluates inf-inf giving NaN. Execution is well defined, but the non-finite reference values reach the comparator, which emits the authenticated process-wide BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker and skips those indices. The result is loss of the model verdict, not a fill or memory fault.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - exclude extreme_values for the fft family or redefine it as the domain extrema +-1.0 from the visible call-site lo/hi. Do NOT file this as a fill-site type fix.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Two distinct, non-UB hazards. (a) The spike element (DBL_MAX/2, DBL_MAX/2) has modulus ~1.27e308; worst-case twiddle phases can push a complex-multiply cross term to within rounding distance of DBL_MAX, so an intermediate may round to inf and produce a non-finite reference. (b) Far more reliably, the oracle output magnitude is ~1e308 while the driver grades with an ABSOLUTE per-component tolerance of 1e-3, so the reference is not reproducible by any candidate that reassociates - a tolerance hazard sitting on the verdict axis.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS / VALUE_RANGE_DOMAIN_POLICY) - exclude spike_at for the fft family or cap value_range; a relative tolerance would be required to keep it. Not a fill-site fix.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: SEMANTIC hazard, explicitly NOT undefined behaviour: the validate oracle fftCooleyTookey floor-halves N at every level and only indexes halves that exist, with an N<=1 early return - memory-safe at every size, VERIFIED. But for any N outside {0,1} union powers of two the recursion silently drops trailing elements (N=7: x_copy[6] never enters a butterfly, so correctReal[6]/correctImag[6] are the raw input components), so the frozen oracle is not a Fourier transform and a semantically CORRECT candidate is marked wrong. specs.py:134 offers static size 7 today, so this false-negative path is reachable.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - restrict this benchmark's spec sizes to {0,1} union powers of two; ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED is the alternative (emit BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE for a non-power-of-two N instead of grading a non-DFT). Not a fill-site action - both sites stay type-safe.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow in the oracle, NOT undefined behaviour: the even/odd split groups identical-sign extremes, so the combine adds two equal-sign DBL_MAX components (baseline.hpp:86-87) giving +-inf, and the difference leg then evaluates inf-inf giving NaN. Those values are copied into correctReal/correctImag (cpu.cc:82-85) and reach BOTH comparator calls, which emit the authenticated process-wide BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker and skip the affected indices. Loss of the model verdict, not a fill or memory fault.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - exclude extreme_values for the fft family or redefine it as the domain extrema +-1.0 from the visible call-site lo/hi. Do NOT file this as a fill-site type fix.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Two distinct, non-UB hazards. (a) The spike element (DBL_MAX/2, DBL_MAX/2) has modulus ~1.27e308; worst-case twiddle phases can push a complex-multiply cross term to within rounding distance of DBL_MAX, so an intermediate may round to inf and produce a non-finite reference. (b) Far more reliably, the oracle output magnitude is ~1e308 while both split halves are graded with an ABSOLUTE tolerance of 1e-4, so the reference is not reproducible by any candidate that reassociates - a tolerance hazard sitting on the verdict axis.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: SEMANTIC hazard, explicitly NOT undefined behaviour: the validate oracle fftCooleyTookey floor-halves N at every level and only indexes halves that exist, with an N<=1 early return - memory-safe at every size, VERIFIED. But for any N outside {0,1} union powers of two the recursion silently drops trailing elements (N=7: x[6] never enters a butterfly, so correct[6] keeps the raw input value), so the frozen oracle is not a Fourier transform and a semantically CORRECT candidate is marked wrong. specs.py:134 offers static size 7 today, so this false-negative path is reachable.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - restrict this benchmark's spec sizes to {0,1} union powers of two; ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED is the alternative (emit BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE for a non-power-of-two N instead of grading a non-DFT). Not a fill-site action - both sites stay type-safe.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow in the oracle, NOT undefined behaviour: the even/odd split groups identical-sign extremes, so the combine adds two equal-sign DBL_MAX components (baseline.hpp:83-84) giving +-inf, and the difference leg then evaluates inf-inf giving NaN. Execution is well defined, but the non-finite reference values reach the comparator, which emits the authenticated process-wide BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker and skips those indices. Loss of the model verdict, not a fill or memory fault.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) - exclude extreme_values for the fft family or redefine it as the domain extrema +-1.0 from the visible call-site lo/hi. Do NOT file this as a fill-site type fix.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Two distinct, non-UB hazards. (a) The spike element (DBL_MAX/2, DBL_MAX/2) has modulus ~1.27e308; worst-case twiddle phases can push a complex-multiply cross term to within rounding distance of DBL_MAX, so an intermediate may round to inf and produce a non-finite reference. (b) Far more reliably, the oracle output magnitude is ~1e308 while the driver grades with an ABSOLUTE per-component tolerance of 1e-4, so the reference is not reproducible by any candidate that reassociates - a tolerance hazard sitting on the verdict axis.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS / VALUE_RANGE_DOMAIN_POLICY) - exclude spike_at for the fft family or cap value_range; a relative tolerance would be required to keep it. Not a fill-site fix.

benchmarks.size_rationale: All validate() inputs derive from TEST_SIZE: points(TEST_SIZE), x(TEST_SIZE), y(TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:65-66); correct/test are outputs sized by the algorithms. Nothing in the validation path is statically sized. reset()/init() use DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE but feed only the perf path (compute/best), not validate().
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Both coordinate arrays - the entirety of the validation input - are ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:74-75). Caveat: the same global pattern is applied to x AND y, so deterministic patterns collapse the 2-D geometry onto the line y=x: all_zeros/all_same -> one coincident point; alternating/extreme_values -> exactly 2 distinct points; ascending/descending -> collinear ramp. These are legitimate degenerate-hull edge cases (Wave-2B baseline handles them via dedup), but no offered pattern produces a structured NON-degenerate 2-D configuration.
benchmarks.input_construction: validate() builds x,y via ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:74-75), then zips them into points[i].x/.y (cpu.cc:81-84). Oracle correctConvexHull (baseline.hpp:11-70, Wave-2B: dedup to DISTINCT point set, <3 distinct -> those points; else monotone chain). Verdict: size check + sorted coordinate-wise reportAndCompare with eps 1e-6 (cpu.cc:95-129).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the lo/hi ARGUMENTS (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and both are double literals, so DType == vector<double>::value_type: every pattern value is stored by a double-to-double assignment with NO conversion. extreme_values writes lowest()/max() (+-DBL_MAX, finite and exactly representable) and spike_at writes DBL_MAX/2, also representable; an ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI override is cast to decltype(lo)=double, so no override can introduce narrowing or an out-of-range conversion at this site.
