benchmarks.adapter_notes: A benchmark-native axis is methodically clean: edge density p (replace rand()%2 with Bernoulli(p)), plus deterministic structure classes (empty / complete / single-edge / star) that stress the counting loop's boundary behaviour. All are {0,1}-preserving and oracle-compatible. What must NOT happen: reusing the 11 numeric pattern names (extreme_values, spike_at, ...) for matrix cell values - that invents numeric-pattern-on-structure semantics and breaks the domain. A separate graph-pattern vocabulary and a spec-layer mapping policy are required.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap std::vector sized size_t (cpu.cc:65); no fixed buffers, no power-of-two requirement. Scaling caveats only: O(N^2) memory (spec size is N, elements N^2: N=8192 -> ~268MB int matrix) and O(N^2) generator/oracle time; oracle's int edge count (baseline.hpp:16) would overflow only for N > ~46340 dense. Nothing in the code blocks e.g. 8192; only the global max_spec_size=4096 policy does.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (size-axis only) - size axis fully effective (validate scales all of A from ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE, cpu.cc:63-65)
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - for the current 11 numeric patterns: no fill site, and wiring one onto adjacency cells would break the {0,1} domain
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - if pattern coverage is wanted, add a graph-native structure/density adapter (Bernoulli(p) density, empty/complete/star classes)
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - define a graph-pattern vocabulary at the spec layer instead of mapping numeric pattern names to structure
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - >4096 is code-feasible but quadratic (N=8192 ~268MB, O(N^2) time); measure before raising the cap
benchmarks.notes: Only graph benchmark whose generator permits self-loops (diagonal not excluded, cpu.cc:28-34 - re-verified) and whose matrix is directed; the oracle counts those diagonal 1s consistently. shapes JSON entry (fill_sites: 0) verified accurate. DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (cpu.cc:45) only affects the perf context, not validate. benchmarks.adapter_notes: Native axes are clean and directly stress component structure: edge density p, forced component-count profiles (k disjoint cliques/paths of chosen sizes), fully disconnected (empty) vs fully connected (complete) graphs. All are symmetric {0,1} constructions the oracle handles. Reusing numeric pattern names for cell values would invent structure semantics -> not allowed; a graph vocabulary + policy mapping is needed. Note: an all-ones-offdiagonal (complete) variant drives oracle dfs recursion depth to N - fine at N<=4096, relevant for large-size probes.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vectors, size_t sizing, no fixed buffers or power-of-two constraints. Scaling caveats: O(N^2) memory/time (N=8192 -> ~268MB), and the oracle's RECURSIVE dfs (baseline.hpp:8-16) recurses once per vertex of a component - depth up to N. At N=8192 a dense random graph makes one giant component -> ~8192-deep recursion, marginal on a 1MB default stack (Windows), comfortable on 8MB (Linux). Nothing hard-blocks moderately larger sizes; only the 4096 spec policy does, but the recursion depth must be watched in any probe.

NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - for the numeric pattern set (no fill site; raw fills break {0,1} + symmetry invariants)
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - symmetric graph-native generator (density p, planted component profiles) if variation coverage is wanted
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - graph-pattern vocabulary at the spec layer
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - quadratic memory plus recursive oracle DFS depth up to N (baseline.hpp:8-16); check stack limits before sizes >4096
benchmarks.notes: Identical driver skeleton to 17/18 but default size 128 (17/18 use 512). shapes JSON verified (fill_sites: 0). RELAYERING: no reachable fill hook -> all four axes NOT_APPLICABLE for all 11 labels; the verdict is an EXACT int scalar comparison (cpu.cc:84 -> reportAndCompareScalar, utilities.hpp:552-553 -> operator==), and mismatchIsFinite (utilities.hpp:174) is compile-time true for integral types, so the non-finite/BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE route (utilities.hpp:517-523) cannot fire for this benchmark, so no BI and no vacuous-pass path exists. DE-CONTRADICTION: E1 recorded the near-constant-oracle-output weakness only for graph/18 although 16 uses the very same fillRandomUndirectedGraph at p=0.5 - at N=128 the graph is almost surely connected and the oracle returns exactly N, so the verdict class is REDUCED, not INFORMATIVE, and the KEEP recommendation carries that qualifier. Recursive oracle DFS (baseline.hpp:8-16) with depth up to N is the one latent scaling hazard shared with 18; fine at the current 4096 cap, worth checking above it.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Native axes are clean and benchmark-relevant: edge density p, planted degree profiles (star graph -> one max-degree hub; regular graph -> tie-heavy max; empty -> degree 0), all symmetric {0,1} and oracle-safe. Reusing numeric pattern names for cells is disallowed (invented semantics) and uniquely dangerous here (raw-summing oracle, see extreme_values_audit). Needs the same spec-layer graph vocabulary policy as the rest of the family.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vectors, size_t sizing, iterative O(N^2) oracle (baseline.hpp:16-26) - no recursion, no fixed buffers, no power-of-two constraint. Max degree N-1 fits int far beyond any realistic size. Only caveats are O(N^2) memory/time (default 512 already allocates 1MB; N=8192 -> ~268MB). Only the global 4096 spec policy blocks larger sizes.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (size-axis only) - size axis fully effective
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - numeric patterns; additionally the raw-summing oracle makes any out-of-domain cell value oracle-UB-prone
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - degree-profile/density generator (star, regular, empty, Bernoulli(p)) if variation coverage is wanted
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - graph-pattern vocabulary; also record the frozen 'cells are {0,1}' premise since the oracle depends on it more strongly than the prompt states

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - oracle sums raw values (baseline.hpp:21) vs siblings' ==1 tests; harmless under the current generator (no fill hook can reach it today) but a latent divergence any future fill/adapter must respect

ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED (conditional - only if a fill site or a value-carrying adapter is ever added here): large cell values would be summed into the int degree accumulator at baseline.hpp:21 and can overflow it (signed overflow = UB). This is an ORACLE-layer guard, NOT a fill-site type fix; it is NOT actionable today because no pattern can reach the input
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - quadratic memory/time only; no code blocker beyond the 4096 policy
benchmarks.notes: Default 512 (vs 128 for 15/16). shapes JSON verified (fill_sites: 0). The 'degree += raw value' oracle (baseline.hpp:21, re-verified) is the family's most fill-sensitive oracle DESPITE having no fill site: under the current generator it is exactly equivalent to counting == 1, so it is harmless today. RELAYERING: that hazard is an ORACLE-layer, not a fill-layer, concern - E1 carried it only in prose and in value_range_risk, so it is now filed as a conditional ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED e2 action; oracle_execution_safe stays NOT_APPLICABLE (not false) because no reachable pattern can produce a hazardous input, and oracle_hazards stays empty for the same reason. the verdict is an EXACT int scalar comparison (cpu.cc:84 -> reportAndCompareScalar, utilities.hpp:552-553 -> operator==), and mismatchIsFinite (utilities.hpp:174) is compile-time true for integral types, so the non-finite/BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE route (utilities.hpp:517-523) cannot fire for this benchmark.

benchmarks.size_rationale: Whole input A(TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:65) sized by the override; generator (cpu.cc:73) and oracle/candidate (cpu.cc:77,80) use TEST_SIZE. Static sizes 0,1,2,7 safe: N=0 -> 0 components (empty loop, baseline.hpp:24-34); N=1 -> 1 component.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Zero ENHANCED_FILL sites (grep-verified); pattern choice cannot change the input at fixed size. benchmark_shapes.json hint (fill_sites: 0) VERIFIED CORRECT. Note the default random graph at N=512, p=0.5 is essentially always ONE component, so the oracle answer is nearly constant - a native adapter (below) would add real discriminative variation.
benchmarks.input_construction: fillRandomUndirectedGraph(A, TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:26-35): zero diagonal, symmetric rand()%2 upper triangle; validate call at cpu.cc:73. No ENHANCED_FILL.
benchmarks.other_input_constructors: fillRandomUndirectedGraph (cpu.cc:26-35), the only input builder; not pattern-controlled
input_types: int (symmetric adjacency matrix cells, domain {0,1}, zero diagonal)

domain.summary: Cells in {0,1}, symmetric, zero diagonal. Oracle DFS follows only cells == 1 (baseline.hpp:11); non-{0,1} or asymmetric inputs diverge from !=0-style solutions and violate the undirected premise.
known_restrictions: Cells in {0,1}, symmetric, zero diagonal. Oracle DFS follows only cells == 1 (baseline.hpp:11); non-{0,1} or asymmetric inputs diverge from !=0-style solutions and violate the undirected premise.
tripwires: none (no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard; grep-verified)

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen domain: an N x N row-major SYMMETRIC adjacency matrix with cells in {0,1} and a zero diagonal (cpu.cc:29-33), N >= 0; the oracle's recursive DFS follows only cells == 1 (baseline.hpp:11), so asymmetric or non-{0,1} matrices are outside the domain.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: This is the graph benchmark where a native adapter pays off most: the current generator almost surely yields exactly 1 component at N=512/p=0.5, so component-count variation (k planted disjoint blocks, empty graph -> N components, complete graph -> 1) is both methodically clean and materially improves discrimination. All variants are symmetric {0,1}. Mapping numeric pattern names onto cells remains disallowed (invented semantics); spec-layer graph vocabulary needed. Dense variants push oracle DFS recursion toward depth N - relevant only above the current cap.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vectors, size_t sizing, no fixed buffers or power-of-two constraints; O(N^2) memory/time scaling (N=8192 -> ~268MB). Oracle uses RECURSIVE dfs (baseline.hpp:8-15) with depth up to the largest component size (~N for dense random graphs): ~8192 frames at N=8192, marginal on 1MB stacks, fine on 8MB. Only the global 4096 policy is a hard blocker today.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED discrimination) - size axis fully effective, but at N=512/p=0.5 the oracle answer is essentially always 1; keep the small static sizes and/or add the adapter below
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - numeric patterns (no fill site; raw fills break invariants)
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - planted-component-count generator (k blocks / empty / complete) would fix the near-constant oracle output of the current p=0.5 generator
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - graph-pattern vocabulary at the spec layer
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - quadratic memory plus recursive oracle DFS depth up to N (baseline.hpp:8-15); check stack limits before sizes >4096
benchmarks.notes: Same skeleton as 16/17. shapes JSON verified (fill_sites: 0). RELAYERING: no reachable fill hook -> all four axes NOT_APPLICABLE for all 11 labels; the verdict is an EXACT int scalar comparison (cpu.cc:84 -> reportAndCompareScalar, utilities.hpp:552-553 -> operator==), and mismatchIsFinite (utilities.hpp:174) is compile-time true for integral types, so the non-finite/BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE route (utilities.hpp:517-523) cannot fire for this benchmark. DE-CONTRADICTION: E1's own pattern_rationale describes reduced discrimination (nearly always exactly 1 component at N=512) while the machine-readable audit still carried an unqualified KEEP_CANDIDATE with no verdict class - the verdict class is therefore REDUCED (never INFORMATIVE when the notes describe reduced discrimination) and the recommendation now carries the qualifier. Weak default input diversity remains a discrimination note, not a correctness bug: no UB, no BI marker, no vacuous pass path exists here.

benchmarks.size_rationale: A(TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:85), the per-attempt zero-reset (cpu.cc:97), the generator (cpu.cc:98), and source/dest draws (cpu.cc:99-103) all scale from TEST_SIZE, so the override scales the entire input. HOWEVER sizes 0 and 1 - both in the global static size list [0,1,2,7] - are UNSAFE for this benchmark: N=1 makes 'rand() % (N - 1)' (cpu.cc:38) and effectively 'rand() % TEST_SIZE' with the dest do-while (cpu.cc:100-103) pathological - mod-by-zero UB at cpu.cc:38 and an infinite dest loop since dest==source always; N=0 underflows the size_t 'N-1' bound at cpu.cc:32 (int i compared against SIZE_MAX) -> out-of-bounds writes through the empty nodes vector, plus rand()%0 at cpu.cc:99. EFFECTIVE for N>=2; the size axis needs a per-benchmark minimum-size guard of 2.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Zero ENHANCED_FILL sites (grep-verified); pattern choice cannot alter matrix, source, or dest. benchmark_shapes.json hint (fill_sites: 0) VERIFIED CORRECT.

No ENHANCED_FILL.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Native axes exist and are clean IF connectivity policy is settled first: (a) density/diameter control while KEEPING the spanning-path connectivity guarantee (path graph -> max diameter, complete graph -> distance 1, sparse tree -> long paths) - fully compatible with current frozen semantics; (b) deliberately disconnected source/dest pairs - semantically DEFINED (unreachable = INT_MAX, exactly gradeable since the Wave 2B comparison fix, cpu.cc:116-126) but a change to the frozen input domain ('Assume the graph is connected', baseline.hpp:10), so it needs an explicit domain-policy decision, not just an adapter. Numeric-pattern-name reuse on cells remains disallowed. Adapter must also respect source != dest and N >= 2.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vectors, size_t sizing, ITERATIVE BFS oracle (baseline.hpp:16-40, queue-based, no recursion) - no stack hazard, no fixed buffers, no power-of-two requirement. Scaling caveats: O(N^2) memory (N=8192 -> ~268MB) and O(N^2) expected generator work (per-node rand()%(N-1) edge insertions, cpu.cc:37-46). std::random_shuffle (cpu.cc:30) is a C++17-removal build hazard independent of size. Only the global 4096 policy is a hard blocker. Separate from LARGE size: SMALL static sizes 0/1 are genuinely broken (see size_rationale).
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: N >= 2 only) - size axis effective for N >= 2

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - (1) exclude static sizes 0 and 1 for this benchmark (UB: size_t underflow loop cpu.cc:32 at N=0, mod-by-zero cpu.cc:38/99 and infinite dest loop cpu.cc:100-103 at N=1); (2) decide whether disconnected pairs (unreachable = INT_MAX) enter the domain
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - numeric patterns (no fill site; raw fills break {0,1}/symmetry/connectivity)

BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - connectivity-preserving diameter/density generator (path / tree / complete / Bernoulli-p plus spanning path); optionally disconnected-pair variants pending the policy decision above

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - edge-test divergence across the family (19's oracle treats any nonzero cell as an edge, baseline.hpp:32, vs ==1 in 15/16/18 and raw summation in 17); also std::random_shuffle (cpu.cc:30) is removed in C++17 - latent toolchain hazard
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - quadratic memory/generator time only; oracle BFS is iterative and safe
benchmarks.notes: Most constrained graph benchmark: connectivity invariant, source/dest scalars, a live minimum-size requirement (N >= 2), and a result-space sentinel (INT_MAX, baseline.hpp:39) that the Wave 2B exact-comparison fix (cpu.cc:116-130) made gradeable for future disconnected inputs. shapes JSON verified (fill_sites: 0). Per-attempt matrix reset (cpu.cc:97) already fixed the attempt-independence bug (audit issue #77). RELAYERING / DE-CONTRADICTION: E1's size_rationale already described sizes 0 and 1 as UB (size_t underflow OOB writes, mod-by-zero, non-terminating dest loop) while the machine-readable audit still carried an unqualified KEEP_CANDIDATE and baseline_gate_only_risk NOT_APPLICABLE; the verdict class is therefore UNKNOWN with explicit per-size conditions, baseline_gate_only_risk is 'conditional' (only the size-0/1 parameterizations fall into the gate/BI path), and the two UB cases are filed as oracle_hazards with DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - NOT as fill-site type problems, since there is no fill site at all. The INT_MAX sentinel cannot be reached by any pattern (sentinel_collision NOT_APPLICABLE); it is latent until a future adapter introduces disconnected pairs. the verdict is an EXACT int scalar comparison (cpu.cc:84 -> reportAndCompareScalar, utilities.hpp:552-553 -> operator==), and mismatchIsFinite (utilities.hpp:174) is compile-time true for integral types, so the non-finite/BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE route (utilities.hpp:517-523) cannot fire for this benchmark.

benchmarks.size_rationale: The single validate() input `image` is sized directly from TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:55, std::vector<int> image(TEST_SIZE)); the output bins are a fixed std::array<size_t,256> (cpu.cc:56) which is a histogram property, not an input dimension. The size override scales the full relevant input.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The only pattern-dependent validation input (image) is entirely ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:64); pattern choice changes every element. Caveat: extreme_values and spike_at always produce out-of-domain values at the default range and hence only ever exercise the baseline-incompatibility gate, never the candidate (see tripwires).
benchmarks.input_construction: validate(): image filled by ENHANCED_FILL(image, 0, 255) (cpu.cc:64), then BCAST (cpu.cc:65); bins zeroed via std::fill (cpu.cc:89-90). Driver-side reset() uses plain fillRand(ctx->image, 0, 255) (cpu.cc:29), which is timing-path only, not validation input.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: ASKS ONLY ABOUT THE ASSIGNMENT AT cpu.cc:64. DType is deduced from the int literals 0/255 (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and equals value_type int, so every built-in pattern assigns int->int with no narrowing and no float->int conversion: extreme_values = INT_MIN/INT_MAX (enhanced-fill.hpp:129-136 verified), spike_at = INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 (enhanced-fill.hpp:153-159), ascending/descending = the integral modulo ramp lo + position % (span+1) which stays inside [0,255] (enhanced-fill.hpp:114-120), alternating = lo/hi. value_range overrides are cast/saturated into int (enhanced-fill.hpp:299-310), also fill-safe. The ONLY conditional case at this site is explicit_values (pattern 10), whose arbitrary spec doubles pass through static_cast<int> in enhancedFromDouble (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171): a spec value outside the int range is an out-of-range float->int conversion (UB) AT THIS SITE - recorded as pattern_audit.explicit_values.fill_type_safe = "conditional". The out-of-[0,255] hazard of extreme_values/spike_at is NOT a fill-site defect: it is a DOWNSTREAM oracle/domain hazard (unchecked bins[image[i]] write, baseline.hpp:15) and is carried by domain_valid / oracle_execution_safe and oracle_hazards.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType deduced from int literals 0/255 matches value_type int, so extreme_values yields INT_MIN/INT_MAX and spike_at yields INT_MAX/2 computed natively in int - no narrowing UB. Residual caveat: explicit_values (pattern 10) converts arbitrary doubles via static_cast<int> (enhancedFromDouble, enhanced-fill.hpp:164-170), which is UB for values outside int range; that is a values-file content risk, not a site-type mismatch. value_range overrides are cast/saturated to int (enhanced-fill.hpp:299-310).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none (validate input is 100% ENHANCED_FILL; reset()'s fillRand at cpu.cc:29 is the timing path only)

domain.summary: Frozen value domain is pixel intensities in [0,255] (prompt-stated; Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-73). Oracle correctPixelCounts indexes bins[image[i]] with no bounds check (baseline.hpp:13-17), so out-of-domain input would be an out-of-bounds write in the oracle - hence the guard.
known_restrictions: Frozen value domain is pixel intensities in [0,255] (prompt-stated; Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-73). Oracle correctPixelCounts indexes bins[image[i]] with no bounds check (baseline.hpp:13-17), so out-of-domain input would be an out-of-bounds write in the oracle - hence the guard.
tripwires: cpu.cc:74-87: harnessOk scan rejects any image[j] < 0 || image[j] > 255; on failure calls mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (cpu.cc:82, BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE transport) and `continue`s the try, so the oracle never sees invalid input and the candidate is never graded on it. Fired ALWAYS by: extreme_values (INT_MIN/INT_MAX), spike_at (INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 > 255). Fired conditionally by: explicit_values with any value outside [0,255], and any value_range override extending outside [0,255]. Never fired at default range by: random, all_zeros (0), all_same (127), ascending/descending (integral modulo ramp stays in [0,255]), alternating (0,255), duplicate_at, sorted_except_one.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen input domain: image[i] in [0,255] (prompt-stated, cpu.cc:2-3 and the Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-73), enforced element-wise by the harness scan at cpu.cc:74-87 because the oracle indexes bins[image[i]] without a bounds check (baseline.hpp:15).
benchmarks.value_range_risk: value_range is applied as int (define mode: (decltype(lo)) cast; runtime mode: saturated to int per enhanced-fill.hpp:299-310), so no UB - but any range extending outside [0,255] makes random/ramp/alternating values out-of-domain and turns runs into BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE-only (candidate never graded). Ranges within [0,255] are safe and meaningful (e.g. narrow sub-band histograms).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: ASKS ONLY ABOUT THE ASSIGNMENT AT cpu.cc:62. oracle_hazards.root_cause: correctFirstLetterCounts reads s[i][0] unconditionally and writes bins[c - 'a'] on a std::array<size_t,26> with no bounds check, so an empty string or a first character outside 'a'..'z' would be an out-of-bounds write. The harness construction guarantees both invariants - length >= 2 via fillRandString(s, 2, 10) (cpu.cc:69) and the first character forced into 'a'..'z' (cpu.cc:65 rand()%26+'a', re-applied at cpu.cc:71) - and there is no ENHANCED_FILL site through which a pattern could break them, which is why no runtime guard was needed.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: No action now (unreachable). If a benchmark-native first-letter adapter is ever added, it MUST preserve the non-empty/lowercase invariant at the cpu.cc:70-72 injection point, or an ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED equivalent to the Wave-2B scans in benchmarks 20/21/24 must be added first.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: A benchmark-native first-letter-distribution adapter is technically definable without breaking validity (only s[j][0] matters to the oracle, and the cpu.cc:70-72 overwrite point is a clean injection site: e.g. all-same-letter, cyclic a..z ramp, single-letter spike, skewed distribution). But every such mapping invents NEW pattern semantics for strings outside the global numeric vocabulary - per the audit rules that makes it a policy invention, not an adapter of existing semantics. Recommended stance: keep this as the honest no-pattern-support reference case; only size is varied.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: ASKS ONLY ABOUT THE ASSIGNMENT AT cpu.cc:64. DType is deduced from the double literals 0.0/100.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and equals value_type double, so every pattern - extreme_values (-/+DBL_MAX), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2), the floating ramp, alternating and explicit_values (identity conversion, enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171) - assigns a double into a double with no conversion and no narrowing. No value_range can make this site unsafe either. The UB risk lives DOWNSTREAM in the oracle's `(int) val` cast (baseline.hpp:18) for |val| >= 2^31 and is recorded on domain_valid / oracle_execution_safe and in oracle_hazards.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType=double matches value_type double; extreme_values (+/-DBL_MAX) and spike_at (DBL_MAX/2) are representable with no conversion, so no UB at the FILL site. The UB risk lives in the ORACLE's `(int) val` cast (baseline.hpp:18), which is UB for |val| >= 2^31 - and the tripwire keeps such values from ever reaching it.

domain.summary: Frozen value domain 0 <= v < 2^31 (Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-74): below 0 the prompt's four half-open fractional intervals contain no value (negative-fraction semantics is the OPEN decision BL-08, deliberately not resolved here), and at |v| >= 2^31 the oracle's `(int) val` cast (baseline.hpp:18) is UB. NaN is out-of-domain via the negated comparison.
known_restrictions: Frozen value domain 0 <= v < 2^31 (Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-74): below 0 the prompt's four half-open fractional intervals contain no value (negative-fraction semantics is the OPEN decision BL-08, deliberately not resolved here), and at |v| >= 2^31 the oracle's `(int) val` cast (baseline.hpp:18) is UB. NaN is out-of-domain via the negated comparison.
tripwires: cpu.cc:75-88: harnessOk scan rejects any x[j] failing !(x[j] >= 0.0 && x[j] < 2147483648.0) - negated form also catches NaN; on failure calls mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (cpu.cc:83) and `continue`s -> BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE, candidate never graded on that try. Fired ALWAYS by: extreme_values (-DBL_MAX at even indices, +DBL_MAX at odd - both out), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2 ~ 8.99e307 >= 2^31). Fired conditionally by: explicit_values with negative/>=2^31/NaN values, and value_range overrides with lo < 0 or hi >= 2^31. Never fired at default range by: random, all_zeros (0), all_same (50), ascending/descending (ramp 0..100), alternating (0,100), duplicate_at, sorted_except_one.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen input domain: 0 <= x[i] < 2^31 (Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:67-74 - below 0 the prompt's four half-open fractional intervals contain no value and the semantics is the deliberately OPEN decision BL-08, and at |v| >= 2^31 the oracle's `(int) val` cast at baseline.hpp:18 is UB), enforced by the harness scan at cpu.cc:75-88 whose negated comparison also rejects NaN.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: lo/hi are doubles. value_range with lo >= 0 and hi < 2^31 is safe AND genuinely useful - ranges far wider than the default 0..100 (e.g. up to ~2.1e9) stay in the frozen domain and stress float precision of fractional-part extraction at large magnitudes. lo < 0 or hi >= 2^31 turns all runs BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE. NaN cannot arise from range overrides.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: correctCountQuartiles computes frac = val - (int) val; the `(int) val` cast is an out-of-range floating->integral conversion (UB) whenever |val| >= 2^31, which +/-DBL_MAX always is. The values are finite, so this is genuine UB and not an IEEE non-finite artefact.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: A bool-native adapter is methodically derivable without inventing numeric-on-structure semantics: control the COUNT and POSITIONS of true bits (all-false, single-true-at-k, alternating, all-true, explicit 0/1 lists). all_zeros/alternating/duplicate_at/explicit_values(0/1) map cleanly onto that; ascending/descending/all_same/extreme_values/spike_at have no non-degenerate bool meaning and would need an explicit policy to exclude. The honest current state (no pattern support, like histogram/23's string input) is also defensible and is what benchmark_shapes.json records.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: O(n) fill, O(n) XOR reduce, heap-allocated vector<bool> plus an O(n) char shadow copy under MPI (cpu.cc:28). No fixed buffers, no int narrowing of the size (loop indices are int vs size_t TEST_SIZE - benign below 2^31), no power-of-two requirement, no complexity blowup. Only the global max_spec_size=4096 policy caps sizes.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE - size axis only: the size override is fully effective (cpu.cc:66-68 and the fill loop at cpu.cc:77-79)
NO_PATTERN_SUPPORT_RECOMMENDED - the current honest state (0 fill sites, explicit_values disabled) mirrors the histogram/23 reference case
EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE - the 2 existing non-random specs (all_same, alternating) run the benchmark's own rand()%2 generator and are exact duplicates of a random spec at the same size; they add no coverage
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - only if bool patterns are wanted: define a bool-native vocabulary (true-density / parity / position of true bits) instead of reusing the numeric pattern ids
benchmarks.notes: vector<bool> is the proxy-reference specialization; ENHANCED_FILL was presumably never applied here partly for that reason (fillRand's x[i] = val works via the proxy, but the harness template has no is_same_v<DType,bool> branch, so a retrofit would need care - bool falls into the is_integral_v branches, where fillRand's rand() % (max - min) with max-min == 1 is degenerate-but-defined: always 0). Grading is exact scalar bool equality (cpu.cc:90); because bool is integral, mismatchIsFinite() is trivially true (utilities.hpp:174-183) and NO baseline-incompatible route exists on this benchmark at all. TEST_SIZE = 0 is safe (XOR of the empty range = false, baseline.hpp:12-14) and stays graded. MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS defaults to 2 (utilities.hpp:34-36).

benchmarks.size_rationale: The single input x is sized TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:116) and fully refilled per trial by ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:125); the frozen D6 comparator even scales its tolerance with the ACTUAL length, eps_rel = 8*n*u with n = x.size() (cpu.cc:69, 139). TEST_SIZE=0: oracle returns the empty-product identity 1.0 (baseline.hpp:16) and epsRel becomes 0, so rule E demands a bit-exact 1.0 from the candidate - a graded (not BI) unpinned-empty-convention edge.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The one and only validation input is fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:125); every pattern id changes the whole input. Matches benchmark_shapes.json (1 site, n elements, explicit_values enabled).
benchmarks.input_construction: ENHANCED_FILL(x, 1.0, 100.0) per trial (cpu.cc:125) then BCAST(x, DOUBLE) (cpu.cc:126). Timed path uses fillRand(ctx->x, 1.0, 100.0) (cpu.cc:90).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the 1.0 / 100.0 double literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and equals the container value_type, so the assignment x[i] = val is a double-to-double copy for EVERY pattern, including +/-DBL_MAX (extreme_values, enhanced-fill.hpp:128-138) and DBL_MAX/2 (spike_at, enhanced-fill.hpp:152-162). No narrowing, no out-of-range floating-to-integral conversion, no assignment UB; a define-mode value_range override casts through (decltype(lo)) = double (enhanced-fill.hpp:451-454) and is lossless, and the runtime path passes doubles through unchanged (enhanced-fill.hpp:311-313). Every hazard catalogued for this benchmark is downstream of the fill (domain / oracle magnitude / verdict), not at the fill.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType deduced from the double literals equals the element type; every pattern value (including +-DBL_MAX extremes and DBL_MAX/2 spike) is representable - no narrowing, no UB. Hazards on this benchmark are all on the DOMAIN axis (overflow/underflow of the PRODUCT), not the type axis.

tripwires: Frozen D6 comparator (pareval_harness::compareProductOfInverses, cpu.cc:58-85): rule D - finite nonzero |r| < DBL_MIN -> mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() -> BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE, trial passes ungraded (cpu.cc:62-65); rule A - NaN/Inf reference -> same BI transport via shared reportAndCompareScalarImpl (utilities.hpp:517-523). Firing patterns at frozen range [1,100]: all_zeros ALWAYS fires A (0.0 input -> 1/0 = Inf -> 0*Inf = NaN reference) - a baseline-gate-only pattern; spike_at frequently fires (k even: DBL_MAX/2 factor -> product overflow -> Inf -> A; k odd: 1/(DBL_MAX/2) ~ 1.11e-308 subnormal factor -> often subnormal product -> D); extreme_values fires A only under adverse std::reduce association (two +-DBL_MAX grouped -> Inf/NaN), otherwise graded near +-1; alternating(1,100) at n in the ~309-320 window can land D (subnormal), while at n=1024 the sequential reference underflows to exactly 0.0 -> graded under rule C, not BI.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen primary domain x_i in [1,100] with zero mathematically excluded by the odd-index inversion 1/x_i (baseline.hpp:15) and frozen sizes S/M/L = 15/64/256 inside the measured product-neutrality window that ends near n ~ 308 (cpu.cc:53-56; numeric gate CLOSED per thesis/docs/benchmark-domain-table.json row 26).
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Define-mode override casts ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI to decltype(lo)=double - lossless, no saturation issue. The risk is purely domain: any range including 0 makes all_zeros-like values reachable by random fill too (1/0 -> NaN reference -> BI); ranges spanning 0 produce near-zero draws with huge inverses (overflow); wide magnitude ranges shrink the product-neutrality window well below the current sizes. Runtime mode uses the same double pass-through (enhancedRuntimeRangeValue non-integral branch, enhanced-fill.hpp:311-313).

oracle_hazards.root_cause: NOT UB (IEEE-defined): an all-zero input makes the oracle evaluate 1.0/0.0 = +Inf at the first odd index and then 0.0 * Inf = NaN in the fold, so the trusted reference is NaN and rule A converts every trial into a BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker. Zero is mathematically excluded by the odd-index inversion, so this is a domain violation surfacing as a non-evaluable reference, not an execution-safety defect.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - exclude all_zeros for 26 or freeze it explicitly as a baseline-gate-only probe; no oracle guard is needed because the frozen D6 comparator already routes it correctly.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: NOT UB (IEEE-defined): a DBL_MAX/2 factor (k even) overflows the product to Inf, and its inverse 1.11e-308 (k odd) drives the product into the subnormal range; the frozen rules A and D then make the trial non-evaluable, while the surviving finite cases grade at magnitudes where reassociation can overflow the candidate.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: Pattern-dependent AT THE SITE (this is a genuine fill-axis hazard, not a relayered downstream one). DType is deduced from the 0.0 / 100.0 DOUBLE literals (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) while the container is std::vector<int> (cpu.cc:54), so every pattern value is produced as a double and converted by the assignment x[i] = val. For values inside [0,100] - random, all_same, both ramps, alternating, duplicate_at, sorted_except_one - the conversion is defined truncation and the site is SAFE (fill_type_safe true per pattern). For extreme_values (+/-DBL_MAX), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2) and any out-of-int-range explicit_values entry it is an out-of-range floating-to-integral conversion = UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR (observed saturation to INT_MIN/INT_MAX under g++ 13.3 -O3, not guaranteed by the standard). The Wave-2B scan at cpu.cc:76-89 runs AFTER the conversion, so it is a domain gate, not a UB fix. Fix: int literals ENHANCED_FILL(x, 0, 100) -> DType = int; extremes then become INT_MIN/INT_MAX type-safely and define-mode value_range overrides saturate at the (decltype(lo)) cast (enhanced-fill.hpp:451-454) instead of invoking UB.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: THE type-unsafe site of the family: DType deduced from the DOUBLE literals, elements are int, so every pattern value is computed as double and converted at x[i] = <double>. In [0,100] that is defined truncation (random/ramps/alternating/all_same=50.0/duplicate/sorted_except_one all fine), but extreme_values (+-DBL_MAX), spike_at (DBL_MAX/2) and any out-of-int-range explicit_values line produce out-of-range double->int conversion = UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR (observed saturation to INT_MIN/INT_MAX, formally UB). The Wave-2B guard fires only AFTER this conversion - it is a domain gate, not a UB fix. Fix: int literals ENHANCED_FILL(x, 0, 100) -> DType=int -> extremes become INT_MIN/INT_MAX type-safely.

domain.summary: Frozen input domain: non-negative ints with INT_MAX excluded (Wave-2B comment, cpu.cc:66-75). INT_MAX excluded because it is simultaneously a legal odd value and the oracle's fold identity (sentinel collision); negatives excluded because the oracle's a % 2 == 1 parity treats negative odds as even (C++ -3 % 2 == -1) - an unpinned parity convention.
known_restrictions: Frozen input domain: non-negative ints with INT_MAX excluded (Wave-2B comment, cpu.cc:66-75). INT_MAX excluded because it is simultaneously a legal odd value and the oracle's fold identity (sentinel collision); negatives excluded because the oracle's a % 2 == 1 parity treats negative odds as even (C++ -3 % 2 == -1) - an unpinned parity convention.
sentinels: INT_MAX: the oracle's fold identity AND its no-odd-exists return value (baseline.hpp:15-25). 'Smallest odd is INT_MAX' and 'no odd exists' are indistinguishable - the catalogued sentinel collision, excluded from the domain by the tripwire. Related unpinned convention: all-even input -> oracle returns INT_MAX; this case is NOT excluded and gets graded.
tripwires: Wave-2B BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard (cpu.cc:76-89): scans the filled input; any x[j] < 0 or x[j] == INT_MAX -> mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (BI marker) + BCAST + continue - the trial is SKIPPED, never graded; after all trials validate returns true (baseline-gate-only). Firing patterns at the current double-typed site: extreme_values ALWAYS (post-UB saturated INT_MIN and INT_MAX both trip both conditions), spike_at ALWAYS (DBL_MAX/2 saturates to INT_MAX), explicit_values with negative/INT_MAX/out-of-range entries, and any value_range override reaching negatives or INT_MAX. Patterns 0-5,7,8 in [0,100] never fire. With the type-fixed int site: extreme_values would still always fire (INT_MIN<0, INT_MAX excluded - baseline-gate-only by domain, no longer UB), but spike_at would STOP firing (INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823: non-negative, != INT_MAX, and odd).

benchmarks.value_range_risk: HIGH at this site. Define mode casts ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI to decltype(lo) = DOUBLE (not int!), so a spec value_range beyond int range is NOT saturated at the cast - the out-of-range double->int conversion happens per element = UB (runtime mode likewise passes doubles through, enhanced-fill.hpp:311-313, then converts per element). Ranges reaching negatives or INT_MAX additionally fire the tripwire on every trial -> validate returns true with only BI markers (baseline-gate-only run). Also: fillRand's integral branch is only reached for integral DType; here random fill computes doubles in range then truncates - so even 'random' silently depends on the double DType.

The serial oracle's left-to-right inclusive_scan stays finite ({-DBL_MAX, 0} alternating, exact cancellation), so the reference is finite and the candidate IS graded. Hazard: any reassociating implementation (inherent in parallel scans; formally even std::inclusive_scan permits arbitrary association) can sum two -DBL_MAX terms -> -inf; finite reference + non-finite candidate = graded FAIL (utilities.hpp:430-438 Contract A1b case 2) - a correct-under-reals parallel scan can be unfairly failed. Also, with values at magnitude 1.8e308 the ABSOLUTE 1e-6 tolerance means only bit-exact agreement passes (ULP at DBL_MAX ~ 2e292); cancellations here happen to be exact so left-to-right candidates pass. Option B (domain extrema from lo/hi, +-100) is trivially derivable but coincides with pattern 5 (alternating). No tripwire fires (there is none). AXIS LAYERING: the fill is type-safe (doubles into a double container) and the oracle's execution is well-defined (IEEE arithmetic, and here it does not even overflow) - the entire problem lives on the verdict axis. domain_valid is 'conditional': true under Option A (the prefix-sum task is total on this input, every partial sum is exactly representable), false under Option B (the derivable call-site domain is [-100,100]). baseline_gate_only_risk stays 'conditional' because the fast-math stability probe, not the non-finite-reference path, is the route that can suppress the verdict.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: THE FAMILY'S ONE GENUINELY TYPE-UNSAFE SITE, but the unsafety is pattern-dependent, which is why the axis value is 'conditional' rather than a blanket false (the E1 entry's own conversion_notes already said 'In-range patterns ... are fine', contradicting its blanket false). DType is deduced from the lo/hi ARGUMENTS (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), and the double literals -100.0/100.0 make DType=double for a vector<float>. UNSAFE patterns - the produced double is outside float's representable range, so the assignment x[i] = <double> is an out-of-range floating conversion and formally UB ([conv.double]; in practice IEEE +-inf): extreme_values(6) (+-DBL_MAX), spike_at(9) (DBL_MAX/2), and explicit_values(10) whenever a spec value exceeds +-FLT_MAX (~3.4e38). SAFE patterns - the produced value is inside float range, so the double->float conversion is well-defined (correctly rounded): random(0), all_zeros(1), all_same(2), ascending(3), descending(4), alternating(5), duplicate_at(7), sorted_except_one(8), and in-range explicit_values. A value_range override does not help: enhancedRuntimeFill casts the override to DType=double (enhanced-fill.hpp:419-425), so the mismatch persists for every override, and an override beyond +-FLT_MAX reintroduces the UB for the ramp/alternating patterns too. FIX: write -100.0f/100.0f (or an explicit float cast) so DType=float; the extrema then become +-FLT_MAX and the spike FLT_MAX/2, all representable. This axis records ONLY the assignment/conversion - the downstream all-BI behaviour of extreme_values is on the verdict axis.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: TYPE-UNSAFE SITE: double literals -100.0/100.0 deduce DType=double for a vector<float>. extreme_values computes +-DBL_MAX and spike_at computes DBL_MAX/2, both outside float's representable range; the implicit double->float conversion on assignment x[i]=<double> is formally UB ([conv.double]) - in practice IEEE +-inf. In-range patterns (ramps, alternating, all_same, all_zeros, random) convert double->float losslessly enough and are fine. Fix: use -100.0f/100.0f so DType=float (extrema become +-FLT_MAX, spike FLT_MAX/2 - all representable).

benchmarks.input_construction: validate() line 54 vectors; ENHANCED_FILL(x, -100, 100) (line 62), BCAST INT (line 63); Wave-2B domain guard lines 72-85 (see tripwires). Oracle: reverse copy + int inclusive_scan (baseline.hpp lines 15-21). Comparison: reportAndCompareEq(correct, test) (line 95) - exact int equality.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: Int literals make DType=int (deduced from lo/hi, enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), matching vector<int>::value_type, so every pattern's produced value is an int assigned to an int: extreme_values yields INT_MIN/INT_MAX, spike_at yields INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823, all_same the exact midpoint 0, and the ramps a modulo sawtooth - all representable, no narrowing and no conversion UB AT THIS SITE. Per AXIS_FACTS A.1 this stays true even though INT_MIN/INT_MAX are domain-invalid here and would overflow the oracle: those belong to domain_valid / oracle_execution_safe. The one genuinely conditional path is explicit_values, whose enhancedFromDouble<int> performs a raw static_cast<int>(double) (enhanced-fill.hpp:163-171, 214-220) - a spec value outside int range is an out-of-range floating-to-integral conversion, i.e. UB at the assignment itself; that is a spec-validation gap, not a defect of the lo/hi literals.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: Int literals deduce DType=int; extreme_values yields INT_MIN/INT_MAX and spike_at yields INT_MAX/2 - all representable in int, no conversion UB at the fill site itself (the arithmetic hazard downstream is what the tripwire guards). Caveat: explicit_values does raw static_cast<int>(double) (enhanced-fill.hpp lines 165-171, 215-219); a spec-authored value outside int's range would be UB at conversion - a spec-validation concern, not intrinsic to this site.

domain.summary: Frozen value domain |x[i]| <= 100, documented in cpu.cc lines 65-71 (D0: keeps every partial suffix sum below 2^31 at every frozen size; outside it the oracle's int inclusive_scan is signed-overflow UB) and enforced by the guard below.
known_restrictions: Frozen value domain |x[i]| <= 100, documented in cpu.cc lines 65-71 (D0: keeps every partial suffix sum below 2^31 at every frozen size; outside it the oracle's int inclusive_scan is signed-overflow UB) and enforced by the guard below.
tripwires: Wave-2B BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard, cpu.cc lines 72-85: after each fill, every element is checked for x[j] < -100 || x[j] > 100 (lines 73-78); any violation sets harnessOk=false, calls mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (line 80, prints 'BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference' with nonce - utilities.hpp lines 363-378), broadcasts the flag, and `continue`s past the trial (lines 82-84) - the candidate is never run/graded for that trial. Fires for: extreme_values (INT_MIN/INT_MAX, always at n>=1), spike_at (INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 > 100, always), explicit_values whose cast values leave [-100,100], and any value_range override beyond +-100 combined with range-following patterns (ascending/descending/alternating/all_same/random-based 7 and the random part of 9). These patterns are baseline-gate-only here. If every trial fires, validate() returns true (line 104) with only the BI marker as signal - the runner-side BI transport, not the boolean, carries the verdict.

benchmarks.domain_note: Explicitly frozen and enforced in-source: |x[i]| <= 100, documented at cpu.cc:65-71 (invariant D0 - it keeps every partial suffix sum below 2^31 at every frozen size, outside which the oracle's int inclusive_scan is signed-overflow UB) and checked element-by-element per trial by the Wave-2B guard at cpu.cc:72-85, which diverts any violation to the baseline-incompatibility transport instead of grading.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: HIGH and silent: value_range override is cast to decltype(lo)=int; any range beyond +-100 makes range-following patterns out-of-domain -> every trial diverted to BI ('continue'), validate() returns true having graded nothing. A spec author widening the range gets no compile/runtime error, just an all-BI run. Ranges within +-100 are fully safe (suffix sums bounded by 100n << 2^31 at frozen sizes).

benchmarks.notes: The family's reference implementation of the Wave-2B frozen-domain tripwire: type-safe int fill, exact equality comparison, explicit D0 rationale in-source. The relayering makes the guard's role precise - it is what keeps oracle_execution_safe TRUE on every pattern (the oracle simply never runs on out-of-domain input), while domain_valid carries the violation and verdict_outcome_class records the consequence (NO_VERDICT_BI for extreme_values and spike_at). Contrast with scan/34, which shares the identical int-overflow exposure but has NO such guard, and where the same hazard therefore lands on oracle_execution_safe=false instead. Two additional relayering results: the per-pattern baseline_gate_only_risk for every range-following pattern is 'conditional', not false, because the benchmark's own value_range_risk finding says an override beyond +-100 sends every trial to BI; and the integral ramp is a modulo sawtooth (enhanced-fill.hpp:112-118), so the ascending/descending/sorted_except_one labels are misleading even though their grading is full-strength. Convention used in this entry: verdict_outcome_class describes the case as authored (call-site range [-100,100]), and verdict_outcome_conditions carry the spec-override branches.

This stays TRUE even for extreme_values, whose values later drive the ORACLE into signed-overflow UB - per AXIS_FACTS A.1 that downstream hazard belongs to oracle_execution_safe/domain_valid and to oracle_hazards, and must not be charged to the fill site (the E1 conversion_notes already said as much). The one conditional path is explicit_values, whose enhancedFromDouble<int> does a raw static_cast<int>(double) (enhanced-fill.hpp:163-171): a spec value outside int range is an out-of-range floating-to-integral conversion, i.e. UB at the assignment - a spec-validation gap, not a defect of the lo/hi literals.

The DOWNSTREAM arithmetic UB under extreme_values (see audit) is a domain issue, kept separate from this type axis.

There is no tripwire and no harness net (ints are always 'finite', so the non-finite-reference contract cannot catch this) - selecting extreme_values on this benchmark executes UB in the baseline itself. scan/33 got a Wave-2B guard for the identical hazard; scan/34 did not. Under extreme_values, targets in [-100,99] are never present, so 9 of 10 attempts test only the false branch - a discrimination reduction, not an invalidity.
benchmarks.input_construction: validate() builds std::vector<int> input(TEST_SIZE) via ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:63); scalar target is drawn from the input on attempt i==1 (cpu.cc:66, guaranteed-positive case) and uniformly from [-100,99] otherwise (cpu.cc:68). Oracle correctContains (baseline.hpp:13-15) is std::find.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: Both bounds are int literals, so DType=int is deduced from the arguments (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and every pattern value - INT_MIN/INT_MAX (extreme_values), INT_MAX/2 (spike_at), DType(0), the modulo ramp - is stored int->int into vector<int>: no narrowing, no float->integral conversion, no assignment UB. A spec value_range keeps DType=int (define path casts with (decltype(lo))(...), runtime path saturates in enhancedRuntimeRangeValue). The discrimination collapse that extreme_values causes downstream is a VERDICT-axis property and is recorded there, not here. explicit_values is the only fill-layer hazard at this site.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: Int literals deduce DType=int; INT_MIN/INT_MAX (extreme_values) and INT_MAX/2 (spike_at) are representable, no conversion, no UB.

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: Scalar target: rand()-based, not pattern-controlled (cpu.cc:64-69). By design patterns only affect containers; on attempt i==1 target is sampled FROM the patterned input, so the positive-containment case tracks the pattern automatically.

domain.summary: None hard: contains() is well-defined over all ints. The frozen fill range [-50,50] is deliberately nested inside the target range [-100,99] so both true and false outcomes occur naturally; patterns that leave [-100,99] entirely collapse non-i==1 attempts to the false outcome.
known_restrictions: None hard: contains() is well-defined over all ints. The frozen fill range [-50,50] is deliberately nested inside the target range [-100,99] so both true and false outcomes occur naturally; patterns that leave [-100,99] entirely collapse non-i==1 attempts to the false outcome.
sentinels: none (attempt i==1 plants a guaranteed-positive target by sampling from input, cpu.cc:66; no magic value written into the vector)
tripwires: none - no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard exists in this cpu.cc; the scalar size_t/bool comparison path (reportAndCompareScalar) has no non-finite trigger for integral results, so no pattern can produce a BI verdict here.

benchmarks.domain_note: Derivable input domain: any int - correctContains is std::find over vector<int> (baseline.hpp:13-15), so no value is out of domain; the call-site range [-50,50] (cpu.cc:63) nested inside the target range [-100,99] is a DISCRIMINATION design, not a domain restriction, which is why leaving it lands on the verdict axis (REDUCED) and never on domain_valid.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Low for correctness: any int value_range is computationally safe. Moderate for discrimination: a range disjoint from [-100,99] makes every non-i==1 attempt trivially false, leaving one positive test per validation.

benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The single vector is fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled minus the one forced 10.0 element. HOWEVER, duplicate-heavy patterns break the intended unique-argmin construction: all_zeros makes |0-pi|=pi (~3.14) < |10-pi| (~6.86) at EVERY non-forced index, so the expected answer becomes a massive tie resolved by the baseline's first-index tie-break (strict < at baseline.hpp:16) - a valid parallel candidate with a different tie-break policy fails, and the prompt ('Return the index of the value closest to PI') does not specify tie-breaking. explicit_values with a cyclic list can duplicate the minimum the same way. All other patterns (extremes, spike, ramps, alternating, all_same at midpoint 550, duplicate_at, random) keep the forced 10.0 as the unique argmin and are deterministic.
benchmarks.input_construction: validate() builds std::vector<double> input(TEST_SIZE) via ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:57), then forces input[rand()%TEST_SIZE]=10.0 (cpu.cc:58) as the intended unique closest-to-pi value (fill domain [100,1000] keeps all other diffs >=96.86 vs 6.86 for 10.0). Oracle correctFindClosestToPi (baseline.hpp:11-22) is a strict-< first-minimum argmin scan.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: Both bounds are double literals, so DType=double is deduced from the arguments (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and matches the container value_type exactly. Every pattern value is a double stored into a double: extreme_values gives lowest()/max() = -/+DBL_MAX (finite, enhanced-fill.hpp:131-132), spike_at DBL_MAX/2, explicit_values goes through enhancedFromDouble<double> which is an identity static_cast. No narrowing, no float->integral conversion, no assignment UB - and no pattern can produce a non-finite value at this site. The tie/sentinel problems that all_zeros creates are DOWNSTREAM (sentinel_collision and verdict axes) and are deliberately NOT charged to this fill site.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: Double literals deduce DType=double matching value_type; extreme_values yields +/-DBL_MAX (finite), spike_at DBL_MAX/2 - no conversion, no UB, no non-finite values from any pattern.

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: Forced sentinel write input[rand()%TEST_SIZE]=10.0 (cpu.cc:58) overwrites one pattern element per attempt at a random index.

domain.summary: Values are non-negative only: rand() yields 0..RAND_MAX (on Windows/MSVC RAND_MAX=32767), despite the prompt example containing -1 — negative elements are NEVER generated by the harness. Expected zero density ~80%. The value 0 is semantically reserved (stay-in-place marker).

sentinels: 0 is the load-bearing semantic sentinel: zero elements must remain in place while non-zeros are sorted around them. tripwires: none — no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard exists in this cpu.cc; reportAndCompareEq's non-finite path is unreachable for int, and there is no size or selftest guard. No offered pattern can fire anything because no pattern reaches the input at all.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: A benchmark-NATIVE adapter is methodically clean along the axes the task itself defines: (a) zero DENSITY (currently hard-coded ~80%, cpu.cc:29-31), (b) zero PLACEMENT (random / blocked / edges / none / all), (c) non-zero value arrangement (random / ascending / descending / one spike). None of these breaks validity or forces BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE — the oracle is total over any int vector and the exact-comparison grading stays sound for every density including 0% and 100% zeros. Some global patterns even have natural native readings (all_zeros -> all elements zero, trivially valid; ascending -> ascending non-zeros with zeros interspersed; spike_at -> one huge non-zero; extreme_values -> INT_MIN/INT_MAX non-zeros at the frozen density). What is NOT derivable mechanically is the mapping policy: which of the 11 global pattern IDs maps to which (density, placement, arrangement) combination, and what the default density is for each — that is a documented policy decision, not new numeric-on-structure semantics. Without that decision, the honest state is the current one: no pattern support.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: input is one O(n) vector; oracle collects non-zeros, sorts O(n log n), writes back (baseline.hpp:7-24). `int i` loops in fillRandWithZeroes (cpu.cc:27) and the oracle (baseline.hpp:18) cap at 2^31 — theoretical only. Coverage caveat, not a blocker: on Windows RAND_MAX=32767, so at large n the ~20% non-zero values are drawn from only 32768 distinct values (heavy duplication — harmless because the correct output is still unique). Only the global max_spec_size=4096 policy blocks >4096.

benchmarks.notes: benchmark_shapes.json entry verified correct (fill_sites 0, explicit_values disabled, 'deliberately not wrapped', cpu.cc:65-67). Zero ENHANCED_FILL sites: at the same size, choosing a different global pattern cannot change one bit of the input. Every pattern label therefore has current_technical_effect NONE and all four axes NOT_APPLICABLE, but the run itself still happens and is graded normally, so the verdict class is INFORMATIVE for all eleven labels - identical to the random one, which is precisely why the ten non-random labels are duplicates and should be excluded rather than recorded as BI or vacuous. Exact element-wise comparison is sound here because the correct output is unique (equal values are indistinguishable, zero positions are fixed). No BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard exists in this cpu.cc and none could fire: the container is int, so reportAndCompareEq's non-finite path is unreachable. The harness-vs-prompt discrepancy (no negative values are ever generated) slightly narrows what candidates are tested on. A benchmark-native adapter along (a) zero density, (b) zero placement, (c) non-zero arrangement is methodically clean and BI-free - the oracle is total over any int vector - but the pattern-ID mapping policy is a documented decision, not something derivable mechanically.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: The D4 construction is fully documented in-source (topology: per-row nnz max(2,round(0.1N)) incl. diagonal, duplicate-free; values: lattice +-[1,4], dominance formula; RHS: b=A*x_gen exact; invariants: dominance gamma=1.25, exactness <2^53). A benchmark-native adapter could pattern the FREE choices without breaking validity: x_gen profile (all_zeros/all_same/ascending within [-8,8]), off-diagonal sign/magnitude profiles within [1,4], diagonal sign profile - b is recomputed exactly afterwards, so every such variation stays domain-valid and cannot fire the tripwires. Applying numeric patterns to the COO structure (rows/columns) would be invented semantics - excluded. Requires an explicit policy decision on which free axes map to which global pattern names.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: No fixed buffers, no stack arrays, no power-of-two requirement; loop counters int in the timed path only. But beyond the global max_spec_size=4096 policy, the oracle correctSolveLinearSystem is dense O(N^3) Gaussian elimination with an O(N^2) vector<vector<double>> matrix (baseline.hpp:17,29-58), buildDominantSystem is O(N^2) (per-row std::fill of used[N], cpu.cc:111), and MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2 (utilities.hpp:35) doubles it: at N=8192 that is ~2x5.5e11 flops plus ~0.5GB dense scratch - a practical compute blocker on top of the spec policy, not a correctness blocker.
e2_actions: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE - generic ENHANCED_FILL patterns: zero fill sites, patterns are inert by construction (every non-random spec is a duplicate of the random one at the same size)
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - if pattern coverage is wanted, a D4-aware constructor adapter over the x_gen / lattice free choices is the only clean route
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - the map of global pattern names onto the D4 free axes must be frozen before any adapter
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - O(N^3) dense oracle x MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2: measure wall time before raising the 4096 cap

Grading is against the independent x_gen at tolerance 1e-3 (cpu.cc:269-277), never against the numeric oracle; the oracle correctSolveLinearSystem only serves as a finiteness selftest whose failure is routed to BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE (cpu.cc:252-267), not to the candidate. Re-layering note: because no pattern reaches the input, this benchmark has NO fill-site, domain, oracle or verdict hazard attributable to the pattern parameter - every pattern spec simply reproduces the random verdict.

benchmarks.size_rationale: All main-trial extents derive from TEST_SIZE: nVals_A = nVals_X = TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE*SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY (cpu.cc:162-163), Y buffers TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:169), square M=K=N=TEST_SIZE in both oracle and candidate calls (cpu.cc:224,227). The additional A8/I13 nonsquare probe also scales from TEST_SIZE (nsM=TEST_SIZE, nsK=TEST_SIZE/4, nsN=TEST_SIZE/2, cpu.cc:246-251). Nothing stays static.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Both main-trial value arrays are ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:185-186), but a graded input component escapes the pattern: the A8/I13 nonsquare probe's value arrays use plain fillRand (cpu.cc:263-264) yet its comparison (cpu.cc:296) can fail the candidate. So a pattern spec controls the main trials only, not all pattern-relevant value inputs of the validate() run. Index arrays are structural by frozen I5 policy (not counted against the pattern).
benchmarks.input_construction: Main trials: unique (row,column) coordinates per matrix via pareval_harness::drawUniqueCoordinates rejection sampling on rand() (cpu.cc:56-80, called 181-184; frozen I5 duplicate contract), VALUE arrays via ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:185-186), assembled and row/column-sorted into COO (cpu.cc:213-221). Nonsquare probe: same unique-coordinate draw within nsM x nsK / nsK x nsN (cpu.cc:259-262) but values via plain fillRand (cpu.cc:263-264).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the (-1.0, 1.0) DOUBLE literals at the call site (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), and the container is std::vector<double>: every value any of the eleven patterns can produce - including extreme_values' +-DBL_MAX (enhanced-fill.hpp:128-141) and spike_at's DBL_MAX/2 (enhanced-fill.hpp:152-162) - is exactly representable and is stored double->double. The fill ASSIGNMENT is therefore UB-free for all patterns. A spec value_range is cast to decltype(lo)=double (enhanced-fill.hpp:450-454), so it cannot introduce a narrowing or out-of-range float->int conversion either. Every huge-magnitude consequence of these patterns is DOWNSTREAM (domain_valid / oracle_execution_safe / verdict axes), not a fill-site defect.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: The PARTIAL gap is purely mechanical: switch the nonsquare probe's fillRand at cpu.cc:263-264 to ENHANCED_FILL with the same (-1.0, 1.0) bounds - identical semantics, no new pattern meaning needed, no validity invariant touched (index draw stays structural). Structural variation (density, topology) would be new semantics and is out of scope for this adapter.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Beyond the global 4096 spec cap: the oracle correctSpmm is O(nnz_A*nnz_X) - a full cross product of the two COO lists (baseline.hpp:19-25). nnz scales as 0.1*N^2, so oracle work is O(0.01*N^4): at N=4096 that is ~2.8e12 element pairs per trial (x MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2) - a hard practical wall well before memory does (Y is N^2 doubles = 134MB at 4096; drawUniqueCoordinates used[] is N^2 bytes). Also int loop counters over nnz (cpu.cc:213,218) overflow only past nnz=2^31 (N~146k) - not the binding constraint. No fixed buffers, no power-of-two requirement.

Same size + different pattern yields bit-identical input: the D5 constructor draws exclusively from rand(). A generic fill into A's values is impossible without severing A = L*U, i.e. without destroying the graded ground truth - so patterns are excluded by the construction itself, not merely unwired.
benchmarks.input_construction: D5 frozen validation construction pareval_harness::buildLuGroundTruth (cpu.cc:100-156): INDEPENDENT ground-truth factor pair - L unit lower triangular, band k, off-diagonal integers +-[1,4] (cpu.cc:112-119); U upper triangular, band k, off-diagonals +-[1,4], diagonal 2^e with e in [0,5] so every Doolittle division is exact (cpu.cc:121-129); A = L*U accumulated exactly in long long and emitted as duplicate-free COO of ALL band cells |i-j|<=k, including exact zeros (cpu.cc:131-155). rand()-driven; BCASTs pin root arrays (cpu.cc:228-232); assembleSortedCoo (cpu.cc:158-164, 233). No x_gen - the ground truth IS the factor pair (cpu.cc:79). Timed path (reset, cpu.cc:168-185) uses fillRand, ungraded.
benchmarks.other_input_constructors: pareval_harness::buildLuGroundTruth (rand()-driven D5 constructor, cpu.cc:100-156); luHalfBandwidth (cpu.cc:95-98); assembleSortedCoo (cpu.cc:158-164); timed-path-only fillRand (cpu.cc:169-171).
