benchmarks.adapter_notes: The D5 construction is fully documented in-source (factor topology: band k density-preserving; values: lattice +-[1,4]; pivots 2^e, e in [0,5]; invariant: A=L*U exact < 2^53, full-band duplicate-free COO). A native adapter could pattern the FREE choices - off-diagonal sign/magnitude profiles within [1,4], pivot-exponent profiles within [0,5] (all_same/ascending/extreme-of-lattice) - and recompute A exactly afterwards, preserving every invariant and the exact-division property. Patterning A's values directly, or the COO structure, would sever A=L*U or invent structure semantics - excluded. Requires a frozen policy mapping global pattern names onto these factor-lattice axes; bandwidth itself is a frozen density decision (cpu.cc:73-74) and should stay out of pattern scope.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Beyond the global 4096 spec cap: validate() holds SIX dense N^2 double arrays (L_true/U_true in the instance, cpu.cc:107-108; L_ref/U_ref/L_test/U_test, cpu.cc:215-216) = 48*N^2 bytes - 805MB at N=4096, 3.2GB at 8192; the oracle correctLuFactorize is dense O(N^3) (baseline.hpp:24-40) and the band product in buildLuGroundTruth is O(N*k^2) ~ O(0.0025*N^3), all x MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2. Compute and memory blow up together on top of the spec policy. No fixed buffers, no int narrowing on sized loops in validate, no power-of-two size requirement (only pivot VALUES are powers of two). Note the family-smallest default (64) already reflects the O(N^3) cost.
e2_actions: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE - generic ENHANCED_FILL patterns: zero fill sites, patterns inert; a direct fill into A's values would falsify the graded ground truth (A = L*U)
BENCHMARK_ADAPTER_NEEDED - a D5-aware factor-lattice adapter (sign/magnitude profiles within [1,4], pivot-exponent profiles within [0,5], A recomputed exactly) is the only clean pattern route
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - the mapping of global pattern names onto the D5 free axes must be frozen first; bandwidth is a frozen density decision and should stay out of pattern scope
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - 6x dense N^2 double buffers + O(N^3) oracle x2 attempts: measure before raising sizes toward 4096 (~800MB dense scratch there)
benchmarks.notes: benchmark_shapes.json entry (lines 444-450) verified correct: fill_sites=0, explicit_values false. Grading compares the candidate L/U against the CONSTRUCTED factors at 1e-3 (cpu.cc:269-273); the Doolittle oracle serves only as a finiteness selftest routed to BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE on failure (cpu.cc:243-258). isCooEqual (cpu.cc:47-59) exists but is unused by validate() - dead helper for this path. Re-layering note: with the pattern parameter inert, every non-random spec (the catalog records 11 non-random specs here) is a duplicate of the random spec at the same size.

benchmarks.size_rationale: The single TEST_SIZE sizes all three validate() vectors (cpu.cc:61) and is passed as N to both oracle (cpu.cc:75) and candidate (cpu.cc:78). Nothing in validate() stays static. Note the size parameter is the grid side: memory/work scale O(N^2). Static size 0 is safe (enhancedFillPattern early-returns on n==0, enhanced-fill.hpp:177-179; empty compare passes).
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The single pattern-relevant input (the NxN grid) is fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:69); matches benchmark_shapes.json (fill_sites=1, n^2 elements, lines 451-459).
benchmarks.input_construction: input filled via ENHANCED_FILL(input, 0, 2) (cpu.cc:69); test/correct are OUTPUT buffers zeroed via std::fill (cpu.cc:70-71); BCAST(input, INT) (cpu.cc:72). Oracle correctCellsXOR uses the frozen 8-neighbor Moore neighborhood counting cells literally == 1 (baseline.hpp:18-39).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the lo/hi ARGUMENTS (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), here int/int, and the container value_type is int, so every pattern value is produced and assigned int->int with no conversion at all. INT_MIN/INT_MAX (extreme_values) and INT_MAX/2 (spike_at) are representable in the target; explicit_values is the only site-level caveat (spec doubles are static_cast to int by enhancedFromDouble, enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171) and is carried as fill_type_safe='conditional' on that pattern only. No downstream consideration enters this judgement.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: int->int, no conversion. extreme_values = INT_MIN/INT_MAX and spike = INT_MAX/2 are representable, and the oracle only COUNTS ==1 neighbors (count <= 8, baseline.hpp:27-36), so no downstream overflow either. Caveat: integral fillRand is hi-EXCLUSIVE (rand() % (max-min) + min, utilities.hpp:160), so random-based patterns (0/7/9 background) draw {0,1}, while alternating writes lo/hi literally ({0,2}, enhanced-fill.hpp:197) and the integral ramp is modulo-inclusive ({0,1,2}, enhanced-fill.hpp:114-119).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none (std::fill zeroing at cpu.cc:70-71 targets output buffers only)

domain.summary: None enforced in code (no guard). Prompt declares 'NxN grids of ints' with a literal ==1 aliveness test; the oracle is a total function over int. Historical/default random distribution is {0,1} (hi-exclusive fillRand); alternating and ramp patterns inject the value 2, which the literal oracle treats as 'not a 1'.
known_restrictions: None enforced in code (no guard). Prompt declares 'NxN grids of ints' with a literal ==1 aliveness test; the oracle is a total function over int. Historical/default random distribution is {0,1} (hi-exclusive fillRand); alternating and ramp patterns inject the value 2, which the literal oracle treats as 'not a 1'.
tripwires: none (no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard in cpu.cc; the comparator's non-finite-reference tripwire cannot fire on int data)

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen domain: the prompt declares 'NxN grids of ints' and the oracle applies a literal '== 1' aliveness test (baseline.hpp:28-36), so the oracle is a total, overflow-free function of any int and the only derivable narrower domain is the call-site value set {0,1} from random draws plus the 2 injected by the inclusive ramp/alternating patterns - nothing is enforced in code.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: value_range is applied as (decltype(lo))(LITERAL), i.e. cast to int with constant-folded truncate-then-saturate (enhanced-fill.hpp:450-457; runtime mirror 289-306) - no conversion UB. Semantics: any range NOT containing 1 makes the reference all-zero for every pattern (only ==1 cells matter); wide ranges dilute the density of exact 1s toward zero, degrading discrimination. Random draws exclude hi (utilities.hpp:160) while alternating/ramp include it - inclusivity asymmetry.

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: Integral fillRand is hi-exclusive (utilities.hpp:160), so the draw is exactly {0,1} - the binary grid the prompt illustrates. At 50% density roughly C(8,1)*0.5^8 = 3.1% of interior cells have exactly one live Moore neighbour, so the reference is sparse but genuinely non-degenerate and a no-op candidate (test is pre-zeroed at cpu.cc:70) fails. The oracle only compares against 1 (baseline.hpp:28-35), so no arithmetic on element values happens at all.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - identically zero reference; useful only as a cheap degenerate-shape case, never as the sole non-random spec)
all_zeros.notes: Values stay inside the call-site [lo,hi] range and 0 is unambiguously in the binary domain. Every cell is 0, so no cell equals 1 and the reference is identically 0 (baseline.hpp:36). cpu.cc:70 pre-zeroes `test`, so a candidate that writes nothing at all is counted as a PASS. This is REDUCED, not VACUOUS_PASS: reportAndCompareEq (cpu.cc:87) does compare every index - the check happens, it just cannot discriminate.

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - identically zero reference at every N)
all_same.notes: enhancedMidValue<int>(0,2) = 1 (enhanced-fill.hpp:143-149), so every cell is alive. The minimum Moore-neighbour count in an NxN grid is 3 (corner, N>=2) and 0 for N=1, so `count == 1` is never satisfied and the reference is identically 0 for EVERY N - same degenerate outcome as all_zeros, against a pre-zeroed `test`. Note this is one of only two pattern labels used by the benchmark's 8 existing specs.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: TEST_SIZE not divisible by 3 (includes the default 512)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: The integral ramp is a modulo ramp over the span (enhanced-fill.hpp:114-119): value(i) = i % 3 over the LINEAR index. When N % 3 != 0 the phase shifts row to row, 1-cells form a non-trivial lattice and the reference has a varied, discriminating structure.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: TEST_SIZE divisible by 3
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: i = r*N + c, so N % 3 == 0 makes i % 3 == c % 3: the grid becomes column-constant. Every interior cell then sees either 3 neighbours of value 1 (c == 0 or 2 mod 3) or 2 (c == 1 mod 3), never exactly 1, so the ENTIRE interior reference is 0 (baseline.hpp:28-36) and only sparse top/bottom-row cells at columns == 1 mod 3 are 1.

ascending.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: injects the value 2, which the literal ==1 oracle treats as dead - covered by the open DOMAIN policy; avoid sizes divisible by 3)
ascending.notes: domain_valid is 'conditional' because the integral ramp is modulo-INCLUSIVE of hi and therefore injects the value 2: in-domain under the prompt's literal 'NxN grids of ints' + '==1' reading, out-of-domain under a binary-grid reading. The oracle is a pure comparison-and-count function, so no arithmetic hazard exists at any value.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: TEST_SIZE not divisible by 3 (includes the default 512)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Mirror of ascending: value(i) = (n-1-i) % 3 (enhanced-fill.hpp:106-119), same non-degenerate lattice of 1-cells.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: TEST_SIZE divisible by 3
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: N % 3 == 0 implies n = N*N is divisible by 3, so (n-1-i) % 3 depends only on c: column-constant grid, entire interior reference 0 by the same neighbour-count argument as ascending.

descending.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: injects the value 2; avoid sizes divisible by 3)
descending.notes: Same value set {0,1,2} and same domain caveat as ascending; the descending ramp is the identical structure traversed backwards.

alternating.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: the value set contains no 1, so the reference is identically zero) - or DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED if a {0,1} alternating variant is introduced
alternating.notes: alternating writes lo/hi literally (enhanced-fill.hpp:197), i.e. {0,2} at this call site - NO cell equals 1, so under the literal ==1 oracle the reference is identically 0 and a candidate that writes nothing passes (test pre-zeroed, cpu.cc:70). This is the benchmark-level 'any range not containing 1 makes the reference all-zero' rule instantiated: the pattern that would otherwise be the best domain-extreme probe is exactly the one the hi-exclusive/inclusive asymmetry ruins here.

extreme_values.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (REDUCED: deterministically all-zero reference either way)
extreme_values.notes: Option A element-type extrema (INT_MIN/INT_MAX alternating) are representable and cause no UB anywhere (oracle counts, never sums values). Reference output is deterministically ALL-ZERO (no cell equals 1), so coverage collapses to discriminating candidates that treat nonzero as alive - defined and gradeable, but weak. Under the literal ==1 prompt rule any int is arguably in-domain; under a binary-grid reading it is out-of-domain - policy call. Option B domain extrema from lo/hi ({0,2}) are trivially derivable; the alternating pattern already produces exactly them. baseline_gate_only_risk corrected to false: this benchmark has NO BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard in cpu.cc and the comparator's non-finite-reference tripwire cannot fire on int data, so there is no BI route at all - the weakness is reduced discrimination, which belongs on the verdict axis.

duplicate_at.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
duplicate_at.notes: fillRand background is {0,1} (hi-exclusive) and x[k] = x[(k+1)%n] only copies an existing in-domain value (enhanced-fill.hpp:203-206), so the case is a random binary grid with one forced duplicate - structurally equivalent to random in grading power.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: TEST_SIZE not divisible by 3 (includes the default 512)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Ascending ramp plus one adjacent swap (enhanced-fill.hpp:207-209); same non-degenerate 1-lattice as ascending, with a local defect at k.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: TEST_SIZE divisible by 3
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Column-constant ramp (see ascending) collapses the interior reference to 0 everywhere except in the immediate neighbourhood of the swapped pair.

sorted_except_one.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: injects the value 2; avoid sizes divisible by 3)
sorted_except_one.notes: Same value set and domain caveat as ascending; the swap adds a single local discontinuity that is the only structure surviving the degenerate size case.

spike_at.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (INFORMATIVE run, but the spike value is outside the nominal binary distribution)
spike_at.notes: Random {0,1} background with x[k]=INT_MAX/2 (enhanced-fill.hpp:210-213). No UB (count-based oracle). The spiked cell simply stops being a 1; effect is local to its 8-neighborhood. Defined, deterministic, gradeable; out of the nominal binary distribution but inside the literal int contract. The rest of the grid keeps the full discrimination of the random case, hence INFORMATIVE. baseline_gate_only_risk corrected to false (no BI route exists on int data at this benchmark).

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec value set contains at least one 1 and is representable in int
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Cyclic fill (enhanced-fill.hpp:214-220) of in-range ints; the ==1 oracle then produces a non-trivial reference.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec value set contains no 1
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Same mechanism as all_zeros/alternating: `count == 1` is never satisfied, the reference is identically zero and a no-op candidate passes against the pre-zeroed `test` (cpu.cc:70).

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec value outside the int range
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: enhancedFromDouble does static_cast<int>(value) (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171): an out-of-range floating->integral conversion is UB, so the produced input - and therefore the counted outcome - is not defined. This is a FILL-layer defect, recorded as fill_type_safe='conditional'.

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: E2 must validate spec value magnitudes against the int element type AND check the value set contains a 1 - specs.py currently validates neither)
explicit_values.notes: Values are arbitrary spec-supplied doubles; for this int container enhancedFromDouble static_casts them (out-of-range = UB at the fill site) and the spec layer does not validate magnitudes. The ORACLE itself stays safe for every representable int (comparison and count only), which is why oracle_execution_safe is true and the hazard sits purely on the fill axis. baseline_gate_only_risk corrected to false: no BI transport exists here.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern support is already EFFECTIVE via the single ENHANCED_FILL site; no benchmark adapter needed. If a binary-domain policy is adopted, a domain-aware extreme (write lo/hi instead of numeric_limits) equals the existing alternating pattern.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: No fixed buffers, no stack arrays, sizes are size_t, no power-of-two requirement. Cost is O(N^2) in the SIDE length N: N=4096 (spec max) is 3 x 16.8M ints (~200 MB) + BCAST; beyond that only memory/time and the global max_spec_size=4096 policy limit. One remote narrowing: fillRand's loop index is int (utilities.hpp:155), so random-based patterns break only past N^2 > 2^31 (N > 46340) - far above any plausible spec size.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: fully size- and pattern-parameterizable, type-safe at the only fill site, no tripwires - but most non-random pattern labels are REDUCED here, see below)

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decide whether non-binary injections (2 from alternating/ramp, INT_MIN/INT_MAX/INT_MAX/2 from extremes/spike) are intended discrimination under the literal ==1 oracle or should be constrained to {0,1}; extreme_values yields an all-zero reference (weak coverage) either way

EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (per-pattern, REDUCED) - all_zeros, all_same (= 1 everywhere), alternating (= {0,2}) and extreme_values each produce an identically ZERO reference under the ==1 oracle while cpu.cc:70 pre-zeroes `test`, so a candidate that writes nothing is counted as a pass; note the benchmark's 8 existing specs use only all_same and explicit_values, i.e. its entire current non-random coverage is in this degenerate set

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - specs.py validates explicit_values neither against the int element type (enhancedFromDouble static_cast, out-of-range = UB) nor against the ==1 domain (a value set without a 1 is silently degenerate); also avoid sizes divisible by 3, which make the linear ramp column-constant and zero the whole interior reference
benchmarks.notes: Default TEST_SIZE 512 differs from the rest of the family (1024). Wave-2B comments record full-vector grading incl. boundary ring (cpu.cc:81-85) and the frozen Moore-neighborhood oracle (baseline.hpp:19-24). Deterministic patterns (1-6,10) repeat the identical input across all MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS trials. Layer summary: the single fill site is unconditionally type-safe (int->int), the oracle is total and overflow-free for every int, no BI/gate route exists at all, and the entire risk of this benchmark sits on the VERDICT axis (all-zero references from the four degenerate labels) plus the open domain policy for non-binary values.

benchmarks.size_rationale: TEST_SIZE sizes all three vectors (cpu.cc:65) and is passed to oracle (cpu.cc:101) and candidate (cpu.cc:104); the in-domain guard scans input.size() (cpu.cc:86), so it scales too. Nothing static.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Single input grid fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:73); matches benchmark_shapes.json (fill_sites=1, lines 460-468). Two of the eleven offered patterns are neutralized by the domain guard (see tripwires) - a domain-coverage limitation, not a pattern-plumbing one.
benchmarks.input_construction: input via ENHANCED_FILL(input, 0, 255) (cpu.cc:73); test/correct zeroed (cpu.cc:74-75); BCAST (cpu.cc:76). Wave-2B in-domain scan of input over [0,255] BEFORE the oracle runs (cpu.cc:85-98). Oracle: 3x3 edge kernel, int sum, clip to [0,255] (baseline.hpp:22-46).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType deduced from the int lo/hi arguments equals the container value_type, so every produced value is assigned int->int with no conversion. INT_MIN/INT_MAX and INT_MAX/2 are representable in the target. The oracle's overflow exposure and the [0,255] guard are downstream facts and are recorded on oracle_execution_safe / domain_valid / the verdict axis, not here. explicit_values is the only site-level caveat (static_cast of arbitrary spec doubles) and is carried as fill_type_safe='conditional' on that pattern.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: int->int, no conversion UB. The oracle's int sum with coefficient 8 would overflow (UB) on INT_MIN/INT_MAX pixels, but the Wave-2B guard (cpu.cc:86-98) rejects out-of-[0,255] input before correctConvolveKernel runs, so no UB is reachable from any offered pattern - they become BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE instead. Integral fillRand is hi-exclusive: random draws are [0,254], while alternating/ramp include 255.

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none

domain.summary: [0,255] grayscale, ENFORCED: Wave-2B scan (cpu.cc:86-91) - any element <0 or >255 emits the BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE non_finite_reference marker via mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (cpu.cc:93; utilities.hpp:363-378) and skips the trial (continue, cpu.cc:97). The candidate is never graded on out-of-domain input.
known_restrictions: [0,255] grayscale, ENFORCED: Wave-2B scan (cpu.cc:86-91) - any element <0 or >255 emits the BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE non_finite_reference marker via mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() (cpu.cc:93; utilities.hpp:363-378) and skips the trial (continue, cpu.cc:97). The candidate is never graded on out-of-domain input.
sentinels: none (the 0/255 clip in the oracle output is saturation, not a sentinel)
tripwires: cpu.cc:85-98: in-domain [0,255] input scan -> BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker + trial skip. Fires ALWAYS for extreme_values (INT_MIN/INT_MAX) and spike_at (INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 > 255) - these two are baseline-gate-only patterns here (they can never grade the candidate). Also fires for explicit_values or a spec value_range outside [0,255]. In-domain patterns (all_zeros, all_same=127, ascending/descending, alternating 0/255, duplicate_at, sorted_except_one, random) never fire it. Note: with a deterministic always-firing pattern, EVERY trial is skipped and validate() still returns true (cpu.cc:96-97,117) - run classification then rests entirely on the gate parsing the nonce-carrying BI marker.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen and CODE-ENFORCED domain: grayscale pixels in [0,255] - cpu.cc:85-98 scans the filled input and routes anything outside it to the BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE transport (mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference, utilities.hpp:363-378) before correctConvolveKernel is ever called, which is also what keeps the oracle's int accumulation (max |sum| = 4080) overflow-free.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Usable value_range is hard-capped to a subset of [0,255]: anything outside deterministically converts the whole validation into BI-only skipped trials. The int cast itself saturates (no UB). Within-domain asymmetry: random draws exclude hi (0..hi-1) while alternating/ramp include hi.

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: Hi-exclusive integral fillRand draws [0,254], comfortably inside the enforced [0,255] domain, so the guard never fires. |sum| <= 8*255 + 8*255 = 4080 is far from INT_MAX, so the oracle is arithmetically safe. The reference is varied (both clip branches and the pass-through branch are exercised), a no-op candidate fails.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - identically zero reference)
all_zeros.notes: Every tap is 0, so sum == 0 at every cell and the reference is identically 0 (baseline.hpp:37-43). cpu.cc:74 pre-zeroes `test`, so a candidate that writes nothing is counted as a pass. REDUCED, not VACUOUS_PASS - reportAndCompareEq (cpu.cc:108) still compares every index.

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - the interior reference is constant 0; it grades essentially only the zero-padding boundary rule)
all_same.notes: enhancedMidValue<int>(0,255) = 127. The kernel's coefficients sum to zero, so every INTERIOR cell gives 8*127 - 8*127 = 0; only the border ring keeps a residue (edge 3*127 = 381, corner 5*127 = 635, both clipped to 255 by baseline.hpp:39-40). The reference is therefore 0 inside and 255 on the ring: it does grade the out-of-image zero-padding rule (which Wave-2B added), but carries no interior information at all.

ascending.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: a linear ramp is in the null space of this zero-sum kernel)
ascending.notes: The integral ramp is value(i) = i % 256 over the linear index (span 255, enhanced-fill.hpp:114-119) - locally linear. With a symmetric tap set whose coefficients sum to zero (8 at the centre, -1 at the 8 neighbours), the response to any locally linear field is exactly 0: away from the modulo-256 wrap the interior reference is 0 (and at a wrap column it is -768 -> clipped to 0, or +768 -> clipped to 255). At the default TEST_SIZE = 1024 the ramp is additionally column-periodic (1024 % 256 == 0, so value depends only on c % 256), leaving non-zero interior output on just 4 of 1024 columns. Grading power is dominated by the border ring and the sparse wrap stripes.

descending.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: mirror of ascending, same null-space collapse)
descending.notes: Mirror of ascending (position = n-1-i, enhanced-fill.hpp:106-107); identical local linearity, identical zero interior response away from the modulo-256 wrap positions.

alternating.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: the reference equals the input, so an identity-copy candidate passes on every cell)
alternating.notes: alternating writes lo/hi literally, i.e. exactly {0, 255} - the domain extremes, fully in-domain, guard never fires. But the clipping makes the case degenerate: for a 0-cell the sum is at most -1020 (clipped to 0) and for a 255-cell at least +1020 (clipped to 255), on the border ring as well as in the interior. The reference is therefore BIT-IDENTICAL to the input, so `imageOut = imageIn` passes every index. Strongest reduced-discrimination case of this benchmark.

extreme_values.notes: Option A element extrema (INT_MIN/INT_MAX) deterministically trip the [0,255] guard on every trial: BI-only, zero grading value; the guard is what keeps the pattern UB-free (unguarded, the oracle's sum += pixel * 8 would be signed-overflow UB, per the Wave-2B comment cpu.cc:78-84). Option B domain extrema derived from lo/hi ({0,255}) are derivable, in-domain, and graded - the alternating pattern already produces exactly them. oracle_execution_safe is TRUE precisely because the guard (cpu.cc:85-98) returns before correctConvolveKernel is ever called on this input - the frozen oracle never executes on it. Explicitly NOT a vacuous pass: validate() does return true at cpu.cc:117 after skipping every trial and the driver prints 'Validation: PASS', but run_binary:512-514 classifies the run baseline_incompatible from the authenticated marker BEFORE parse_authenticated_validation, and precompute_gates would already have recorded the spec as baseline_incompatible so the model never runs (process_sample:657-670).

duplicate_at.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
duplicate_at.notes: Random [0,254] background with one copied neighbour value (enhanced-fill.hpp:203-206): in-domain, guard never fires, grading power equivalent to random.

sorted_except_one.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: ramp null-space collapse with a single local defect)
sorted_except_one.notes: Ascending ramp plus one adjacent swap (enhanced-fill.hpp:207-209): the null-space argument of ascending applies everywhere except the immediate neighbourhood of the swapped pair, which is the only extra structure the pattern contributes.

spike_at.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE pending EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS)
spike_at.notes: INT_MAX/2 spike always exceeds 255 -> guard fires every trial -> BI-only, candidate never graded. A domain-scaled spike (value within [0,255], e.g. hi) is not derivable from the current numeric_limits-based spike semantics (enhanced-fill.hpp:152-158). Same runner path as extreme_values: the BI marker outranks the driver's 'Validation: PASS', so this is NO_VERDICT_BI and not a vacuous pass.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: all spec values inside [0,255]
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Guard passes (cpu.cc:86-91), the oracle runs, the candidate is graded normally; a constant or locally linear value set degrades to REDUCED by the same null-space argument as all_same/ascending.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: any spec value outside [0,255] but representable in int
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: cpu.cc:86-98 fires mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() and skips every trial; run_binary:512-514 then classifies the run baseline_incompatible.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: any spec value outside the int range
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: enhancedFromDouble does static_cast<int>(value) (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171) - out-of-range floating->integral conversion is UB at the FILL site, so the produced input is undefined before the guard ever sees it.

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: E2 must validate value magnitudes against the int element type and against the enforced [0,255] domain - specs.py currently validates neither)
explicit_values.notes: Values are arbitrary spec-supplied doubles; for this int container enhancedFromDouble static_casts them (out-of-range = UB at the fill site), and the spec layer does not validate magnitudes. oracle_execution_safe stays true for every in-int value because the [0,255] guard keeps the oracle from running on anything it cannot sum safely.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Patterns already act natively on the pixel grid. The only gap is policy-level: a domain-aware extreme/spike mapping (extremes at lo/hi; spike within [lo,hi]) would restore those two patterns from BI-only to graded - a harness/spec policy change, not a benchmark adapter.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: No fixed buffers/narrowing; O(N^2) memory and O(9*N^2) work in side length N. N=4096: ~200 MB across three int vectors. Only the global 4096 spec cap blocks larger sides (fillRand int-index bound only past N > 46340).
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: clean size/pattern plumbing and the cpu.cc:85-98 guard makes every offered pattern UB-free - at the price of turning two of them into BI-only runs)

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - extreme_values and spike_at are deterministically BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE-only at this site (cpu.cc:85-98); either exclude them for this benchmark or introduce domain-aware extreme/spike variants ({0,255} / in-range spike)

EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (per-pattern, REDUCED) - the edge kernel's coefficients sum to zero, so locally linear input has zero response: ascending/descending/sorted_except_one leave the interior reference 0 except at the modulo-256 wrap positions, all_same leaves it constant 0, all_zeros makes it identically 0, and alternating makes the reference BIT-IDENTICAL to the input so an identity-copy candidate passes everywhere. All six pattern labels used by the benchmark's 12 existing specs (all_same, all_zeros, alternating, ascending, descending, explicit_values) fall in this reduced set

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - specs.py validates explicit_values magnitudes neither against the int element type (enhancedFromDouble static_cast) nor against the enforced [0,255] domain, so an out-of-domain value set silently degrades a spec to BI-only runs
benchmarks.notes: This is the family's reference implementation of the frozen-domain tripwire: out-of-domain harness input is announced via the BI transport and never grades the candidate (cpu.cc:78-84). reportAndCompareEq is called WITH the input vector (cpu.cc:108) so mismatch feedback includes input values. Layer summary: fill site unconditionally type-safe; oracle execution safe for every reachable input BECAUSE of the guard; the guard moves extreme_values/spike_at onto the verdict axis as NO_VERDICT_BI (never a vacuous pass, run_binary:512-514); the dominant residual problem is REDUCED discrimination across the in-domain deterministic patterns.

benchmarks.size_rationale: TEST_SIZE sizes all three 1D vectors (cpu.cc:54); oracle (cpu.cc:68) and candidate (cpu.cc:71) take the vectors themselves (size implied). Nothing static. Size 0 is safe (empty fill/compare; the oracle's input.size()-1 underflow at line 19 of baseline.hpp is unreachable because the size-0 loop never runs).
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Single 1D input fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:62); matches benchmark_shapes.json (fill_sites=1, n elements, lines 469-477).
benchmarks.input_construction: input via ENHANCED_FILL(input, -100.0, 100.0) (cpu.cc:62); test/correct zeroed (cpu.cc:63-64); BCAST DOUBLE (cpu.cc:65). Oracle: 3-point average with zero boundary padding, double accumulation (baseline.hpp:13-25). Full-vector grading incl. both boundary elements, tolerance 1e-4 (cpu.cc:74-81).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType deduced from the double lo/hi arguments equals the container value_type: every pattern value, including +-DBL_MAX (extreme_values), DBL_MAX/2 (spike_at) and any spec double (explicit_values via enhancedFromDouble), is assigned double->double with no conversion and no representability question. The IEEE overflow that +-DBL_MAX later causes happens inside the ORACLE and is recorded on oracle_execution_safe / the verdict axis, not here.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: double->double, no conversion. extreme_values (+-DBL_MAX) overflows to +-inf inside the ORACLE's 3-term sum - IEEE-defined (not UB), but it produces non-finite reference values (see audits).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none

domain.summary: No explicit guard. Frozen numeric range [-100.0,100.0] via lo/hi; implicit finite-double domain: a non-finite ORACLE output at a graded index is skipped and emits the BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE non_finite_reference marker (utilities.hpp:422-428, called from reportAndCompare at cpu.cc:81).
known_restrictions: No explicit guard. Frozen numeric range [-100.0,100.0] via lo/hi; implicit finite-double domain: a non-finite ORACLE output at a graded index is skipped and emits the BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE non_finite_reference marker (utilities.hpp:422-428, called from reportAndCompare at cpu.cc:81).
tripwires: No guard in cpu.cc itself; the comparator-level non-finite-REFERENCE tripwire (utilities.hpp:425-428) is the active one. extreme_values fires it at essentially every interior index (see audit); spike_at does NOT fire it (all outputs stay finite). A finite-reference/non-finite-candidate index is a hard FAIL, not BI (utilities.hpp:430-438).

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen domain: finite doubles from the call-site range [-100.0, 100.0] (cpu.cc:62) with no guard in cpu.cc - the only active boundary is the comparator's non-finite-REFERENCE rule (utilities.hpp:423-428), plus the derivable magnitude ceiling implied by the absolute 1e-4 tolerance (|values| beyond ~1e12 make one ULP exceed the epsilon).
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Range literals are cast to double (no-op). Widening the range raises two distinct risks: (a) |lo|,|hi| > DBL_MAX/2 makes alternating/extreme-style sums overflow to inf -> BI-dominated runs; (b) far earlier, the ABSOLUTE 1e-4 tolerance falls below one ULP once |values| exceed ~1e12, silently turning grading bit-exact and failing rounding-equivalent candidates. Default [-100,100] keeps ULP ~1.4e-14 << 1e-4.

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: Uniform draws inside the frozen [-100,100] range; at |values| <= 100 one ULP is ~1.4e-14, far below the absolute 1e-4 tolerance (cpu.cc:81), so reassociation and divide-vs-multiply differences are all absorbed - no false-fail and no parallel bias. Reference is fully varied.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - identically zero reference)
all_zeros.notes: All sums are 0.0, so the reference is identically 0.0 and `test` is already zeroed at cpu.cc:63 - a candidate that writes nothing is counted as a pass. REDUCED, not VACUOUS_PASS: reportAndCompare (cpu.cc:81) compares every index, the check simply cannot fail.

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - collapses onto all_zeros at this symmetric range)
all_same.notes: enhancedMidValue<double>(-100,100) = -100 + 200/2 = 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:143-149), so all_same is BIT-IDENTICAL to all_zeros at this call site: identically zero reference against a pre-zeroed `test`. Any symmetric value_range reproduces the collapse; a non-symmetric range would give a constant c with reference c on the interior and 2c/3 at the two ends.

ascending.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: only the 2 boundary indices discriminate)
ascending.notes: The floating ramp is exactly linear, x[i] = a*i + b (enhanced-fill.hpp:108-113), and a 3-point average reproduces a linear function exactly: interior reference == input, to well inside the 1e-4 tolerance. Only output[0] = (x[0]+x[1])/3 and output[N-1] = (x[N-2]+x[N-1])/3 differ from the input, so an `output = input` candidate - and any candidate whose interior stencil preserves linear functions, e.g. a 5-point average - fails on just 2 of N indices.

descending.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: mirror of ascending)
descending.notes: Mirror of ascending (position = n-1-i): same exact linearity, same interior identity, same 2 discriminating indices.

alternating.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
alternating.notes: Writes the domain extremes -100/+100 literally. Interior reference is -x[i]/3 = -/+33.33 (the two neighbours are both -x[i]) and the two ends are exactly 0.0, so the reference is genuinely different from the input and separates a 3-point average from other symmetric stencils (a 5-point average would give x[i]/5 here). Magnitudes stay ~100, so the absolute tolerance keeps ~10 orders of headroom.

extreme_values.notes: Option A extrema alternate -DBL_MAX/+DBL_MAX by index parity. Every interior 3-term sum contains two same-sign DBL_MAX terms -> +-inf (IEEE overflow, defined) -> non-finite reference at ALL interior indices: each is skipped and the BI marker is emitted; only the two boundary elements (where DBL_MAX + (-DBL_MAX) = 0 exactly) are actually graded. Effectively BI-dominated: ~2 of N indices graded, run classified baseline-incompatible at gate level. Option B domain extrema (+-100) are derivable from lo/hi and safe - alternating already provides them. oracle_execution_safe is TRUE: IEEE overflow to infinity is defined behaviour, not UB (the consequence is purely on the verdict axis). The counted outcome is baseline_incompatible either through precompute_gates' oracle-only probe (run_enhanced_tests.py:596-620, model never runs) or through run_binary:512-514; it is NOT a vacuous pass, and no reordering hazard exists at the two graded ends (their two terms cancel exactly in any order).

duplicate_at.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
duplicate_at.notes: Random [-100,100] background with one copied neighbour value: in-domain, finite, grading power equivalent to random.

sorted_except_one.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: ramp identity with one local defect)
sorted_except_one.notes: Ascending ramp plus one adjacent swap: the interior-identity argument of ascending holds everywhere except the ~4 indices touched by the swap, which together with the 2 boundary indices are the only discriminating positions.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the fast-math stability probe diverges from the normal oracle at spike magnitude (expected: one ULP at |x| ~ 1.5e307 is ~1.8e291, astronomically above the 1e-4 tolerance)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: precompute_gates runs a second oracle instance compiled with perturbed FP flags and requires it to still validate (run_enhanced_tests.py:596-618). A divergence stores gate 'numerically_unstable', and process_sample:657-670 then records the spec with that status and NEVER runs the model - no candidate verdict is produced. This is the gate sibling of BI, not BI itself.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the stability probe passes and the model is run
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: cpu.cc:81 grades with an ABSOLUTE tolerance of 1e-4 while one ULP at the spike neighbourhood (~DBL_MAX/6) is ~1.8e291: a mathematically equivalent candidate that writes x*(1.0/3.0) instead of x/3.0 mismatches at the 3 spike-adjacent indices and is FAILED.

spike_at.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (plus a tolerance policy: an absolute epsilon cannot grade large-magnitude patterns)
spike_at.notes: Random [-100,100] background + x[k]=DBL_MAX/2. No overflow (DBL_MAX/2 + ~200 < DBL_MAX): references near the spike are ~DBL_MAX/6, finite, no BI. Out of the frozen [-100,100] range but fully defined - domain_valid is 'conditional' because the benchmark carries two readings of its domain (the lo/hi range, under which the spike is out; the implicit finite-double domain, under which it is in). GRADING HAZARD from the ABSOLUTE tolerance (std::abs(a-b) > 1e-4, utilities.hpp:209 semantics via cpu.cc:81): at magnitude ~1.5e307 one ULP is ~1.8e291, so a mathematically equivalent candidate that rounds differently (e.g. x*(1.0/3.0) instead of x/3.0) fails at the 3 spike-adjacent indices while passing on the default range. Summation ORDER is harmless here (the small terms are absorbed below half-ULP in any order), which is why parallel_bias_risk is false - the divide-vs-multiply rounding split hits serial and parallel candidates equally. baseline_gate_only_risk is 'conditional' for the GATE route only (numerically_unstable), never for BI: all references are finite so the non-finite tripwire cannot fire.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec values of ordinary magnitude and not all equal / not linear
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Cyclic double fill (enhanced-fill.hpp:214-220) with no conversion; the oracle and the 1e-4 tolerance behave exactly as for random.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: constant or linear spec value sets
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Same mechanisms as all_same/ascending: a constant collapses the interior, a linear sequence is reproduced exactly by the 3-point average.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec values large enough that one ULP exceeds 1e-4 (|value| > ~1e12) or that the 3-term sum overflows to infinity
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: The tolerance cliff turns grading bit-exact (FALSE_FAIL_RISK) and, past ~DBL_MAX/3, the oracle output becomes non-finite -> the comparator's non-finite-reference rule (utilities.hpp:423-428) makes the run NO_VERDICT_BI; which of the two fires is a pure spec-value question that specs.py does not check.

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: E2 must validate spec value magnitudes against the frozen [-100,100] range and against the absolute 1e-4 tolerance - specs.py currently validates neither)
explicit_values.notes: The container here is double, so enhancedFromDouble is an identity conversion and the fill is unconditionally type-safe - the generic 'int container static_cast' caveat of the family does NOT apply at this site. The residual risk is entirely domain/tolerance-shaped: magnitudes above ~1e12 make the absolute epsilon smaller than one ULP, and magnitudes near DBL_MAX make the oracle output non-finite.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow to +-infinity in the oracle's 3-term sum when two same-sign +-DBL_MAX terms are added - DEFINED behaviour, explicitly not UB - producing a non-finite reference at every interior index, which the comparator skips while emitting the BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - adopt domain-scaled extremes (+-100 from lo/hi, already produced by alternating) or exclude extreme_values for this benchmark; no oracle guard is required because nothing undefined happens.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Grading hazard, not an execution hazard: the oracle runs cleanly and returns finite values ~DBL_MAX/6, but cpu.cc:81 grades them against an ABSOLUTE epsilon of 1e-4 while one ULP at that magnitude is ~1.8e291, so rounding-equivalent implementations are separated.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - either scale the spike into [lo,hi] or adopt a relative/mixed tolerance for large-magnitude patterns; expect the fast-math stability gate to intercept the spec as numerically_unstable in the meantime.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Patterns act natively on the numeric 1D input; no adapter needed. Domain-scaled extreme/spike variants would avoid the BI/tolerance issues.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: 1D linear scaling: 3 double vectors of N (N=4096 -> ~100 KB). No fixed buffers, no narrowing (fillRand int index only matters past N > 2^31). Only the global 4096 spec policy blocks larger N; the benchmark itself would run at millions of elements trivially.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: cleanest of the family - 1D, linear cost, type-safe double site - but its ramp and constant patterns are strongly REDUCED)

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - extreme_values is BI-dominated (inf references at all interior indices); spike_at is defined but the absolute 1e-4 tolerance demands near-bit-exactness at spike magnitude: decide domain-scaled extremes/spike or a relative-tolerance policy for large-magnitude patterns

EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (per-pattern, REDUCED) - all_same collapses onto all_zeros (the midpoint of a symmetric range is 0.0) and both leave an identically zero reference against a pre-zeroed `test`; ascending/descending/sorted_except_one are exactly linear and a 3-point average reproduces a linear function, so only the 2 boundary indices discriminate

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - specs.py validates explicit_values magnitudes neither against the frozen [-100,100] range nor against the absolute 1e-4 tolerance; note also that the benchmark's 7 existing specs use only explicit_values and extreme_values, i.e. one unvalidated label and one BI-dominated label
benchmarks.notes: Wave-2B comment (cpu.cc:74-79) confirms full-vector grading incl. boundaries with the historical 1e-4 tolerance. Comparator role-awareness: non-finite reference -> per-index skip + BI; non-finite candidate under finite reference -> FAIL. Layer summary: the fill site is unconditionally type-safe (double->double) and the oracle NEVER executes UB (IEEE overflow is defined), so this benchmark has no fill-layer and no oracle-layer defect at all; everything sits on the verdict axis - NO_VERDICT_BI for extreme_values, a gate/tolerance question for spike_at, REDUCED for the linear and constant patterns.

benchmarks.size_rationale: TEST_SIZE sizes all three N^2 vectors (cpu.cc:57) and is passed as N to oracle (cpu.cc:71) and candidate (cpu.cc:74). Nothing static. O(N^2) memory in doubles: N=4096 -> 3 x 134 MB = ~400 MB.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Single grid input fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:65); matches benchmark_shapes.json (fill_sites=1, n^2 elements, lines 478-486).
benchmarks.input_construction: input via ENHANCED_FILL(input, -100.0, 100.0) (cpu.cc:65); test/correct zeroed (cpu.cc:66-67); BCAST DOUBLE (cpu.cc:68). Oracle: 5-point average, zero padding, double accumulation (baseline.hpp:14-34). Full-grid grading incl. border ring, tolerance 1e-6 (cpu.cc:77-84).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType deduced from the double lo/hi arguments equals the container value_type, so every pattern value - +-DBL_MAX, DBL_MAX/2, arbitrary spec doubles - is assigned double->double with no conversion and no representability question. The subsequent IEEE overflow in the oracle's 5-term sum is a downstream, DEFINED event and is recorded on the verdict axis and in oracle_hazards, never here.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: double->double, no conversion. extreme_values (+-DBL_MAX) overflows to +-inf in the oracle's 5-term sums - IEEE-defined, produces non-finite references (see audits).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none

domain.summary: No explicit guard. Frozen range [-100.0,100.0] via lo/hi; implicit finite-double domain via the comparator's non-finite-reference rule (utilities.hpp:422-428, reached from reportAndCompare at cpu.cc:84).
known_restrictions: No explicit guard. Frozen range [-100.0,100.0] via lo/hi; implicit finite-double domain via the comparator's non-finite-reference rule (utilities.hpp:422-428, reached from reportAndCompare at cpu.cc:84).
tripwires: No guard in cpu.cc; active tripwire is the comparator-level non-finite-REFERENCE skip + BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker (utilities.hpp:425-428). extreme_values fires it across the whole interior (see audit); spike_at stays finite and does not fire it.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen domain: finite doubles from the call-site range [-100.0, 100.0] (cpu.cc:65) with no guard in cpu.cc - the only active boundary is the comparator's non-finite-REFERENCE rule (utilities.hpp:423-428), plus the derivable magnitude ceiling implied by the absolute 1e-6 tolerance (|values| beyond ~1e10 make one ULP exceed the epsilon).
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Same two-tier risk as 52: (a) ranges near DBL_MAX make oracle sums overflow -> BI-dominated; (b) the ABSOLUTE 1e-6 tolerance drops below one ULP once |values| exceed ~1e10, making wide value_ranges grade effectively bit-exact and failing rounding-equivalent implementations. Default [-100,100] is comfortable.

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: Uniform draws inside the frozen [-100,100] range; at |values| <= 100 one ULP is ~1.4e-14 against the absolute 1e-6 tolerance (cpu.cc:84), so reassociation across omp/mpi is absorbed with ~8 orders of headroom. Fully varied reference.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - identically zero reference)
all_zeros.notes: All sums are 0.0, the reference is identically 0.0 and `test` is pre-zeroed at cpu.cc:66, so a candidate that writes nothing is counted as a pass. REDUCED, not VACUOUS_PASS: reportAndCompare (cpu.cc:84) compares every one of the N^2 indices.

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - collapses onto all_zeros at this symmetric range)
all_same.notes: enhancedMidValue<double>(-100,100) = 0.0, so all_same is BIT-IDENTICAL to all_zeros here: identically zero reference against a pre-zeroed `test`. all_same is one of the four pattern labels used by the benchmark's 7 existing specs.

ascending.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: only the border ring discriminates)
ascending.notes: The floating ramp is exactly linear in the LINEAR index, x[i] = a*i + b, and the 5-point average reproduces a linear function exactly ((x[i-N] + x[i+N] + x[i-1] + x[i+1] + x[i])/5 = x[i] because the offsets cancel pairwise). The interior reference therefore equals the input to well within the 1e-6 tolerance, and only the 4N-4 border cells discriminate: an `output = input` candidate, or any candidate whose interior stencil preserves linear functions, fails only on the ring. ascending is one of the four labels used by the existing specs.

descending.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: mirror of ascending)
descending.notes: Mirror of ascending (position = n-1-i): same exact linearity, same interior identity, same border-ring-only discrimination.

alternating.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
alternating.notes: Writes the domain extremes -100/+100 by LINEAR index parity. For even N the vertical neighbours share the centre's parity, giving an interior reference of x[i]/5 = +-20; for odd N the pattern is a true checkerboard and the interior reference is -3*x[i]/5 = -/+60. Either way the reference differs from the input and separates the 5-point stencil from other symmetric stencils. Magnitudes stay ~100, so the 1e-6 absolute tolerance keeps ample headroom.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: residual graded set (the border ring), if a domain-scaled variant or a changed classification ever let a verdict be counted
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: On the finite border cells the oracle's value depends on ITS summation order (corner = +-DBL_MAX/5 only because baseline.hpp:18-31 adds the opposite-sign term before the second same-sign one); a candidate that reassociates the same 3-5 terms can legitimately overflow to inf and is then FAILED by the finite-reference/non-finite-candidate rule (utilities.hpp:430-438). This condition does not change the counted outcome today, which is baseline_incompatible.

extreme_values.notes: Extrema alternate by LINEAR index parity; in row-major with even N the vertical neighbors (+-N) share the center's parity, so every interior 5-term sum hits same-sign DBL_MAX pairs -> +-inf references over the entire interior -> per-index BI skips, BI-dominated run; only the border ring (where signs interleave to finite values, e.g. corners = +-DBL_MAX/5) is graded. (For odd N the two vertical neighbours are instead both of the OPPOSITE sign to the centre, which still gives a same-sign pair and the same infinite interior, so the conclusion does not depend on N parity.) Extra hazard on those graded border cells: the finite oracle value depends on ITS summation order - a candidate summing the same 3-5 terms in a different order can legitimately overflow to inf (e.g. corner: (-M + -M) before +M) and then FAILS under the finite-reference/non-finite-candidate rule (utilities.hpp:430-438). So extreme_values is simultaneously BI-dominated and order-unfair on the residual graded set. Option B domain extremes (+-100) derivable from lo/hi; alternating provides them safely. oracle_execution_safe is TRUE: IEEE overflow is defined, not UB. parallel_bias_risk is true because that reassociation hazard is exactly what distinguishes vectorised/omp/mpi candidates from a serial one - it is currently MASKED by the run being classified baseline_incompatible (precompute_gates' oracle-only probe already fails, so the model never runs), but it would become a counted false-fail the moment a domain-scaled extreme variant is adopted without a tolerance/role rule.

duplicate_at.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
duplicate_at.notes: Random [-100,100] background with one copied neighbour value: in-domain, finite, grading power equivalent to random.

sorted_except_one.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: ramp identity with one local defect)
sorted_except_one.notes: Ascending ramp plus one adjacent swap: the interior-identity argument of ascending holds everywhere except the handful of cells whose 5-point neighbourhood touches the swapped pair; those cells plus the border ring are the only discriminating positions.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the fast-math stability probe diverges from the normal oracle at spike magnitude (expected: one ULP at |x| ~ 1.8e307 is ~1.8e291, astronomically above the 1e-6 tolerance)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: precompute_gates requires a perturbed-FP oracle instance to still validate against the normal one (run_enhanced_tests.py:596-618); a divergence stores gate 'numerically_unstable' and process_sample:657-670 records the spec with that status without ever running the model.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the stability probe passes and the model is run
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: cpu.cc:84 grades with an ABSOLUTE epsilon of 1e-6 while one ULP in the spike neighbourhood (~DBL_MAX/10) is ~1.8e291: a candidate writing sum*0.2 instead of sum/5.0 mismatches at the 5 spike-adjacent cells and is FAILED.

spike_at.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (plus a tolerance policy: an absolute epsilon cannot grade large-magnitude patterns)
spike_at.notes: One DBL_MAX/2 spike over [-100,100] background: all references finite (spike neighborhood ~DBL_MAX/10), no BI. Out of frozen range but defined - domain_valid is 'conditional' because the benchmark carries two readings of its domain (the lo/hi range, under which the spike is out; the implicit finite-double domain, under which it is in). Same absolute-tolerance hazard as 52, sharper here: eps=1e-6 (cpu.cc:84) vs one ULP ~1.8e291 at spike magnitude - divide-by-5 vs multiply-by-0.2 rounding splits mathematically equivalent candidates into FAIL at the 5 spike-adjacent cells. parallel_bias_risk is false: the four small neighbours are absorbed below half an ULP of the spike in ANY summation order, so reassociation is not what separates candidates - the divide-vs-multiply choice is, and it is orthogonal to the execution model. baseline_gate_only_risk is 'conditional' for the numerically_unstable GATE route only; the BI route cannot fire because every reference is finite.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec values of ordinary magnitude, neither constant nor linear in the linear index
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Cyclic double fill (enhanced-fill.hpp:214-220) with no conversion; the oracle and the 1e-6 tolerance behave exactly as for random.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: constant or linear spec value sets, or a cycle length that divides the row length
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Constants collapse the interior (all_same argument) and linear sequences are reproduced exactly by the 5-point average (ascending argument); a cycle aligned with N makes the grid column-constant, which reduces the interior to a 1D problem.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec values large enough that one ULP exceeds 1e-6 (|value| > ~1e10) or that the 5-term sum overflows to infinity
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: The tolerance cliff turns grading bit-exact (FALSE_FAIL_RISK) and, past ~DBL_MAX/5, the oracle output becomes non-finite -> comparator non-finite-reference rule -> NO_VERDICT_BI; specs.py checks neither.

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: E2 must validate spec value magnitudes against the frozen [-100,100] range and against the absolute 1e-6 tolerance - specs.py currently validates neither)
explicit_values.notes: The container here is double, so enhancedFromDouble is an identity conversion and the fill is unconditionally type-safe - the family's generic 'int container static_cast' caveat does NOT apply at this site. Residual risk is domain/tolerance-shaped only: the 1e-6 epsilon drops below one ULP already at |values| ~ 1e10.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: IEEE overflow to +-infinity in the oracle's 5-term sum whenever two same-sign +-DBL_MAX terms meet - DEFINED behaviour, explicitly not UB - producing non-finite references across the whole interior, which the comparator skips while emitting the BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE marker.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - adopt domain-scaled extremes (+-100 from lo/hi, already produced by alternating) or exclude extreme_values; no oracle guard is required because nothing undefined happens.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Order-unfairness on the residual graded border ring: the oracle's own accumulation order (baseline.hpp:18-31) keeps corner/edge sums finite, while a candidate that reassociates the same 3-5 terms may overflow to infinity and is then FAILED under the finite-reference/non-finite-candidate rule. This biases against vectorised/omp/mpi candidates.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - if a domain-scaled extreme variant is ever adopted, decide a role/tolerance rule for reassociation-induced non-finite candidates before the ring becomes gradeable; today the whole run is classified baseline_incompatible, which masks this.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Grading hazard, not an execution hazard: the oracle runs cleanly and returns finite values ~DBL_MAX/10, but cpu.cc:84 grades them against an ABSOLUTE epsilon of 1e-6 while one ULP at that magnitude is ~1.8e291, separating rounding-equivalent implementations.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - scale the spike into [lo,hi] or adopt a relative/mixed tolerance for large-magnitude patterns; expect the fast-math stability gate to intercept the spec as numerically_unstable in the meantime.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Patterns act natively on the numeric grid; no adapter needed. Domain-scaled extreme/spike variants would remove the BI and order-fairness issues.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: No fixed buffers/narrowing; size_t throughout. Cost is O(N^2) in doubles - the heaviest of the family (N=4096 -> ~400 MB, N=8192 would be ~1.5 GB) - but nothing in the source blocks side lengths beyond 4096; only the global spec cap does. fillRand int-index bound only past N > 46340.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: clean plumbing and a type-safe double site, but the linear and constant patterns are strongly REDUCED and extreme_values yields no verdict)

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - extreme_values is BI-dominated AND order-unfair on the residual graded border cells; spike_at defined but absolute 1e-6 tolerance forces near-bit-exactness at spike magnitude; decide domain-scaled variants or relative-tolerance policy

EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (per-pattern, REDUCED) - all_zeros and all_same (midpoint 0.0) leave an identically zero reference against a pre-zeroed `test`; ascending/descending/sorted_except_one are exactly reproduced by the 5-point average on the interior, so only the 4N-4 border cells discriminate. Three of the four labels used by the benchmark's 7 existing specs (all_same, ascending, extreme_values) are in the reduced or no-verdict set
LARGE_SIZE_PROBE_NEEDED - memory probe advisable before granting sizes above 4096 (double N^2 x 3 vectors + BCAST)

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - decide a role/tolerance rule for reassociation-induced non-finite CANDIDATE values before any domain-scaled extreme variant makes the border ring gradeable (utilities.hpp:430-438); this is the family's only genuinely parallel-biased hazard
benchmarks.notes: Wave-2B comment (cpu.cc:77-82) confirms full-grid grading incl. border ring at the historical 1e-6 tolerance. The parity interaction between the linear-index extreme pattern and row-major 2D adjacency (even N: vertical neighbors same parity) is what makes extreme_values overflow here even though each single value is representable. Layer summary: no fill-layer defect (double->double) and no oracle-layer UB (IEEE overflow is defined); the risks are NO_VERDICT_BI (extreme_values), a gate/tolerance question (spike_at) and REDUCED discrimination (the linear and constant patterns).

benchmarks.size_rationale: TEST_SIZE sizes all three vectors (cpu.cc:67) and is passed as N to oracle (cpu.cc:81) and candidate (cpu.cc:84). Nothing static. O(N^2) ints.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Single grid input fully ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:75); matches benchmark_shapes.json (fill_sites=1, lines 487-495).
benchmarks.input_construction: input via ENHANCED_FILL(input, 0, 2) (cpu.cc:75); test/correct zeroed (cpu.cc:76-77); BCAST INT (cpu.cc:78). Oracle sums the RAW values of the 8 Moore neighbors into an int (baseline.hpp:27-51) and applies the ==1 alive test plus sum thresholds (baseline.hpp:52-66); frozen dead-outside-grid boundary, full-grid grading (cpu.cc:87-95).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: CORRECTED from the previous type_safe=false, which encoded a DOWNSTREAM oracle hazard at the fill layer. DType is deduced from the int lo/hi arguments and equals the container value_type, so every pattern value - including INT_MIN/INT_MAX from extreme_values and INT_MAX/2 from spike_at - is produced and assigned int->int with no conversion and full representability: the fill assignment itself has no UB. The real defect (the unguarded oracle summing raw INT_MIN/INT_MAX neighbours, signed-overflow UB) now lives on oracle_execution_safe for extreme_values and in oracle_hazards, and the E2 action is ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED, not FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES. explicit_values keeps a genuine fill-layer caveat (static_cast of arbitrary spec doubles into int) and is carried as fill_type_safe='conditional' on that pattern only.
fill_sites.conversion_notes: The fill ASSIGNMENT is int->int (no conversion UB) for every offered pattern. Downstream (recorded on the oracle axis, not here): the UNGUARDED oracle sums raw neighbor values into int (baseline.hpp:27-51), so extreme_values' INT_MIN/INT_MAX cells overflow - e.g. the two vertical neighbors share the extreme pattern's index parity for even N (and same-sign pairs exist for odd N via the diagonals), so sum += INT_MIN twice is signed-overflow UB. Unlike sibling 51 there is no in-domain scan in cpu.cc. Random-based patterns draw {0,1} (hi-exclusive fillRand, utilities.hpp:160); alternating/ramp inject the value 2 (defined, see domain).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none

domain.summary: Prompt freezes cells to {0,1} ('A cell is 1 if it is alive and 0 if it is dead') but NOTHING is enforced in code - no 51-style guard. Out-of-{0,1} values are semantically arbitrary under this oracle: a cell of value 2 is treated as DEAD by the ==1 test yet counts as TWO live neighbors in the raw sum - deterministic, but not Game-of-Life semantics, and it diverges from the equally reasonable count-neighbors-==1 reading (which sibling 50's oracle uses).
known_restrictions: Prompt freezes cells to {0,1} ('A cell is 1 if it is alive and 0 if it is dead') but NOTHING is enforced in code - no 51-style guard. Out-of-{0,1} values are semantically arbitrary under this oracle: a cell of value 2 is treated as DEAD by the ==1 test yet counts as TWO live neighbors in the raw sum - deterministic, but not Game-of-Life semantics, and it diverges from the equally reasonable count-neighbors-==1 reading (which sibling 50's oracle uses).
tripwires: none - and notably MISSING: cpu.cc has no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard although its oracle has exactly the overflow exposure 51 guarded against. extreme_values therefore produces unguarded signed-overflow UB in the ORACLE (grading process), not a clean BI classification. The comparator's non-finite tripwire cannot fire on int data.

benchmarks.domain_note: Frozen domain: cells in {0,1} - the prompt states 'A cell is 1 if it is alive and 0 if it is dead' (cpu.cc:3, baseline.hpp:5) - but NOTHING enforces it in cpu.cc, so any value the fill produces reaches the oracle, where a non-binary cell is simultaneously treated as dead (== 1 test) and counted by its raw magnitude in the neighbour sum.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Casts saturate (no conversion UB), but semantics degrade fast: any range beyond {0,1} makes the oracle grade candidates on its arbitrary raw-sum treatment of non-binary cells (e.g. ascending/descending ramps over [0,2] mix 1s and 2s, where a count-alive-neighbors candidate diverges from the raw-sum oracle); ranges with |values| > ~INT_MAX/8 re-expose the unguarded overflow UB. Note the current default lo/hi (0,2) already put 2s in play for alternating/ramp - only the random patterns stay binary (hi-exclusive).

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: Hi-exclusive integral fillRand draws exactly {0,1} (utilities.hpp:160) - the prompt's frozen binary domain - so the raw-value neighbour sum coincides with the live-neighbour count and the oracle is genuine Game of Life. Sum <= 8, no overflow. The reference is varied and a no-op candidate fails.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: REDUCED - identically zero reference)
all_zeros.notes: Every cell dead with sum 0: the dead branch needs sum == 3 (baseline.hpp:61-65), so the reference is identically 0 and `test` is pre-zeroed at cpu.cc:76 - a candidate that writes nothing is counted as a pass. REDUCED, not VACUOUS_PASS: reportAndCompareEq (cpu.cc:95) compares every index.

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: only the 4 corner cells of the reference are non-zero)
all_same.notes: enhancedMidValue<int>(0,2) = 1, so every cell is alive and in-domain. Neighbour sums are 8 (interior), 5 (edge) and 3 (corner), so under baseline.hpp:52-59 only the four CORNERS survive: the reference is 0 on all N^2-4 other cells. A candidate that writes nothing fails on exactly 4 indices out of N^2 (4 of 1048576 at the default size), which is the weakest discrimination in the family. Note 9 of the benchmark's existing specs use only all_same and explicit_values.

ascending.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED + FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW (the graded semantics on value-2 cells are not specified by the prompt)
ascending.notes: The integral ramp is modulo-INCLUSIVE of hi, so values cycle {0,1,2} and the pattern leaves the prompt-frozen {0,1} domain (domain_valid=false; nothing enforces it, unlike sibling 51). Arithmetic is safe (max sum 8*2 = 16). The verdict hazard is semantic: a cell of value 2 is treated as DEAD by the ==1 test yet contributes TWO to the raw neighbour sum (baseline.hpp:29-51), so a candidate implementing the equally reasonable 'count neighbours == 1' reading - the reading sibling 50's oracle uses - is FAILED on input the prompt never defines. That is a false fail against the specified domain, not a discrimination win.

descending.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED + FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW
descending.notes: Mirror of ascending: same {0,1,2} value set, same out-of-{0,1} domain violation, same unspecified raw-sum semantics on value-2 cells.

alternating.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (REDUCED: identically zero reference) + DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (injects the out-of-domain value 2)
alternating.notes: alternating writes lo/hi literally, i.e. {0,2}: no cell equals 1, so every cell takes the dead branch, and every neighbour sum is even and therefore never 3 - the reference is identically 0 for every N, against a pre-zeroed `test`. Out-of-domain (value 2) but, unusually for this benchmark, NOT a false-fail case: the 'count neighbours == 1' reading also yields an all-zero grid, so both semantics agree. The problem here is purely reduced discrimination.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the signed overflow is compiled to wrapping arithmetic and both oracle and candidate wrap identically
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: The run would be counted as an ordinary pass/fail, but the compared semantics are undefined by the C++ standard, so the verdict carries no defensible meaning - this is NOT a vacuous pass (the comparison at cpu.cc:95 does happen) and NOT a BI case (no marker exists).

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the candidate is vectorised / OpenMP-parallel and the compiler exploits the UB differently on the two sides
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: -O3 may fold or reassociate the oracle's and the candidate's overflowing int sums differently (baseline.hpp:29-51 vs generated-code.hpp), producing a mismatch that has nothing to do with candidate correctness.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the build enables a signed-overflow sanitizer or trapping arithmetic
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: The oracle-only probe in precompute_gates would abort and the spec would be recorded baseline_incompatible - but that depends on build flags, not on the source as it stands.

extreme_values.recommendation_for_e2: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED (EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE until a {0,1} in-domain guard exists) + DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED
extreme_values.notes: HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING of the family, now correctly layered: the FILL is type-safe (int->int), the ORACLE is not. Option A element extrema (INT_MIN/INT_MAX alternating by linear index) feed the oracle's raw 8-neighbor int sum: for any N >= 3 same-parity neighbor pairs exist (even N: vertical neighbors; odd N: diagonals), so INT_MIN+INT_MIN / INT_MAX+INT_MAX overflows - undefined behavior in correctGameOfLife (baseline.hpp:27-51) with NO guard and no BI transport. Needs a 51-style in-domain scan ({0,1}) or per-benchmark exclusion of extreme_values before this pattern is ever offered. Option B domain extrema from lo/hi ({0,2}) avoid overflow but still inject the out-of-domain value 2. baseline_gate_only_risk corrected to FALSE: there is no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE guard in cpu.cc and the comparator's non-finite tripwire cannot fire on int data, so nothing routes this case to the BI path - the run proceeds on undefined arithmetic, which is strictly worse than a BI-only run and must not be recorded as a gate risk.

duplicate_at.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
duplicate_at.notes: fillRand background is {0,1} (hi-exclusive) and x[k] = x[(k+1)%n] only copies an existing in-domain value, so the grid stays binary: genuine Game of Life semantics, grading power equivalent to random.

sorted_except_one.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED + FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW
sorted_except_one.notes: Ascending ramp plus one adjacent swap: the {0,1,2} value set carries the same out-of-domain violation and the same unspecified raw-sum treatment of value-2 cells as ascending.

spike_at.recommendation_for_e2: DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE pending EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS)
spike_at.notes: Single INT_MAX/2 spike over a {0,1} random background: each neighbor sum contains at most one spike, so max sum = INT_MAX/2 + 7 - no overflow, fully defined (oracle_execution_safe true). The spiked cell is treated as dead (==1 false); its 8 neighbors get sum >= INT_MAX/2 != 3, so their outputs are deterministically 0. Out of the frozen {0,1} domain; discriminates candidates that use nonzero-as-alive or bool conversion - and since such a candidate is CORRECT on the domain the prompt actually specifies, that discrimination is a false fail, which is why the verdict class is FALSE_FAIL_RISK and the policy question (EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS) has to answer it. baseline_gate_only_risk corrected to false: no BI transport exists at this benchmark.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec value set is a subset of {0,1}
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: In-domain binary grid, oracle semantics are genuine Game of Life, sums <= 8; the case behaves like a deterministic random grid (REDUCED if the set is all-0 or all-1, by the all_zeros/all_same arguments).

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: spec values outside {0,1} but with |value| <= INT_MAX/8
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: Same mechanism as ascending: the raw-sum oracle (baseline.hpp:29-51) grades candidates on semantics the prompt never defines for non-binary cells.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: any |value| > INT_MAX/8 (or an out-of-int-range spec double)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: The unguarded 8-neighbour int sum overflows - the same signed-overflow UB as extreme_values, at baseline.hpp:29-51; an out-of-int-range double additionally makes the FILL conversion UB at enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171. specs.py validates neither magnitude.

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED + DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED (conditional: E2 must validate spec value magnitudes against the int element type, against the {0,1} domain, and against the oracle's INT_MAX/8 accumulation bound - specs.py validates none of the three)
explicit_values.notes: Values are arbitrary spec-supplied doubles; for this int container enhancedFromDouble static_casts them (out-of-range = UB at the fill site), and the spec layer does not validate magnitudes. Uniquely in this family, explicit_values here can also reach the ORACLE hazard: any |value| above INT_MAX/8 reproduces extreme_values' unguarded signed overflow, which is why oracle_execution_safe is 'conditional' rather than true.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: correctGameOfLife accumulates the RAW values of the 8 Moore neighbours into an `int` with no domain guard; extreme_values writes INT_MIN/INT_MAX by linear index parity and for every N >= 3 same-sign neighbour pairs exist (even N: the two vertical neighbours; odd N: the diagonals), so INT_MIN+INT_MIN / INT_MAX+INT_MAX is signed-overflow UB inside the ORACLE itself. Sibling 51 guards exactly this hazard class at cpu.cc:85-98; 54 does not.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - add a 51-style {0,1} in-domain scan in cpu.cc that calls mismatchNoteNonFiniteReference() and skips the trial, or exclude extreme_values for this benchmark, BEFORE the pattern is offered. This is an oracle/harness-layer fix; the fill site needs no change.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: The same unguarded 8-neighbour int accumulation is reachable from explicit_values whenever a spec value exceeds INT_MAX/8 in magnitude; specs.py validates neither the magnitude nor the {0,1} domain.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED - the same {0,1} in-domain guard covers this path; additionally add spec-layer magnitude validation against the int element type and the accumulation bound.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern plumbing is already EFFECTIVE; what is needed is protective, not adaptive: a {0,1} in-domain guard (51-style BI transport) or per-benchmark pattern exclusion for extreme_values, plus a domain policy for the value 2.

Explicitly an oracle-layer action: the fill site is int->int and type-safe, so FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES is the wrong layer for this defect

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED - decide whether value-2 injections (alternating and the ramps under lo/hi = 0/2, plus the INT_MAX/2 spike) are acceptable given the oracle's non-GoL raw-sum semantics on them; the prompt freezes the domain to {0,1} while the call site's hi=2 puts 2 in play for every inclusive pattern

FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW - on non-binary input the frozen oracle (raw-value neighbor sum + ==1 alive test) diverges from the count-neighbors-==1 reading used by sibling 50; candidates are then graded against semantics the prompt never specifies, which makes ascending/descending/sorted_except_one/spike_at FALSE_FAIL_RISK rather than extra coverage

EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (per-pattern, REDUCED) - all_same (midpoint = 1) makes every cell alive, which under the frozen rules leaves exactly the 4 CORNERS alive and zeroes all N^2-4 other cells; all_zeros and alternating give an identically zero reference against a pre-zeroed `test`. The benchmark's 9 existing specs use only all_same and explicit_values
benchmarks.notes: Contrast within the family: 51 guards its overflow-exposed int oracle, 54 does not, despite the identical hazard class. 50's oracle (pure ==1 counting) is total and overflow-free, which is why the same int fill site is safe there but not here. Layer summary after normalization: the fill site is unconditionally type-safe (previously mis-recorded as type_safe=false); the ORACLE is the unsafe layer for extreme_values (signed-overflow UB, oracle_execution_safe=false) and conditionally for explicit_values; there is NO BI/gate route anywhere in this benchmark, so every baseline_gate_only_risk is false and the residual risks are FALSE_FAIL_RISK (non-binary injections) and REDUCED (the three all-but-zero reference patterns).

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the lo/hi ARGUMENTS (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174) and here equals the container value_type, so every pattern value is assigned double->double with no conversion at all: extreme_values writes +-DBL_MAX (enhanced-fill.hpp:129-133), spike_at writes DBL_MAX/2 (enhanced-fill.hpp:153-156), all exactly representable. explicit_values goes through enhancedFromDouble<double> (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171), which is the identity for a double target, so even arbitrary spec values are fill-safe here; whether such a value is USEFUL is a domain/oracle question and is judged on those axes, not on this one.

Writing 0.0 is perfectly type-safe; that it is the singular point of 1-1/x is a DOMAIN/oracle-output matter and is recorded on those axes and in oracle_hazards, not here.
