domain.summary: Implicit x != 0: the operation is 1 - 1/x (baseline.hpp:11). The frozen continuous fillRand(-50.0,50.0) draw hits exact 0.0 with probability ~0, but deterministic patterns hit it: (a) all_zeros fills the ENTIRE vector with 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:185); (b) all_same fills the ENTIRE vector with the midpoint of [-50,50] = exactly 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:148,188); (c) ascending/descending and sorted_except_one use the float ramp lo+(hi-lo)*(pos/(n-1)) (enhanced-fill.hpp:113) which is exactly 0.0 whenever pos/(n-1) is exactly 0.5 in binary - true at offered static size 7 (pos=3, 3/6=0.5) and at n=1025 (512/1024), NOT at the default 1024 (would need pos=511.5). At x=0.0: 1/0.0=+inf, result -inf - IEEE-defined, not UB, but the comparator std::abs(x-y)>eps (utilities.hpp:491) is NaN-absorbing: (-inf)-(-inf)=NaN which compares 'equal', so a candidate producing NaN (or any non-finite value) at those indices silently PASSES against the baseline's -inf. Singular inputs therefore degrade the oracle's discriminative power rather than crashing.

benchmarks.domain_note: The oracle 1.0 - 1.0/x (baseline.hpp:10-12) carries an implicit domain x != 0: at exactly 0.0 it yields -inf, which is IEEE-defined and never UB but makes the reference non-finite; the frozen sampling range is [-50.0, 50.0] (cpu.cc:26,55).
benchmarks.value_range_risk: High relative to family: any value_range spanning 0 preserves the all_same midpoint-zero hazard and (size-dependent) ramp-zero hazard; all_zeros ignores value_range entirely and is ALWAYS the singular input. A positive-only range (e.g. [1,100]) fixes all_same/ramp but not all_zeros.

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: fillRand computes (rand()/(double)RAND_MAX) * 100 - 50 (utilities.hpp:152-168). Exactly 0.0 requires rand() == RAND_MAX/2, which is not an integer for the odd RAND_MAX (2147483647), so the singularity is not reachable on the random grid; the smallest attainable magnitude is about 2.3e-8, giving |1-1/x| <= about 4.3e7 whose ulp (about 7.5e-9) stays far below the ABSOLUTE tolerance 1e-5 (cpu.cc:68). Reference finite everywhere, every index graded. No sentinels exist on this benchmark, so sentinel_collision is false rather than UNKNOWN on every row.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (it can never produce a model verdict under the current runner) or DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED if x=0 is to be declared in-spec
all_zeros.notes: all_zeros writes DType(0) = 0.0 into EVERY element (enhanced-fill.hpp:184-186), so the reference is 1.0 - 1.0/0.0 = -inf at every index. That is IEEE-defined, never UB, so oracle_execution_safe stays TRUE. But reportAndCompareSelectedWith checks the reference first, skips every non-finite reference index and emits the authenticated marker BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference (utilities.hpp:425-426), and run_binary classifies the run baseline_incompatible BEFORE parse_authenticated_validation ever reads the driver's Validation: PASS line (run_enhanced_tests.py:512-514); the oracle-only gate (precompute_gates:538-620) already records non_finite_reference and the model never runs (process_sample:657-670). CORRECTION: E1 called this a silent pass through a NaN-absorbing comparator - that is wrong for the current enhanced stage; it is a no-verdict/BI case, not a vacuous pass. This also corrects the generic E1 row note that 'values stay within the call-site [lo,hi] range', which said nothing about the singularity the same catalog documented at benchmark level.

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (identical to all_zeros at the frozen range; no verdict possible) or DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED
all_same.notes: enhancedMidValue = lo + (hi-lo)/2 = -50.0 + 50.0 = exactly 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:144-149), so all_same ACCIDENTALLY produces the fully singular input as well - the same -inf reference at every index and the same BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE route (utilities.hpp:425-426). A value_range whose midpoint is non-zero would make this pattern usable again; all_zeros would still be singular because it ignores lo/hi entirely.

extreme_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: hazard-free but weakly discriminative - the whole reference collapses to the constant 1.0)
extreme_values.notes: Option A extrema +-DBL_MAX: 1 - 1/(+-DBL_MAX) rounds to exactly 1.0 for BOTH extremes (1/DBL_MAX is about 5.6e-309, far below the ulp of 1.0) - finite, well-conditioned, exact-comparable. Ironically extreme_values is one of the SAFEST patterns here; the hazardous ones are all_zeros/all_same (whole-vector singularity) and the ramp patterns at specific sizes. The price of that safety is discrimination: the reference is the constant 1.0 at every index, so a candidate that simply returns 1.0 everywhere passes - hence REDUCED rather than INFORMATIVE. Option B domain extrema (-50/50) derivable but not needed.

The real exposure is the x=0 singularity and the absolute-tolerance cliff, both of which are domain/oracle-output questions. sentinel_collision is false, not UNKNOWN: no sentinels are defined.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: 1.0 - 1.0/0.0 = -inf at every index. IEEE-defined, NOT undefined behaviour (oracle_execution_safe stays true), but a non-finite reference is skipped and the authenticated BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference marker fires, so the run is recorded baseline_incompatible and the model gets no verdict.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE for this benchmark, or resolve the x=0 domain policy first; all_zeros ignores value_range, so no range setting can rescue it.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: enhancedMidValue(-50.0, 50.0) is exactly 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:144-149), so all_same silently reproduces the fully singular all_zeros input and the same -inf reference.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE at the frozen range, or require a value_range whose midpoint is non-zero.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: The float ramp lo + (hi-lo)*(position/(n-1)) is exactly 0.0 whenever position/(n-1) is exactly 0.5 in binary - true at the offered static size 7 (3/6) and at n = 1025 (512/1024), not at the default 1024. One such index makes the reference non-finite and triggers the process-wide BI marker.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED or per-size spec audit: exclude the ramp patterns at sizes whose ramp crosses exactly 0.0 (n = 7 is already in static_base_sizes, specs.py:134).

oracle_hazards.root_cause: A spec value of exactly 0.0 (or a non-finite value) produces a non-finite reference; specs.py validates the value count and numeric type but never the values themselves.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED: reject 0.0 and non-finite explicit values for this benchmark in specs.py.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern effect already EFFECTIVE; the open question is domain policy, not adapter design.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vector, O(n); no structural blockers. Only max_spec_size=4096. (Note the ramp-zero hazard is size-dependent: sizes with (n-1) a power of two, e.g. 1025 or 4097, put exact 0.0 in ascending/descending/sorted_except_one inputs.)
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional): only random, alternating, duplicate_at, spike_at and extreme_values are unconditionally verdict-producing; extreme_values is additionally weakly discriminative (constant 1.0 reference).

DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED: decide handling of the x=0 singularity - either exclude all_zeros and all_same (and audit the ramp patterns per size: the offered static size 7 hits exact 0.0) or declare IEEE totalization in-spec. CORRECTED MECHANISM: under the current runner a singular index does NOT slip through a NaN-absorbing comparator - the non-finite reference is skipped, BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference is emitted (utilities.hpp:425-426), and run_binary classifies the run baseline_incompatible before the driver's Validation line is parsed (run_enhanced_tests.py:512-514), so the case yields NO model verdict at all.

ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED: reject explicit_values containing 0.0 or non-finite values, and consider bounding tiny magnitudes - cpu.cc:68 grades with an ABSOLUTE tolerance of 1e-5, so a reference of magnitude above about 1e11 turns single-ulp formulation differences into failures.
FURTHER_SEMANTIC_REVIEW: confirm whether the thesis wants 'x=0 out of spec' (the prompt example has no zero) or 'IEEE totalization in-spec'.

SPEC_POLICY (size axis, family-wide): size 0 is an accepted spec size for every non-k pattern (specs.py:134,289-292 vs 321-323); the graded set is then empty and the run is counted as a PASS with nothing compared (utilities.hpp:412-465).
benchmarks.notes: extreme_values and spike_at are hazard-free (extreme_values only weakly discriminative); the family-atypical risk is that the two constant patterns (all_zeros, all_same) both produce the fully singular input, all_same doing so accidentally via the exact midpoint of the frozen [-50,50] range, and that the three ramp-derived patterns do so at specific sizes. Carried over from the dropped E1 fields: value_range risk is HIGH relative to the family - any range spanning 0 preserves the all_same midpoint-zero hazard and the size-dependent ramp-zero hazard, while all_zeros ignores value_range entirely and is ALWAYS singular; a positive-only range (e.g. [1,100]) fixes all_same and the ramps but not all_zeros. Large sizes are blocked only by max_spec_size = 4096 (specs.py:138), with the caveat that sizes with (n-1) a power of two (1025, 4097, ...) put an exact 0.0 into the ramp patterns.

benchmarks.size_rationale: Single validate() input vector<int> input(TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:54); results are copies (cpu.cc:59,63). Fully scaled.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: Single ENHANCED_FILL-controlled input (cpu.cc:55); matches shapes hint. But two offered patterns make the ORACLE itself UB (below).
benchmarks.input_construction: validate(): vector<int> input(TEST_SIZE) at cpu.cc:54, ENHANCED_FILL(input, -50, 50) at cpu.cc:55, BCAST at cpu.cc:56. Perf path: fillRand(ctx->x, -50, 50) at cpu.cc:26.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the int lo/hi arguments (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), so patterns 0-9 assign int to int: INT_MIN, INT_MAX and INT_MAX/2 are all int-representable and the ASSIGNMENT is unconditionally safe - the signed-overflow problem those values cause is created later, by the oracle's x[i]*x[i], and is recorded on oracle_execution_safe and in oracle_hazards, never here. The site is 'conditional' solely because pattern 10 converts arbitrary spec doubles with static_cast<int> (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171), which is UB outside the int range and is magnitude-unvalidated (specs.py:328-367).
fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType=int matches value_type; INT_MIN/INT_MAX/INT_MAX/2 all int-representable, so no conversion UB AT THE FILL SITE. The UB risk is downstream in compute (see extreme_values/spike_at audits). explicit_values caveat as for 56: double->int static_cast (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171) is UB for out-of-int-range values; specs.py does not bound magnitudes.

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none

domain.summary: Overflow-safe squaring requires |x| <= 46340 (floor(sqrt(INT_MAX))). Frozen domain [-50,50] (cpu.cc:26,55) is deep inside it. Baseline computes x[i]*x[i] (baseline.hpp:12) - signed int multiplication, so any |x| > 46340 is signed-overflow UB in BOTH baseline and any straightforward candidate.
known_restrictions: Overflow-safe squaring requires |x| <= 46340 (floor(sqrt(INT_MAX))). Frozen domain [-50,50] (cpu.cc:26,55) is deep inside it. Baseline computes x[i]*x[i] (baseline.hpp:12) - signed int multiplication, so any |x| > 46340 is signed-overflow UB in BOTH baseline and any straightforward candidate.

benchmarks.domain_note: Squaring is overflow-safe only for |x| <= 46340 = floor(sqrt(INT_MAX)); the frozen sampling range [-50,50] (cpu.cc:26,55) is deep inside that bound, but correctSquareEach computes the signed product x[i]*x[i] (baseline.hpp:11-13), so any larger magnitude is signed-overflow UB inside the trusted oracle itself.
benchmarks.value_range_risk: High: define-mode value_range casts to decltype(-50)=int with saturation to int range only - NOT to the square-safe domain. Any spec range with |bound| > 46340 pushes random/ramp/alternating/all_same values into overflow-UB territory. Spec layer has no benchmark-specific bound.

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: fillRand for integral types is hi-exclusive, so random covers -50..49 (utilities.hpp:152-168) - deep inside the square-safe bound |x| <= 46340. Exact comparison via reportAndCompareEq (cpu.cc:68). This is an int benchmark, so no non-finite/BI route exists for any pattern (mismatchIsFinite is constant-true for integral value types, utilities.hpp:353-364) and baseline_gate_only_risk is false on every row; no sentinels are defined, so sentinel_collision is false rather than UNKNOWN.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: low discrimination - reference equals input, so a no-op candidate passes)

Fill-safe, domain-valid, oracle-safe, and every index is still compared - reduced discrimination, not a vacuous pass. (This pattern is already used by an existing spec for this benchmark.)

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (duplicate of all_zeros at the frozen range; only distinct if a value_range moves the midpoint off 0)

ascending.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
ascending.notes: Integral modulo ramp lo + (position % (span+1)) = -50..50 inclusive (enhanced-fill.hpp:106-119); every value is far inside the square-safe bound and both signs are covered.

descending.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
descending.notes: Same modulo ramp with reversed position; elementwise map, so discriminatively equivalent to ascending.

alternating.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: the overflow UB happens to manifest as two's-complement wraparound in BOTH oracle and candidate (the usual x86-64 -O3 outcome)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: a verdict is produced and counted (int comparisons can never emit the non-finite BI marker, utilities.hpp:353-364,425-426), but it grades the candidate against a UB-derived reference, so a pass certifies nothing about correctness

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: oracle and candidate exploit the signed-overflow UB differently (a candidate that promotes to long long or is vectorised differently, or a build with -ftrapv / UBSan)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: correctSquareEach computes the signed product x[i]*x[i] (baseline.hpp:11-13); with UB the two sides are under no obligation to agree, and a trapping build aborts the run entirely

extreme_values.notes: Option A extrema INT_MIN/INT_MAX (enhanced-fill.hpp:129-136): the FILL ASSIGNMENT IS FINE - int into vector<int>, no conversion - but correctSquareEach then computes INT_MIN*INT_MIN and INT_MAX*INT_MAX, signed integer overflow and formal UB in the ORACLE (baseline.hpp:11-13). That hazard now sits on oracle_execution_safe = false and in oracle_hazards, not on the fill axis. extreme_values is unusable as-is on this benchmark. Option B domain extrema from lo/hi (-50/50) would be safe and IS derivable from the call site, but the current pattern ignores lo/hi. No tripwire exists to catch this - the run would silently rely on whatever the optimizer does.

duplicate_at.notes: Random fill then x[k] = x[(k+1)%n] (enhanced-fill.hpp:202-205), all within [-50,49]; size >= 2 enforced (specs.py:321-323).

sorted_except_one.notes: Modulo ramp -50..50 then one adjacent swap (enhanced-fill.hpp:206-209); inside the square-safe bound.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: every spec value satisfies |v| <= 46340
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: the double->int conversion is in range and x[i]*x[i] cannot overflow, so reportAndCompareEq (cpu.cc:68) grades every index exactly

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES (bound magnitudes to the int element type) + ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED (bound them further to |v| <= 46340 so the oracle cannot overflow)
explicit_values.notes: Values are arbitrary spec-supplied doubles; for this int container enhancedFromDouble static_casts them (out-of-range = UB at the fill site) and the spec layer validates count and numeric type only. This benchmark is the one place in the family where explicit_values is hazardous on BOTH the fill axis (int range) and the oracle axis (square-safe bound 46340), which is why the two recommendations are filed in different layers. sentinel_collision is false, not UNKNOWN: no sentinels are defined. baseline_gate_only_risk is false, not conditional: int comparisons have no non-finite/BI route.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: The fill legitimately writes INT_MIN/INT_MAX into vector<int>, but the frozen oracle then evaluates the signed product x[i]*x[i]; INT_MIN*INT_MIN and INT_MAX*INT_MAX are signed integer overflow, i.e. formal UB inside the trusted reference. No tripwire or guard exists to intercept it.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED / DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED: exclude extreme_values here, or adopt Option B (derive the extrema from the call-site lo/hi, which are -50/50) so the pattern stays inside |x| <= 46340. This is NOT a fill-site type fix.

oracle_hazards.root_cause: x[k] = INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823; the oracle squares it to about 1.15e18, far beyond INT_MAX - signed overflow UB at the one index the pattern exists to probe.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED: exclude spike_at here or clamp the spike magnitude to 46340 (a spike derived from lo/hi would satisfy this automatically).

oracle_hazards.root_cause: Any spec value with |v| > 46340 (even one comfortably inside the int range, so the fill itself is defined) makes the oracle's signed square overflow; specs.py enforces no benchmark-specific bound.
oracle_hazards.e2_recommendation: ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED: bound explicit values for this benchmark to |v| <= 46340 (in addition to the generic int-range bound that belongs to the fill layer).

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern effect mechanically EFFECTIVE; the issue is value-domain policy (safe-square clamp), not a structural adapter.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vector, O(n) compute/memory, size_t loop in baseline (baseline.hpp:11); no structural blockers. Only max_spec_size=4096.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE for the eight in-range patterns (random, all_zeros, all_same, ascending, descending, alternating, duplicate_at, sorted_except_one) - all stay inside [-50,50] and are exact-comparable.
DOMAIN_POLICY_DECISION_NEEDED: extreme_values and spike_at MUST be excluded or value-clamped to |x| <= 46340 - as offered they produce signed-overflow UB inside the trusted oracle itself.

ORACLE_GUARD_NEEDED (relayered from E1's FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES, which was the wrong layer - E1's own text conceded it is 'not a call-site type bug'): the fill assignment of INT_MIN/INT_MAX/INT_MAX/2 into vector<int> is perfectly type-safe; the defect is that the frozen oracle squares those values. The harness-level fix (Option B: derive extrema and the spike from lo/hi instead of numeric_limits) would make both patterns safe here.

FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES (genuinely fill-layer, explicit_values only): bound explicit-value magnitudes to the int element type - specs.py:328-367 validates count and numeric type but never magnitude, so an out-of-int-range value is UB at the conversion in enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171.

EXCLUDE_CANDIDATE (duplicate): all_same collapses to the midpoint 0 at the frozen range and is byte-identical to all_zeros; both are weakly discriminative because 0*0 = 0 leaves the reference equal to the input.

SPEC_POLICY (size axis, family-wide): size 0 is an accepted spec size for every non-k pattern (specs.py:134,289-292 vs 321-323); the graded set is then empty and the run is counted as a PASS with nothing compared (utilities.hpp:412-465).
benchmarks.notes: All other offered patterns stay inside [-50,50] (integral modulo ramp, midpoint 0, alternating +-50, all_zeros 0) and are exact-comparable via reportAndCompareEq (cpu.cc:68). The only UB vector is huge magnitudes from extreme_values/spike_at/unbounded explicit_values/wide value_range - and it lives in the ORACLE, not at the fill site. Carried over from the dropped E1 fields: value_range risk is HIGH because define-mode value_range casts to decltype(-50) = int and saturates to the INT range only, NOT to the square-safe domain, so any spec range with |bound| > 46340 pushes random/ramp/alternating/all_same into overflow-UB territory; the spec layer has no benchmark-specific bound. Large sizes are blocked only by max_spec_size = 4096 (specs.py:138) - heap vector, O(n) compute/memory, size_t loop in baseline.hpp:11, no structural blockers; there is no large-size probe to run, only the pattern-value clamp decision.

benchmarks.size_rationale: validate() input vector<int> input(TEST_SIZE) (cpu.cc:58); both result masks are sized input.size() (cpu.cc:63,67). Everything scales with the override.
benchmarks.pattern_rationale: The single input container is ENHANCED_FILL-controlled (cpu.cc:59); the vector<bool> mask is a freshly sized output, deliberately outside pattern control. Matches shapes hint (1 site, n).
benchmarks.input_construction: validate(): vector<int> input(TEST_SIZE) at cpu.cc:58, ENHANCED_FILL(input, 1, 1025) at cpu.cc:59, BCAST at cpu.cc:60. vector<bool> correctResult/testResult (cpu.cc:63,67) are OUTPUT buffers, not inputs. Perf path: fillRand(ctx->x, 1, 1025) at cpu.cc:29.

fill_sites.fill_type_safe_rationale: DType is deduced from the int lo/hi arguments (enhanced-fill.hpp:173-174), so patterns 0-9 assign int to int with no conversion at all - INT_MIN/INT_MAX (extreme_values) and INT_MAX/2 (spike_at) are int-representable and the site is unconditionally safe for them, and because the predicate is total there is no downstream hazard to relayer either. The site is 'conditional' only for pattern 10: explicit_values converts arbitrary spec doubles with static_cast<int> (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171), UB outside the int range, magnitude-unvalidated (specs.py:328-367).
fill_sites.conversion_notes: DType=int matches value_type; no conversion UB at the site. Same explicit_values double->int cast caveat as 56/58 (out-of-int-range explicit values would be UB; not magnitude-validated in specs.py).

benchmarks.other_input_constructors: none (mask containers are outputs)

domain.summary: None: the predicate (x > 0) && !(x & (x - 1)) is total for EVERY int - x > 0 short-circuits before x - 1, so even INT_MIN is safe (documented at baseline.hpp:18-23). Frozen domain [1,1025]; values outside it (0, negatives, huge positives) are all well-defined 'false'. Prompt example itself includes 0.
known_restrictions: None: the predicate (x > 0) && !(x & (x - 1)) is total for EVERY int - x > 0 short-circuits before x - 1, so even INT_MIN is safe (documented at baseline.hpp:18-23). Frozen domain [1,1025]; values outside it (0, negatives, huge positives) are all well-defined 'false'. Prompt example itself includes 0.

benchmarks.domain_note: There is no input-domain restriction: referenceIsPowerOfTwo(x) = (x > 0) && !(x & (x - 1)) (baseline.hpp:21-23) is total for every int because x > 0 short-circuits before x - 1 is evaluated (so even INT_MIN is safe); the frozen sampling range is [1,1025] (cpu.cc:29,59).
benchmarks.value_range_risk: Low: any int value_range is domain-safe (total predicate). Discriminative note: ranges should include powers of two - the frozen [1,1025] modulo ramp covers 1,2,4,...,1024; alternating (1,1025) includes 1 = 2^0 -> true; all_same midpoint 513 and all_zeros 0 are both 'false'-only inputs (weakly discriminative but valid).

random.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
random.notes: fillRand for integral types is hi-exclusive, so random covers 1..1024 (utilities.hpp:152-168), which contains the powers of two 1,2,4,...,1024 - genuinely discriminative for the predicate. The oracle is total over every int, so domain_valid is true, not conditional. This is an int/vector<bool> benchmark: mismatchIsFinite is constant-true for both (utilities.hpp:353-364), so no non-finite/BI route exists for any pattern and baseline_gate_only_risk is false on every row; no sentinels are defined, so sentinel_collision is false rather than UNKNOWN.

all_zeros.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: low discrimination - an all-false mask, so a constant-false candidate passes)
all_zeros.notes: DType(0) into every element (enhanced-fill.hpp:184-186). 0 is domain-valid (the prompt example itself contains 0) and the predicate is total, so the run is fully defined - but referenceIsPowerOfTwo(0) is false at every index, so the reference mask is uniformly false and a candidate that always answers false passes. E1 recorded this as 'weakly discriminative but valid'; it is relayered here as REDUCED rather than left as an unqualified KEEP_CANDIDATE.

all_same.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional: low discrimination - constant 513 gives an all-false mask; a value_range whose midpoint is a power of two would make it informative)
all_same.notes: enhancedMidValue = 1 + (1025-1)/2 = 513 (enhanced-fill.hpp:144-149), which is not a power of two, so the reference mask is uniformly false - same reduced discrimination as all_zeros, and E1 likewise recorded it as weakly discriminative but valid.

ascending.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
ascending.notes: Integral modulo ramp 1 + (position % 1025) = 1..1025 inclusive (enhanced-fill.hpp:106-119), covering 1,2,4,...,1024 as well as their neighbours - the most discriminative pattern for this predicate.

descending.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
descending.notes: Same modulo ramp with reversed position; elementwise map, so discriminatively equivalent to ascending.

alternating.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
alternating.notes: 1/1025 alternating (enhanced-fill.hpp:196-198): 1 = 2^0 is true and 1025 is false, so the mask contains both outcomes in equal measure.

extreme_values.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (policy review: EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS Option A vs B stays open; no technical hazard here)
extreme_values.notes: Option A extrema INT_MIN/INT_MAX (enhanced-fill.hpp:129-136): the oracle referenceIsPowerOfTwo (baseline.hpp:21-23) returns false for both with no UB - the x > 0 test short-circuits so INT_MIN - 1 is never evaluated - and the prompt-provided candidate predicate has the identical form. The wave-fixed candidate-independent oracle makes this the family's cleanest extreme_values benchmark. Note the mask is uniformly false here too, so the case is discriminatively similar to all_zeros; it is kept INFORMATIVE because its value is precisely to prove the total-predicate boundary (INT_MIN) rather than to separate true from false. Option B extrema (1/1025) also trivially safe.

duplicate_at.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
duplicate_at.notes: Random fill then x[k] = x[(k+1)%n] (enhanced-fill.hpp:202-205), all in [1,1024]; size >= 2 enforced (specs.py:321-323).

sorted_except_one.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE
sorted_except_one.notes: Modulo ramp 1..1025 then one adjacent swap (enhanced-fill.hpp:206-209); the value set, and therefore the discriminative power, is that of ascending.

spike_at.recommendation_for_e2: KEEP_CANDIDATE (policy review: EXTREME_PATTERN_SEMANTICS open; no technical hazard here)
spike_at.notes: Spike INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823 = 2^30 - 1, not a power of two -> false; a genuinely discriminative near-boundary value (2^30 itself IS a power of two). The rest of the vector is random in [1,1024], so both mask values occur. Safe.

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: all spec values are inside the int range and the list contains at least one power of two and one non-power
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: the conversion is defined, the predicate is total (baseline.hpp:21-23) and reportAndCompareEq on vector<bool> (cpu.cc:72) is exact

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: all spec values are inside the int range but none is a power of two (or all are)
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: the reference mask is then uniformly false (or uniformly true) and a constant-answer candidate passes - the same mechanism as all_zeros/all_same

verdict_outcome_conditions.condition: any spec value lies outside the int range
verdict_outcome_conditions.evidence: static_cast<int> of an out-of-range double is UB at the FILL site (enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171); specs.py:328-367 validates the value count and numeric type but never magnitude

explicit_values.recommendation_for_e2: FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES (bound explicit-value magnitudes to the int element type in specs.py); no domain or oracle guard is needed here because the predicate is total
explicit_values.notes: Values are arbitrary spec-supplied doubles; for this int container enhancedFromDouble static_casts them (out-of-range = UB) and the spec layer does not validate magnitudes - a genuine FILL-layer issue, correctly carried on fill_type_safe. domain_valid is true, not conditional: the predicate is total for every int, so no in-int-range value can be domain-invalid. sentinel_collision is false, not UNKNOWN: no sentinels are defined. baseline_gate_only_risk is false, not conditional: int/bool comparisons have no non-finite/BI route.

benchmarks.adapter_notes: Pattern effect already EFFECTIVE on the sole input; mask is an output by design.
benchmarks.large_size_rationale: Heap vector + vector<bool>, O(n); only structural quirk is the oracle's int loop index (for (int i = 0; i < x.size(); i++), baseline.hpp:34) which would only matter beyond INT_MAX elements - irrelevant at any plausible size. Only max_spec_size=4096 blocks >4096.
e2_actions: KEEP_CANDIDATE: the total predicate plus the hardened candidate-independent oracle make every offered pattern fill-safe (patterns 0-9), domain-valid and oracle-execution-safe, including extreme_values and spike_at.

FIX_FILL_SITE_TYPES (explicit_values only): bound explicit-value magnitudes to the int element type - specs.py:328-367 validates count and numeric type but never magnitude, so an out-of-int-range value is UB at the conversion in enhanced-fill.hpp:165-171. No oracle or domain guard is needed on this benchmark.

KEEP_CANDIDATE (conditional) for all_zeros and all_same: both produce a uniformly false reference mask (0 is not a power of two; the midpoint 513 is not either), so a constant-false candidate passes - keep them only as cheap smoke tests, and prefer ascending/alternating/random for discrimination.

SPEC_POLICY (size axis, family-wide): size 0 is an accepted spec size for every non-k pattern (specs.py:134,289-292 vs 321-323); the graded set is then empty and the run is counted as a PASS with nothing compared (utilities.hpp:412-465).
benchmarks.notes: reportAndCompareEq on vector<bool> (cpu.cc:72) is exact; no tolerance or NaN issues, and because neither the input ints nor the bool mask can be non-finite there is no BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE route anywhere on this benchmark. The oracle was explicitly fixed to not call the candidate's isPowerOfTwo (baseline.hpp:12-25,33-41), removing the historical candidate-dependent-reference defect. Carried over from the dropped E1 fields: value_range risk is LOW because any int range is domain-safe, with the discriminative caveat that ranges should include powers of two; large sizes are blocked only by max_spec_size = 4096 (specs.py:138), the only structural quirk being the oracle's int loop index (for (int i = 0; i < x.size(); i++), baseline.hpp:34), which would matter only beyond INT_MAX elements.
